text: storms then >> that's also new. Yeah. Yeah. I went on vacation uh obviously when we had that little break and then coming back and seeing a I'm I'm assuming it was a monsoon in the month of July I was like okay what are we what are we doing here you know and then call my dad who's in California and he's getting 70°ree weather sunny. Um but yeah first uh first introduction to a real summer I guess >> with uh with the way the return game goes is Do you guys go into it thinking you want Durene to be that guy? Is it still wide open kind? How are you kind of approaching that return position? >> Yeah, I think with that position and honestly any position um on a roster right now, it's going to be competitive. You know, we have a lot of guys that have the ability to do that skill set. You know, obviously Dev, tons of respect for him, what he's done in the league. He's done a nice job in training camp and he's done a nice job in the offseason. So, he'll definitely get opportunities to show us why he deserves that spot, but so will other guys. Um, ultimately in this league, I think competition brings out the best um, in one another and it ultimately puts your best person out there. So, um, Dev's not going to short change the competition it takes for him to compete at his greatest level and other guys are also hungry to get ops. So, it's going to be really cool uh, just having an extra preseason game to get guys meaningful reps and really show us what they can do. >> Outside of, you know, good hands, vision, are there any qualities in particular that you look for in returners that help them stand out? >> Yeah, absolutely. I think number one is ball security is held at the highest premium. Um because we all know that the most telling statistic in football is turnover margin. So taking care of that football like it's a bag of money is critical for us to have success. Um you know the other thing I'd say is making smart decisions when the ball isn't in your hands. You know that guy has to be an active blocker on kickoff return. Um and then on punt return he has to make decisions when the ball's on the ground when the ball is near another teammate. um you know, understanding the field position if we're backed up on the uh uh in sky territory. You know, those things are are really uh critical for that guy. So, decision-m is another thing that I'm looking for. >> How you talked a little bit about kind of the adjustments that Chad made throughout the offseason. How have you kind of seen him him kicking during training camp? >> Yeah. Um you know, progressively getting better. The more ops he gets, uh especially in a team setting, that feels more like a game than you could ever get. you know, there's the ramp up to kicking in that period. You know, we we do some of these field goals a lot of uh in practice has been towards the end. So, the mentality to not get too high or too go too low is important as well. So, his buildup throughout practice, he's getting used to what it'd be like in a game, you know, and then getting the opportunity to kick in front of the team with bodies around him with a rush uh against them. Those are things that are are really good for him. So, it's just again comfort uh being comfortable and then also getting used to the specialist play with his holder and his snapper. Um, but he's done a nice job. >> Is there any way to recreate kind of the nerves and intensity of actually kicking in a in a game when it matters? >> You know, I I believe there is because if you prepare the right way, whether it be a game or whether it be in practice, um it takes a certain level of focus and discipline to do your job. um in this league you can't ease into that and you can't short change that process and if you do the product shows. So um all these guys are very prideful going into a practice of putting the best tape they can out there and ultimately there's a lot of learning moments that come with that. um if you kind of ease into it in this uh league, whether it be the the mental approach, um you know, getting your adrenaline the right level, then ultimately that's going to affect the product that's out there and you truly won't find growth in that because you're not at your highest level there. So, um I believe there is if you practice the right way. >> Deon, what stands out about his >> I'm sorry. Can you say that one more time? >> What what stands out about his stand >> Devin? Oh, he uh you know, he's a guy that when he gets moving, he can run with the best of them, you know, and um part of that deals with catch mechanics. You could have the fastest guy out there and if you don't have clean catch mechanics, you're not going to see that guy hit his top speed. So, um I think one thing that really stands out for his speed is his catch mechanics because he gets to his top speed quickly. Um he's a very efficient mover in that sense. So, um that is the the number one thing that allows him to showcase that speed. Go ahead. >> How do you with when you have one kicker and one punter on the roster? Um, and maybe it's a little different for a kicker because there's only so many chances, but how do you balance getting them the work they need in practice, but knowing that they're going to have to do everything in the game and not having them overwork? Like, how do you kind of go with that? >> Yeah, I I think number one, you have to monitor how many reps they get in a practice. Uh, number two, it's understanding that this is a game week for them. So kicking every day isn't synonymous for them having success. So um you know being able to space out their kick days I think is important and my job as a coach is articulating that to them is hey these are our kick days this week. This is so you can feel the best on game day because game come game day um there are no backups, right? They got to perform at the their greatest level the whole game. So, um, you know, it's it's really just monitoring the amount of reps in their kicking sessions and then almost training it like it's the regular season for them because they won't have another guy backing them up. >> What stands out with a guy like >> in in preseason games when starters aren't typically playing. So then maybe the backups are playing a lot of those roles. Backups who would usually be on special teams in the regular season might not be getting special teams reps in the preseason with that shift. So, what are the challenges from an evaluation standpoint that it's likely a lot of the players that will be on special teams unit in the regular season might not get a lot of those game reps in preseason? >> Yeah, I think the and this is something I hit with the the team this morning is one of the biggest challenges is your role in some of these preseason games is to play special teams and offense and defense. And in that reveals some fatigue. I told all the guys that it is undeniable in a football game, there's going to be a point where you will be tired. And to me, that's a true test of how bad do you really want it. So, when you talk about a backup, a backup could really earn a starting spot real quick. Um, it takes mental toughness. It takes good conditioning and it takes a connection to your technique. So, um, it's going to be a great opportunity for guys to get a lot of tape out there. Um, and I'm excited to see these guys perform. >> What's caught your eye with a guy like Amir so far in the return game? Yeah, you know, he's a guy that I've worked with in the past. Um, and he's very intentional and deliberate with all the drills that he does. So, um, it's been it's been cool to see uh, you know, his recall of kind of how he did stuff uh, with the Giants and then coming here and understanding. I was like, "Oh, I've done this before. I could do this a little bit different. I could take this to another level." So, he's continued to stack positive days and I'm excited to see what he can do again. >> And what about a guy with like Maxel? How what have you been seeing from him so far? >> The fastest kid alive. [laughter] Um he he's a guy, you know, obviously uh a defensive-minded guy, right? That's aggressive, can run. Um and in the return game, you see that mentality show up, too. You know, one of the things that I preach to any defensive starter that has the ball in his hands is ball security. So, that's something that defensive players don't necessarily work because they're working on taking the ball away predominantly. So, when they get the opportunity to have the ball in their hands, it's my job as a coach to put them in those situations to where they got to work on the other side of it. they're now an offensive player. Um, but it's really cool for guys that have that skill set obviously because um, you know, any additional returners you have on your roster in a limited uh, number come the season is valuable. >> Throughout your career, have you seen this much 11 on 11 in practice training camp >> from a specialist perspective >> just overall? >> Yeah, I I I think that is uh ultimately a great way to learn how to play off one another. Um, you know, I I truly believe in drills being the number one way you develop skill. Um, once that skill is developed, you have to stay connected to that. So, drills will always be a a huge component of what we do. But there is an element to understanding, okay, this is my piece in the puzzle. This is why I got to do it this way. Oh, this is how I play off this person when he does this. This is how I got to communicate to him. So, there's so many valuable lessons in both. And I don't think you can overload on one and forget the other. Ultimately, we got to put them in situations that it feels like a game in individual drills and then once they do the unit stuff, that's got to also feel like game reps. Um, so they're both very valuable and it's something that I've always kind of done. >> Have you seen Is it more than you've seen a coach do in camp? >> No. No. I I I think it's uh um the the cool thing about the way we've been doing things offensively, defensively, and the kicking game is it's been ultra competitive and and guys are out there competing so hard that um you know, it the intensity may feel different. You know, we got a lot of good veteran leadership and we got a lot of rookies that love football. So, it may feel like it's a higher volume, but those snaps just may have a little bit more meaning, like it feels different. And uh that's where I could see it being looked at as a more volume, but I I don't believe that's the case.

title: Nathaniel Hackett Press Conference 8.4.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: seen him have quite a big role in training camp. >> Love me some KB. >> What what is his impact on what you guys do offensively? >> I mean, first just just when he walks out onto that field, I mean, I hope you all feel it, but his juice is electric. Um I mean, this is a guy that talk about a guy that loves football. I mean, just being out there, it doesn't matter. He could be running a clear and he's celebrating. Um I mean, he's going in there, he's physical. You know, he's he's such a great standard for the guys to see. I mean, he's going to go in and make all the blocks. He's going to run. He might not be the priority, but he's going to run it as fast as he possibly can. And then when he gets his opportunities, he understands the game well and where to fit and and fit in those little zones and catch it and his finish and everything. I mean, he's a true pro and you can feel that standard that he sets. >> Not to say that a late draft pick can't perform quickly as a rookie, but Jaden Williams seems to be having a good camp and getting reps with twos. what's allowed him to maybe seamlessly transition into this phase? >> No, that's that's a great point. I mean, he's really doing great in this camp and that's exciting anytime you have anybody for us once they're drafted, once they're signed, they're here. It doesn't matter where they come from. So, it's more about them and what they're going to be able to accomplish starting point from a mental world. And for him, you know, mentally, he's really picked it up. So, it's kind of like what we talked about with Marvin. you know, you see a guy that's out there and he's not doesn't have to think as much. He can go through his technique and he can play and he can show his god-given talents. And I think that's what we're starting to see. >> Do you see that right tackle spot as an open competition still or or do you kind of see that as Elijah Wilkins spot for now? >> Heck, I like to think that everything's competition. Doesn't matter what position it is all the time. Um, right now we just want to keep keep pressing forward. >> What about a guy like Reggie? He see he's coming off one of his best days at camp. Where where have you seen his biggest growth? And I know you just talked about market and everything like I mean, it really it's it's kind of the same answer, you know. I mean, we're gonna know more when we get to the game because that's when, you know, those details really come in to where I'm supposed to align, what kind of route I'm supposed to run, but as you see throughout practices, it gets what we're always hoping is that we're always getting better and better and better and peing, you know, all the way through the season. Um, because they understand what they're doing. And I think in the beginning, any rookie that you have, they just have to rethink everything and they have to process everything. It's not a system they've been in for a long time. And I think that we're seeing that with a lot of these guys. >> Speaking about Preston wanting to um want to see him kind of operate just through managing the game on Thursday. But are you also seeing like how he responds to adversity or a mistake? Maybe he doesn't get pressure, anything like that is also something that you're going to >> without a doubt. I mean, you can call perfect play versus a perfect coverage and something can go wrong. I mean, who know? There's a lot of people out there, a lot of human error that goes on in every single football play. And if it's good, again, we don't want him to get too excited. Uh, it's still a long game and he'll have a lot of opportunity out there. And then obviously like you said when something bad happens you know if if [snorts] I don't even want to say the things that can but um but you know anything that that might bad happen on an offensive football play how do you respond the next play you know if you lose yardage you know are you excited about the opportunity next are you next play or are you thinking about that last one and letting it affect that next play I mean that's a huge mental part of our game especially at that position >> what you were talking about a minute ago about kind of the the rookies getting comfortable how is Jeremiah progressing throughout training camp kind of what areas do you feel like he's better now than two and a half weeks ago? >> I mean, you know, like we mentioned uh with any rookie being able to learn it, understand it, and go out there and execute. I think you're definitely seeing that in him. I mean, I think we all see his explosion, his ability to uh move his feet. Um there's still things that he's learning every day and there's great coaching points to give to him, but I mean, you definitely feel him getting more comfortable. I mean, in his blitz pickup, in his route running, just even in his tracks in running, you know, we sometimes get so detailed. We want to be able to give him the best advantage, but it's about him feeling that and understanding why. And I think every day we have the chance to coach him and help him understand the wise of what we want to do. And I think the other day, I mean, he had he had some some really cool runs that not a lot of people can do. >> What's been most impressive about him as a pass catcher? I think one just the intelligence aspect of being able to see the front, see the different contours that we get because it is insane across this league and especially out on the practice field for us from the different fronts, the different responsibilities we put on the back. I mean, it's it's a lot. And for him to understand that, see that, go through his checklist each time in that split second and then be able to be now be physical up to the line and block some pretty good linebackers that we have. Um, has been great to see. I mean, his confidence going in there to block him is great, but his ability to actually know which one to block has been great, too. >> Is he playing on Thursday? >> Uh, we're still working through everything. >> Nice quick one there. Try to see. I like that. Well done. How about love as a pass catcher and be either lining up as a receiver, breaking out of the the back field, being able to catch the ball game. What impressed you about his ability to >> I mean hands first and foremost. I mean to be able to release out of the back field. I think a lot of the time when you look at it as a back, they have to get to the line of scrimmage and they turn their heads around and the ball is right there. So just having that ability to track the ball is different than a wide receiver that's running maybe back to the ball across the field and it gets to see the ball travel a long distance. Um so his ability to turn his head around and track the ball is is really impressive. And then just understanding the different routes that we're giving him at this time. You know as a coach you're always excited and you want to do so many different things but it's about those baby steps and uh getting there when we can.

title: Nick Rallis Press Conference 8.4.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Is that hat in year four? >> It I think it is. I just I just told Marcus, one of our equipment guys, that like I actually have another one. I was like, "Hey, where's that hat at?" We have a lot of people in this building that are experts in that stuff. Um so, not really necessarily my field in terms of where I think a guy is optimal, right? So, I know this like he's he's powerful and explosive right now. >> He already looked so explosive last year when he was on the field. Can you see that he look he said he feels more explosive. Can you see that he looks more explosive? >> I mean, that's that's a hard one to really be [clears throat] able to differentiate explosive versus even more explosive, but um he looks really good right now and so I'm glad he's feeling that as well. >> What is an emphasis on quick pressure from the front seven? What have you seen from that group during camp so far? Yeah, I mean we have our our good plays, our bad plays. We have our good days and our bad days. I mean, that's the back and forth with the the O line and the D line. Um, you know, I'm I'm I want those guys to be great and I want them to hit their hit their ability, their max potential. So, like there's things everyone needs to improve on cuz like I you know, I was talking to I think Zaven the other day like, dude, I I want you to win every single rush and so like like yeah, you won these rushes and here's how you can win these ones and so this is what I want to see from you today. So, man, like we just everyone needs to continue to get better. Um, and the more you can win your one-on- ones up front, like that we know that that's today's football, that creates a lot of problems for offenses. >> I know it's a hard kind of um side of the game to judge during training camp, but what are you seeing from the spine of your run defense, the defensive tackles and the linebackers, you know, spec specifically the first? >> Yeah. Um, you [clears throat] know, I think when the pads came on, you're able to see really kind of where we're at. Um, you know, I like the knock knockback that we're getting. I think we're playing very fast. Um, and that's not necessarily always just fast downhill, but I feel like the backers are processing fast and understanding the different run fits that we have. Not everything fits the same. Um, they're doing a really good job of, I would say, like they've taken a jump and really understood it. So like you know Cody in year two um you know Mac in year three um and then you know like you know Giby's new like it's just like we have a really good understanding of how to fit and how we fit into the front with the OB setting edges. I think we've done a good job of of really collapsing those edges um and and the guys up front getting knocked back. So there's again there's always things to clean up whether that's hand placement and here's how you could have won this down cuz the offense they're making their plays too you know like some of those runs will will find that crease and there's things to clean up but overall like I think those guys are very intentional about what they need to do as it relates to all 11 to get my job done in the run game. >> How do you seen that CB2 battle shaping up? >> Yeah, I mean the entire corner room is in in competition right now. Um, and you know, there's there's guys that have had good weeks, you know, and there's guys like that continue to improve their game. So, I mean, we're we're early in camp still and and they're in, you know, they're neck and neck with each other right now. >> What are the guys who value for the nickel corner spot need to do to stand >> Yeah. I mean, I think like when those stressful downs happen and the ball is coming to you, you have to, you know, you're not going to win every single one-on-one, but you have to win those hard downs. You know, that goes into denying the football. So, you know that and like with everybody on our defense, like what's your play style? How how much do you take the ball away? Um, and do you execute even if it isn't a stressful down, are you executing things the right way? >> Kind of joked with us that he had come to you offering maybe Cody take his role and he blitzes off the edge a little more. Was that a short or long conversation when he said you told him no? >> Um, it must have been real short. I can't even recall that conversation to be honest. I must not have put too much thought in it. seen an uptick in turnover last couple days in camp. What is that a product of in your >> um you know like [sighs] it's execution? I mean there's a lot that goes into that thing. um you know, execution, you know, play style. Like sometimes like there was a play the other day where um key trail he just he just played violently and it knocked the blocker into the bulk car and ball ball came out. Um you know, so like play style, execution that can lead to takeaways, but then there's been some very intentional shots on the football. Um and I know Mike loves that from an offense perspective cuz that's getting our guys better. like even when we don't get that ball out, you know, that intention where it's on our mind and we're working on, okay, once this play declares here's where it is, here's my track on the ball carrier, as I approach that ball carrier, am I taking that shot, if it's open, um, is my technique on that shot on the ball correct? So, even if that ball doesn't come out, like we just got better, the ball carrier just got better. Um, so I think guys are very intentional with that. Um, you know, there's been some there's been some violent attempts on the ball. A couple have come out. So, um I'm always going to be a stickler on that. You know, it's what you really got to point out as a coach is when you pass up those opportunities cuz it's like shots on goal. Um I don't want to, you know, butcher like Wayne Gretzky's quote, but just go look it up. There's, you know, I think it's he misses 100% of the shots he doesn't take. So, when those shots show, when those opportunities present themselves, like, dude, take a shot right there. Like, this is an opportunity where the ball's compromised. like don't pass that up because you never you're not going to I remember showing them in the offseason a game that we had last year with like 10 good shots. None of them came out and like that's what it is. Like we're going against the best. Like these guys know how to protect the football and so you have you can't get discouraged by all those shots on the football not coming out. Like it takes a lot of shots to eventually get those balls out. So, you know, just keep harping on shots on those ball carriers. >> Was that a focus for you this off season? Um, man, that's been every year. Um, I think that's pretty clear uh across the league that takeaways and turnovers are a stat that has high correlations with wins and losses. >> If if it's been the focus every year, I guess what gives you kind of the confidence that this year could could be a step forward in that regard. >> You never know. I mean, I just focus on one day at a time in terms of like did we take those opportunities and did we do it with good technique? Having missed all of last season, what tells you from what you're seeing physically from Star that mentally he was still getting any sort of reps or taking in knowledge that he could. >> Um [clears throat] he's he's been a very intelligent player since he's been here, you know, which is probably before, you know, I got to work with Star. Um yeah, I mean like the game comes easy to him and he studies and he has a really good understanding of coverage is and you know he knows where the the stress of it but where the strength of it is and when I have that down where I have you know help or I have the strength of it and the offense presents this like I'm going to go like take my shot on things. So um he's he's always had a really good understanding of that. So the game comes pretty natural to him. You've been known to be a pretty creative defensive coordinator, especially whenever it comes to like dialing up pressure, you know, those packages, stuff like that. >> Um I'm curious, not in like practice or preseason, but just like actual games, like what goes into the decision of um deciding, okay, like let's send the house and style it up or let's kind of hold it back. Like what's the thought process? >> Um you know, I mean like going into the game like you're trying to, you know, hit those at as high a percentage as you can. And like I don't I don't believe in like you know just blind blitzes or just drawing up random patterns on the board. Like you have to have an understanding of how your entire pressure package is in marriage, you know. And what I mean by that is like it's got to marry the matchups you want to create up front. It has to marry the protections that you're getting from the offense and it has to marry the coverages you want to put behind it. So, you know, when it comes to game time, like if I feel good about [clears throat] attacking the protection, um, and it's a situation where I feel like we're getting that protection, I like the coverage behind it for what routes I think I'm going to get, um, then I'll take that shot, you know, and then, you know, even if that's on the table, like there's times where I feel good about, hey, maybe I want to rush forward and play coverage here. So, this it's a little bit of a I can't tell you like like that goes into week to week. Well, I'm just saying like it just happens, you know, like there's a little bit of intuition on when to take that shot within a game. Um, I will map things out kind of heading into it, but as that game flows, you got to be ready to adjust and usually kind of give myself a little bit of a checklist on where I want to go with things. So, um, it's calculated, you know, um, sometimes it's okay to be even less calculated because at the end of the day, like pressures, they speed up the quarterback. So, even if you're not perfect, like there's there's benefits to it. When uh when Jacobe was gone, there was obviously when he came back, a lot of conversation about catching up with the playbook and all of that stuff. Um the fact that Josh was here last year, when he finally gets back on the field, is there going to be any kind of catchup that he's going to need to do? >> No. No. Um especially like he's he's locked in right now with everything that you know, meetings and postpractice tape and all that stuff. So, not really. You've been calling defense for a few years at this point, but first game of the season, still preseason. I mean, do you get butterflies or anxious or anything, >> man? Um, yeah. Um, it's about performance still, you know, like I got to do my job at a high level to best serve the people on the field. Um, so, but you know, I like to like you'll feel that energy. Um, but I wouldn't necessarily say that that's a negative thing. That's where I want my activation level at on game day. And to be honest, I even felt it yesterday because Mike had us on the sideline, you know, working, you know, substitutions, like realistically what it is from a game. And I, so I try to stand where I would stand. And just standing there made me gave me that feeling. Um, and then, you know, just the two-minute drive. It's a situation um that Mike put together where it's a field goal, wins it, and you know, you're calling it and, you know, I'm like replaying in my mind like how does how does Mike like to call these two minutes? And so like that right there kind of generated the little bit of a feel for me and it was it was good to feel that. But yeah, it's it's a real thing like you got to perform. >> You said sweat was locked in every season meetings and such. He can't practice right now but like what's his role been like just in terms of being around his teammates? >> It's the same Yeah, he's the same sweaty like um funny guy, you know, when you're not talking ball but locked in leader all that. Yeah.

title: Darnell Wright on contract extension | Press Conference

Um, it [snorts] doesn't get me into heaven, so, you know. >> Were you acknowledged before practice today? Were there Was there an acknowledgement of the contract signing today with the team? >> Say again? >> Were you acknowledged before practice or or after practice? >> Oh, yeah, after practice. Ben said something. He said I owed uh, Dayne a loan or something. Dayne Rochard, which I probably do. That guy's helped me a tremendous amount, so. >> Uh, yeah, big shout out to him as well, so. >> I was going to talk to you the other day about his relationship with Dayne. How has Dayne brought the best out of you? >> Um, well, I think first like, he's he's consistent [snorts] every day in what he does and in what he says. He's consistent in what he's telling you. Um, he's honest and he's not a, you know, some some coaches I've had in the past or some coaches, um, in the league, you know, they're not very good teachers. >> Um, you know, they see a guy with talent and blah, blah, blah, but they can't really convey um, >> what it is and teach you. You know, you still need to be taught. So, I think he's such a good teacher >> and he does it with such good He's not yelling at you. He's not screaming at you. He's not demeaning you. You know, he's telling you what's good and what's what's good about the rep. He's telling you what's bad about the rep so you can see both sides. You know, instead of you know, maybe he if you have a coach that tells you just you know, what you did what wrong with the rep. So, maybe the next rep you just change everything and then now you have a different result. You have no consistency to stack on top of each other. Whereas, I think Dan he shows you what you did good with the rep so that you can you know keep doing the good things and then fix the bad things he tells you. So, I think that's the biggest thing. >> This time last year he was telling us just that he felt that he wanted you to develop a more consistent high motor. He wanted to see it throughout the game. How did that either motivate you? Did conversations that [snorts] you might have had with him about that? How did you get better in that area in a year's time? >> Well, you have to understand Dan he uh he there's he's never going to come to you and say uh this guy is just perfect. You know, he's there's always something he's has something which I appreciate. There's always there always is something to work on. But uh I have to take it with a grain of salt sometimes, you know, he uh uh he's hard to please so. >> So, he told you recently back [clears throat] in college like one day you're going to be the highest paid right tackle in the NFL. Would would you have believed it? >> I would have said, "Well, I don't know. I I play left tackle right now so." >> [laughter] >> Not much on the right. I don't know. >> When you say the teaching part of Dan is rare like how rare? How many coaches have you had that take that approach and it connects with you? >> Well, it's just um I mean my my uh college coach he was very good. Coach Ellerbe he um you know, he taught me very good and he he kind of had that approach as well. I think that's why I learned a lot in college. Um and then Dan he comes and he kind of has that same approach. He's teaching more. It's not uh >> I just don't vibe I just don't well with a coach that's just you know you can yell till your lungs you know go out but uh there has to be some substance in what you're saying you know so as long as there's substance you can yell as much as you want you know what I mean just you know have something you know just teach about. >> Jaquan you [snorts] you were the first first round pick for Ryan Poles in this regime you're a guy who's been obviously a key pillar part of this team rising back up but what does it mean to you to get this long term investment to be considered a cornerstone for where the Bears want to be going? >> Yeah I feel very grateful that they they trusted me like that and um they believe in me. I mean I think back to you know for like even with Ryan I think it was uh maybe a year year and a half ago I don't I don't know two years maybe he uh like Poles really invested in us like like besides the financial investment now obviously but like he really invested in me like um helping me get uh like one-on-one time more with the coaches one-on-one time more with the strength staff one-on-one time more with uh Mark in there doing like uh core strength like he's helping me set it up cuz it's hard like even when I was a young player it's like it's hard for you to go up to a coach and want [snorts] to demand their time and I know you're you're a first round pick blah blah blah blah so they would probably be obliged but you know sometimes it's hard for a player to approach a coach and you know want to take all their time when they've got stuff to do blah blah blah but he like he was invested in me at a really early age like beyond what [snorts] a you would think a GM would do. I mean I know they have all the they got to handle sorry my excuse my language they have all that stuff they are handling but like he's really invested in me like even from like a long time ago so I really appreciate that. >> So what [snorts] does it mean to you to to have that investment from Ryan what what does that mean to you? >> I mean it's just I I can see even long before like now like I was saying like even [snorts] long before this financial investment I knew he was invested in me. I mean he he drafted me first and foremost so I know he believed in me so then >> to see that he puts his foot forward first to even like invest some of the time into me, you know? Um obviously he's not coaching me, but he's he's investing more than just being a general manager into me. So, I feel like it's I want to pay that back forward, you know what I'm saying? And be a good player, not just for the team, you know, just for everybody that helped me, Ryan, >> you know, strength staff, coaches. >> With a young core mentioning Caleb Ro >> O-linemen that don't always get the same love, [snorts] but how much pride do you take in being a part of that young group of guys on the offensive >> Yeah, I mean, um you know, there's a yeah, like the young core that we have. Um I think I mean, I'm I'm part of it, but you know, I think I've been here maybe I'm [snorts] the older of the young core, I guess you could say. Um at least that's how I kind of feel myself as being. Um But yeah, I'm I'm whatever, young, old, you know, whoever it is, everybody has a place a part, so. >> Ro, you can't say that. >> Well, my What's today? >> Uh >> What is it? Monday? Well, I'm about to be 25. >> Try not [clears throat] to give it give >> When when they drafted you, they told the story about going down >> uh to Tennessee and putting you through [clears throat] a workout, right? But they didn't get to see how you got through it. Can you appreciate kind of how far you have come from >> then to today? Uh yeah, I just been like um you know, I talked with my mentor, he was here uh last he's not here anymore, but not he didn't die, but he's just he's not here with the Bears anymore, but um [snorts] you know, we talked about just like uh like a uh some guy that's just, you know, you're you're chipping away at something, chipping away, chipping away, chipping away, and you never know when it's going to break, but >> you know, doesn't matter, you just keep chipping away, and I think eventually it cracks, and >> and you start you know, that's just the approach that I have to stuff, so. >> And uh who is who is it that Who was it that told you that? >> Huh? >> Who was it that told you that? >> Andy uh his name's Andy uh he's either Rise or Reese, I'm not sure how he pronounces it, but yeah. >> He's uh he's like a mental coach, mental performance, so he helped me a lot last year. >> Going back to what has helped you be effective in the run game. Is this some something that Dan teaches or is it more about Ben Johnson's scheme? >> Um I mean, it's a little bit of both. I mean, Ben has the scheme and I think Ben even he know he gets players >> like he um I mean, he gets he premieres you in place and he like the biggest I mean, the biggest thing I've said it before, but like [snorts] um when he when I first when he first got here like he instilled the confidence into me that I was going to be like a part of the offense. Like I've never had a coach really come up to me and be like like we are depending on you. Obviously, you do your job, but like we are depending on you to [snorts] complete this play and this is pretty much your play. Obviously, you're not getting the ball, but you know, just to see a coach coming in like a coach like Ben Johnson, you know, and he has that confidence you confidence in you already. It's like uh >> it gives you a little bit of like um confidence in yourself, a little bit of courage to go out there and um you know, do good for the team. >> Last Last two, Herb and Joey. >> Going back to Ryan Poles' investment in you when the time he picked you, he kind of went against the grain a little bit and a lot of the conversation was about trading Robert Quinn. There was a need here for that as well. Getting to the second contract, being an All-Pro, does that feel like a form of validation for you and him? >> Um I mean, as if when you I guess I don't know how they you know, the draft is the draft, whatever. >> But I think if you you draft a player and he plays good and um things work out in that way, I mean, yeah, it's probably it's [snorts] good. It's good, you know, either way you slice it, so it's probably good. >> Just coaching and the investment from Poles, just what has been key for, you know, being more and more consistent every year? >> Um I think it's just knowing that you'll knowing that you'll fail [snorts] like I'll fail. I won't everything won't be perfect. Everything I might not have a good game. Might not have a good practice. Might not I a but it's um it doesn't change the fact it change the way you approach things and the way [snorts] you work towards what you're trying to accomplish, you know, failure is just a part of it. So, I had to really accept that, I guess, to move forward, you know, I was kind of okay with you know, maybe winning ugly or just maybe barely losing or just >> but to reach the next level, you have to just be okay with failing. So, I had to get good with failing.

title: Dillon Thieneman, Kyle Monangai, Dayo Odeyingbo say details are key to executing | Press Conference
text: Seven practices in, how do you feel sort of started to acclimate and adjust to uh the action? >> Uh, I say it feels good. Like everything's starting to slow down, starting to pick up things. Uh, tendencies from the offense and um just building more like connection with the the guys on defense. >> How are you looking at uh not having Kobe and it's kind of more on your shoulders? >> Yeah. No, I mean um great guy. sorry he's not out there, but um still just taking it day by day. Like I know he's going to be back at some time. He's still still in the the meetings like talking with us, telling us about stuff he knows and learns. So um we're all just going to be there for him. >> You talked about building a connection. How do you get that quickly established with Cam now? >> Uh I [clears throat] think just more reps and getting to know him. I I I'm locker buddies with Cam, so I talk to him a good amount and uh just getting out there talking about how we see things, how we how we think about things, how we operate. Um we're both pretty similar in that aspect. So I think there's a good connection there. >> What's your scouting report on his game as a safety? >> Uh has a lot of experience. I think he's going his eighth year now. So um definitely knows how to play uh in the back end, knows different tendencies, knows how to work well with other guys. So, he's been another guy I've been been asking questions, been talking to. Um, just to get his viewpoint on the game. >> Looked like Marlon Su and TJ Edwards had to do their 40 up downs and you were doing them with them. Is there a reason behind that? >> Yeah, there was a they said the rookies had to join their position group when they have as someone. So, um, when Tez did the other day, some of the like Jordan and Jay Love did theirs. So, me and uh, Skyler did ours today. So, for that. [laughter] >> Can't say >> the communication like that safeties have on the back end of the defense. DA was talking about how one person on one side of the field might be communicating something that's totally different for you. Like how do you become a good communicator at that position when there's probably so much more thrown at you in an NFL playbook? Like what steps are you taking to master that element of your game? It's first understanding the call and then the different things you can get in. Um, normally safeties are controlling what they have to their side and then they're communicating with the other safety just so you guys are on the same page. Um, and then pre- snap you can alert like fast motion, slow motions if they get into this set like what are we checking to. Um, so it's really just thinking one step ahead about who can move and how the pieces will fit together. Do you found it more difficult or just more challenging because there's more to to communicate in the NFL or is it than it was in college? How do you master that part of it? >> Uh it's just different systems. So there's there's definitely uh similar stuff and carry over from college um in my stuff that I did at Oregon, but um you go through progressions a little bit differently, so it's just getting adjusted to that. >> How comfortable are you playing in the box close to the line scrimmage? >> I feel very comfortable. Um, still obviously getting more reps can can be better at that. Always working to get better, but um, I feel good down there. I just I feel like more reps I'll just get more and more comfortable. >> And those reps, what's it like facing Coloulston? What's it like facing Luther? Getting those reps against those types of players? >> Yeah. No, I'm very grateful to go against them. They're uh they're very good players. So, um, going against them every day just just helps me to get better. Like iron sharpens iron. So, I'm I'm very glad to go against them. >> What's the physicality of NFL practice? not today but maybe the previous two days. How does that compare to what you did in college? >> Um similar aspects like we went live a little bit uh the other day and then just other um like thud or wrap up tempos uh which is pretty similar to college but um some there might be some speed differences or some size differences from from college to NFL. >> To to Adam's question, what makes Coloulston a difficult cover? >> Uh he's tall. He's he's got long arms and uh he's fast. He's got a good burst. So, just staying connected with him because he can get out of his breaks pretty pretty quick. And then um just his length like I have to cover more ground against him. >> On the one play at the goal line today, you had him. >> You're sort of in an impossible spot in that situation, aren't you? >> Which play? >> He had a touchdown catch. >> It was like an out route. He was >> Yeah. Yeah. I just I need to be in better um position there and just anticipate the route from his stem. Um just tendencies you get from the offense looking at different stems that the uh wide receivers and tight ends can give you. So I could just anticipate that more and be be able to drive it. >> Been I bet about a month since you signed your rookie contract. Is there anything that you took your first paycheck or you're planning to spend your first paychecks on big purchases? >> Not really. kind of just invested in um just doing some stuff with my dad. >> Dylan, even at this level, you're still one of the fastest players on the field. What are you looking forward to to help slow the game down for you [clears throat] physically? >> Thinking more pre- snap and what are the the formations, splits, situation, like what are they telling me? Um so, just taking in what the offense is is showing you and be able to think more pre- snap. Um because if you anticipate what they're going to do, you can react and play faster. So that's kind of what I'm working on right now. >> Does it feel like a lot right now for you being a rookie and playing with starters? >> It it can. Yeah, at times it definitely does. But um I just try to break it down. Just take it one day at a time. Like don't look too far ahead. Um right now during camp like you can't win any games at the moment. So right now I'm just working on getting better. What are the moments when it feels like a lot? >> Uh, it can at practice like sometimes that first rep you get you get a little little nervous, a little those butterflies, but um I like to say I'm excited more than nervous, but um once you get one rep down, I kind of get get comfortable. You get get in there like you're supposed to be there. >> What What are the coaching points for couple that Al's been working with you on? What's his emphasis for you? >> Um really been working on cross trainining. So, just learn some more nickel. Um, be able to play in different spots and and focusing some more on man coverage because I feel like that's where I can improve. >> How have you adjusted to NFL life, like being on your own and who's helping you with like the in ins and outs of life off the field? >> Um, just been talking to some of the older guys like uh some Cam and Kobe and um Elijah um about like I see there some of their routines just talking about uh with them like what else I could do. um talking with coach Lang and uh Brent on the staff and then um I feel like in in college I built good routines so transition NFL I feel pretty comfortable in what I'm doing. >> Bill, when uh when Caleb scrambles, how does that help prepare you for scrambling quarterbacks, the things that he can do when he gets outside the pocket? >> Yeah, he's he's very talented, very athletic, uh faster than I thought. Um, so doing scrambles against him definitely helps us prepares us for for what we're going to see in season. >> Is your note takingaking process similar to college or have you made any adjustments to like how you take notes for both for overall concepts and well obviously you haven't got the games yet but what's your plan for that? Uh, so we we we obviously we watch practice together as a unit and then um myself, I watch by myself and I know a lot of other guys too. When I watch by myself, I'm watching like specifically uh me seeing how I can improve my technique, all that stuff. And then um when we're watching together, I'm seeing more overall scheme, how how the nickels playing it, how the backers are playing it. And that way I can ask questions and be able to um understand how every all the other pieces are moving. Let's go a couple more. >> What's the biggest difference you've noticed between the college game and the NFL so far than you're in? >> Uh I feel like it's another step up in speed and then um a lot more under center like play action type stuff. >> You're talking about something first paycheck. You have any ideas? >> Uh it's just an investment I'm doing with him. How you feeling? >> Good. >> Go back to uh your normal self. >> Yeah. Yeah. Getting there, you know, getting back into the swing of things. Obviously missed a few days and getting back into team and getting getting those reps back in and just trying to keep going on the right direction. >> How different is it for you, you know, this year having a year under your belt coming in right now? >> Uh just just building like, you know, there's not the head on a swivel, not knowing what to expect. I know what to expect now. Um, and then now this with that ease of mind, I can kind of just go play, focus on what really matters, not like, you know, the the extra stuff and, you know, just focus on the day-to-day process. >> Press Taylor was saying that when talking about the run game that Ben doesn't talk about efficiency, but explosives when he's teaching and installing it for you guys, like what do you notice about his tone of how you guys are supposed to lead this offense? Um, you know, it's no secret he loves to run the ball and uh, like you said, explosive plays, but um, in that there's efficiency as well. Like there's no, you know, he's hunting them and like every play is a big hitter. We know that's not the nature of football and running the football well. Um, but like yeah, like we we want to make big plays in the run game. Like that's that's no secret. We're going to rely on the guys up front. We're going to follow their lead and when they're there, we want to hit them. We don't want to miss out on any opportunities, but uh, just keep going forward and, you know, keep moving the sticks. Does that kind of make I mean we always hear the term from players coaches we're going to take what the defense gives us but if you're in hunting mode and attacking and like Ben with explosives isn't that kind of go against that when you're trying to dictate the tone as a runner. >> Yeah I think there's a time and place for for for both you know depending on the situation and you know nobody knows better than him himself. So you know he kind of sets the tone for us and he gives us the script and we go execute. So, whatever mode we're in, you know, we just go out there and try and execute to the the best of our ability. >> You sat down this off season and made a list of the things you wanted to get better at during the break. >> Yeah. Yeah. Um, speaking with coaches and and, you know, just doing self-reflection, you know, I I think I did some good things last year, but um, it's nowhere where I want to be for sure. Just um, not even just statwise, but just as a whole. Like, you know, I watched the film for how well I did and how I executed obviously and like did I do my job? Did I, you know, get a good gain on one play? Did I not? Did I miss an assignment? Did I not? But then you kind of sit back and I also look at it, you know, holistically like what was I thinking on this play? What was I doing? Was I set right away? Was I taking too long? Was I thinking too much? Was I, you know, like that aspect of it. So, um, just building off the little things. OB, it always comes back to that. like the the major things we know, we see. If I had a drop pass, like obviously I got to catch the ball there. If I miss a read, like I got to make that read. If I fall and nobody was there to attack me, I got to pick my feet up. So those things are obvious, but like the little details, that's what I go back and watch and like coaches obviously help me as well with their feedback. But those are the things they I kind of got to focus on to, you know, show up because those little things obviously add up to big things and that's where the the big gains and the big improvements come from. >> You and me had such a good relationship. What have you been different about the process? What you learn still there? >> Yeah. Um definitely had a good relationship and then yeah, coach Stew since he's been in the building, we've had a great relationship kind of building on that since he's been here. Um taught me a lot and um you know, we we all have a good relationship in the room just building off each other, helping each other get better. You know, it's obviously u we're all competitors in that room and coach East, he loves that stuff. So he he kind of urges that um that energy in the room and on the practice field. So, um it's it's been great and like I said, I hate being missing those few days cuz like I hate not being out there with the guys. So, um being back out here just is it's great to now just get better again like to just sharpen the iron. >> You can still hear EB in the back of your head sometimes. >> Uh yeah. I mean, yeah. >> What's it like running behind Darnell? >> Um easy because he moves whatever's in front of him. Yeah, it it he makes it, you know, very easy. A lot of the guys up front do like it's not just him, but you know, I'll talk about him because you mentioned him. Like he does a great job and, you know, we all heard the news about his recent signing. Like no one's more deserving and um you know, like him as well as the other guys up front, they just do a great job of making me and Swift and the rest of the guys in the room like have a peace of mind knowing they're going to do their job. >> Is this uh running game kind of complex and difficult to master? Like knowing your marks or like when does it start clicking? What's that process to get there for you? >> Um complex. I don't know if that's the word. I mean, it's um there's a lot of details that go into it. There's a lot of details that go into the whole offense. Um like to the to the minute details are the difference between winning and losing a play. Like execution is key and details are key to execution. Um so that's that's everything in our offense. Everybody's part matters. Everybody needs to do their part for a play to be successful. And um our run game is yeah it's not bland like everyone knows that. I think you ask D coordinators they'll tell you that Ben Johnson's run game is not bland and he's going to come at you in different ways and we try to make things look similar and attack you in whatever way we see weakness and we also sometimes say like hey we're going to run the ball and do this and you have to try and stop us. So um yeah like we take a lot of time each day trying to master it so that when we go out there it's it's flawless for us. Press was talking earlier about how much he loves the Donnell Jonah combo. When you're running to the right behind two guys, like as a running back, what what's going through your mind? >> Yeah, I mean they they do a great job. Like when they have a deuce block and you know they're moving a three tech, it's it's kind of much over for that three technique, wherever that is. So like I said, just the ease of mind knowing that they're going to move the guys in front of them. seeing guys like Bon Robinson um and those who share your position, you know, get big big paydays. Does that inspire you or fuel you at all to for like personal goals going into this season and the rest of, you know, your career? >> Um, yeah. I mean, that's a little ways away until I'm speaking contracts and stuff, but um I love that for the running back position. like, you know, I think it's no secret the the running back position has kind of been looked at as less valuable in in recent years and I think that trend's kind of going in the other direction now and uh you know, a long ways away, but that things like that like Bejian and all these other guys that are getting paid like I think that's that's great for the position value and teams are starting to realize that and um yeah, congrats to him for for a big accomplishment. Uh Ben has talked about 13 a lot and you know how they he's able to disguise things in the right game, but from your perspective like what does 13 personnel uh do for you? >> Um puts three great athletes on the field like you know whoever those three tight ends are um like they our tight end room is very equipped to do anything that that our offense asks of them. And um yeah, we can run the ball at at them with three tight ends at one side or we can throw the ball at a three tight end personnel set as well. So it's like just gives us that that flexibility to do both. And um I think when we excel at doing that, it kind of, you know, it makes it hard on the defense. >> What's impressed you with 18 so far this year? [laughter] >> I mean, it's it's 18. Like it's what he does. Just every day is, you know, the consistency, the the growth. Um, we all know the talent he has in and his arm and and what he does, but the growth and other aspects of just being a quarterback and taking the the the helm of this offense and kind of everybody just following his lead, I think that's that's the the most impressive thing I've seen so far. >> How relationship with DeAndre compared to last year? Was it more mentor mentee last year and more peers now or how would you describe it? >> Um, yeah. No, I learned a lot from him last year. um like just just watching him like he's a very u number one he's been elite for a long time so he's a pro and um I'm very observant and I take to guys that do things the right way and he's somebody that as soon as I walked in the building you kind of know like okay he's he he's had the success he's had because for a reason. So, learned a lot from him just watching him do what he does on the practice field, outside the practice field and um you know, kind of took to him very quickly and and trying to learn like how to be a pro and and go about my business. So, um but like I said, even last year and continuing this year, we just pushed each other every day uh practice and in the meeting rooms and everything so that we can both be the best that we can be. >> I know today was lighter, but how would you describe the physicality the last couple of days? >> [clears throat] >> Um, well, like I said, I just was getting back out there, but um it's been physical. It's been a physical camp, but that's that's the nature of how we play, so that's how we're going to practice. Now, >> how'd you go about getting your back yourself back as quickly as you have? >> Uh, let's just say uh staying locked in, just attacking the rehab every day. Uh, just taking it one day at a time. So, >> have you surprised yourself with how how quickly you've been able to progress? >> Uh, no. I mean, I've dealt with an Achilles before, so I kind of knew how the rehab went, and this was a little bit easier process than the first time, so wasn't too much of a surprise. Just sticking to the process. >> Was it the same Achilles that you had the last time? >> No, it's my other one. >> Is that strange to to be doing it on both sides or is anything different from the the two rehabs? >> Uh, I don't think it's that uncommon. Like, I know a couple other people in the league that have done both of them. Uh, I think it's better than doing the same one twice. So, it's kind of, you know, once you repair it, you're in a good good place. >> So, you knew right away what did you learn from the first rehab specifically? Is it more of a mental thing or >> Yeah, I would say uh the mental thing and then like kind of what to do outside of rehab as far as staying in shape and staying uh like how to still get better outside of, you know, just rehab. >> What do you do? Uh just being able to still do cardio, still find ways to work out like even, you know, when I wasn't able to walk like still the cast. So, uh just finding ways to stay active. >> I think Ben said that like the game before you got hurt was your best game that season and the coaches were seeing you moving you inside, all that stuff. Did that I mean, I'm sure it was so frustrating, but did that make it extra frustrating for you that you were starting to really come >> uh Yeah. Yeah, I mean I think there was definitely a lot of progress uh like being made as far as that goes and it it was tough like the timing of it, but um you know I kind of look at everything as as a good situation. So uh I feel like that's the time that was supposed to happen. You know it was God's timing. So uh I'm just excited for this year. >> What was the uh what were the challenges mentally, emotionally both your initial reaction and then dealing uh through the recovery? Um, I would say the hardest part is, you know, just watching like the team be able to play and like this the first time, my first time uh that tore my Achilles was before I was in the NFL. So, it kind of was different, you know, coming into a team and not being able to play initially than playing later in the season versus, you know, being in the season and having to watch the team go through the rest of the season and kind of just be on the sidelines. So, that that'd be the hardest part mentally. >> Have you seen the social media discussion throughout the spring of motivated dio? >> Yeah, I've seen it. [clears throat] >> Did you create that or? >> No, I did not create it. I don't really use social media like that, but uh I've seen it. It's I seen it. [snorts] >> Did you find it offensive at all? Like there, you know, as if you weren't motivated in the past like how do you know? >> No, I don't find it offensive. You know, it's it's entertainment at the end of the day. That's what football's about. So, people keeping themselves entertained. the idea inside. I know that's nothing new for you, but what has the balance been like in a week? >> I think there's definitely been more emphasis on uh getting me inside on passing downs and that's something that's helped me throughout my career and that's I've made a been able to make a lot of plays in. So, that's something I'm excited about for this year. >> What do you need to be good at rushing the passer inside? That's different. >> Uh I think it things just happen quicker. uh you know the the fights you know within your first couple steps.
