I'm sure you've heard a lot of the chatter about not bringing in bringing in a new body. >> Um, I think it's just committing to more of an attack style of play, which is what we've been practicing. That's what we've been working on this year versus last year. stop, you know, um kind of reacting to what the offense is doing, playing more on the off on the offensive and attacking more as a defense

title: Press Taylor discusses offense’s progress through first week of training camp | Press Conference
text: Pressa want to get your thoughts of like how are you feeling having a second crack at being an OC and um what things do you feel will be different this time for you? >> Yeah, I'm really excited for the opportunity. You know, I don't know if that's something that comes along a lot in this league. Um getting a second chance to to be an offensive coordinator. Uh I'm grateful for the opportunity to work with Ben and the staff. I think the greatest thing about being here is the staff, the people around me that I'm working with, the offensive line coaches, the receiver coaches. I mean, I could go up and down our entire list of offensive coaches that I get a chance to work with. Um, and then just being here, being a part of this organization, the alignment from top to bottom from Ryan through Ben throughout the coaching staff, the support staff around here, it's been incredible. So, grateful for the opportunity. Uh, plan to make the most of it. >> What you learn from your previous experiences that you can apply now? >> Learned a lot. I've learned a lot. You know, this is my 14th year in the NFL. Every single year, you learn something. Sometimes it's the way not to do things and you take that with you. You apply it to you. The number one thing is just be yourself. You know, I'm not going to change who I am as a person and the way I go about treating people and operating. Um, but obviously learning a lot of football. You know, that's been that's been the greatest part being involved in the run game, the protection aspect of things. I've always kind of had, you know, probably lean towards the pass game, just my background as a quarterback and how I grew up in this league, coaching quarterbacks and working with receivers and stuff like that. So the biggest thing, you know, kind of seeking out an opportunity to work with Ben when it came about was what Ben was doing in the run game throughout his history at Detroit and then what we've been able to do here, being able to learn from that aspect of it, be around Dan Roshar and Kyle Dean, the way they coach the offensive line. Um, you know, Jim Dre and the tight end world and working with Declan last year, like that was a great opportunity and really being exposed to a whole new run game that I'd never really been a part of. Um, and then being able to marry the entire system together. That's the the beauty of Ben is the way everything is tied together from the top down. From the the passing game, the shifts, the motions, the presentation to everything looks, feels, smells the same. And we can hit you a number of different ways. >> With Ben, how much do you think he enjoys an efficient running attack? It seems like we see him light up when he talks about the run game in particular. >> I would tell you, I don't think I don't think Ben's ever mentioned the word efficiency. We talk about explosive. I mean, we are trying to attack a defense. I think there's a perception a lot of people, we're going to run the ball. We're going to stay efficient. We're going to control the clock. We are looking to attack a defense. We're looking to attack fronts, to expose space, u to create run lanes, to create explosives. I mean, we don't look at the run game as a way to stay on track. We look at the run game as a way to attack defenses and really be explosive and continue to just put our foot on the gas the entire game. >> With Darnell's extension yesterday, just how would you describe his importance to exactly what you're talking about right now, especially in the game? Well, I think a big part of Darnell is the growth you've seen from the time we've been here. I mean, he's obviously a very talented player. He's taken the top 10. Um, and then he's just he continues to take those steps towards being more consistent every single day. You see the the focus level really dial in and we we put the pads on. You're watching a Trey block with with him and a tight end coming across. And I think he takes the defensive end, throws him into the backside corner. I mean, what he's able to do just manhandle another person on the field is impressive. And it's just about Darnell continuing to to earn the contract he just got and continuing to put his best foot forward every single day and just keep getting better and better. >> Ben said in the spring that, you know, with Darnell in mind, you guys are more of a right-handed offense than left-handed. Like, how do you go about when you have a player that's that dominant on the right side of the offensive line, building things that naturally go that way? >> Yeah, there's there's certain blocks, certain combinations. Obviously, it's not always just him. It's him and Jonah together a lot of times in combination is a pretty devastating force. Uh, so we're very mindful of that. But then there's also aspects where technically he's on the back side of things because of his his range and his quickness. He's able to do a good job on the backside cutting off and the ball tends to spill back there. So there we're we're mindful of there may be certain times and certain points in the game where we're going to lean on our best players and we certainly feel that Darnell's one of our best players. So we're going to feature him. We're going to try to get behind him a little bit. But there's other times where the ball tends to find its way back there because of things he does well or Darnell does well. Um, and we're always trying to utilize or feature the strengths of everybody on the offensive line. So, there's things Joe does really well that we're going to feature on the left side or maybe getting Joe pulling around because of his consistency in that aspect. Um, and then it's no secret, you know, we were in and out of left tackles a little bit last year, so things tended to move and when we needed a certain situation or we needed a yard here or there, then we're probably going to find a way to get behind Darnell, Jonah, and and feature those guys a little bit. >> [clears throat] >> two practices and and full pads with Braxton getting the majority of the snaps with the ones. How did you evaluate him through those two days with pads on and what you're seeking for and what you know everybody said consistency, but yeah, >> what you see when you watch the tape. >> Yeah, that's the biggest thing with all those guys. I mean, we're going to give everybody an opportunity at that left tackle spot and and we'll see who ends up taking the bull by the horns there. I think Braxton has has done what we've expected in terms of being physical, being comm being in great communication with our left guards as well, being in communication with the tight ends. That's something that I think as an entire unit. Um, so far with two days in pads, we can improve and that that'll be a big part of our step forward, but just giving those guys opportunity and seeing who's going to who's going to step up and take that job. From an operational standpoint, just the left tackles, I know we saw this early on in camp where it'd be whoever was starting with the ones that day. First team offense goes through the reps, but there's one rep at the end of whatever of the end of the first team that the second team left tackle gets in. What's what's the rationale? >> It's really just keeping a big picture on number of reps. So throughout the course of camp, you'll see guys move in and out. Well, at the end of the day, we want to be able to evaluate this guy had 20 reps, this guy had 20 reps, this guy had 19 reps. try to keep it as close as possible so we can get a fair evaluation of everything. Sometimes it maybe there's certain plays the coaches have a script a lot of times when we're in these scripted periods of knowing okay on this particular play we need to see this guy on this screen action so we're going to give him an opportunity he hasn't gotten that yet. We're very mindful of the number of rep or the types of reps that everybody gets. So from the quarterbacks and that's something we're managing. The quarterbacks are all getting different concepts. the receivers are getting put in different position to see what they can do because you could go a couple days where this guy hadn't gotten a ball because he just hasn't been a primary on a certain thing. Well, we're going to we're going to move him to the slot because we know he's going to get this ball right here, get an opportunity at and we really want to be able to evaluate. So, I think that's just a natural part of camp and being in control of um what the type of play is and how many reps we're getting so we get a fair evaluation on everybody. >> For a casual for a casual [clears throat] observer, it may be tough to quantify what Cole commit brings to this offense. Can you articulate [snorts] how valuable he is to what you guys want to do? >> Yeah, I'm I'm glad you mentioned that because Cole is everything that we are about. I mean, the way he approaches his work in the meeting room, in the building, um just the presence he is, you know, he's a guy that as we started yesterday and we knew we were going into a live period and it was an unscripted, it was it was more of a scrimmage type feel as we broke up as an offense, he's the guy to call on to make sure he's addressing the offense just because he sets the tone for us. He's got the right mindset. He's about the right stuff. Um he can do anything we ask. You know, he can line up at fullback, he can be in line, he can motion out, he can he can play in space. Um and he's he's been a great role model for, you know, Coloulston, for Sam, for that guys, but also just our entire offense as as an entire unit. He's done a great job. >> What have you seen from that relationship between Caleb and Coloulston that has really grown since the end of last season and through the summer? >> Yeah, I think those guys just put time in together. You know, they they're they're out throwing in LA. They spend a lot of time talking together. We try to make sure we meet every single day as a pass unit, you know, following practice. That's the very first meeting we have just so everybody's hearing the exact same message in the pass game. Um, so we may be talking to receivers, but it's a certain situation where in our offense you anybody could do anything. So we may be talking about a receiver outside the numbers, how he runs a certain route. There's going to be a point in time where our tight ends are doing it or our running backs are doing. We want to make sure they're hearing the message and the way we're coaching these guys on the certain details. So I think Coulson takes that, you know, it's very natural for him. He's he's a grinder. He wants to put his time in. He wants to know everything. That was something that last year he wasn't able to do it in the offseason and then half of training camp, but he was asking more questions than anybody of just what does this look like? How would I adjust this? What would you do? And I think now as those two grow in the system and they're communicating with one another. It's just it's continuing to grow with those two, which is really cool to see. >> Where is Kyle guy at with a year under his belt year? >> Yeah, Kyle Kyle's another guy. I mean that that kind of rookie class last year, those guys just put their head down and went to work. And so that that was Kyle from the jump. You know, you didn't hear a lot about Kyle. Um or you didn't hear a lot from Kyle. He didn't he didn't he doesn't speak a whole lot. Um but he just he's a guy that's about the right stuff as well. We talked about Cole earlier. Kyle's kind of that same way where Kyle's just going to work. He's going to do it exactly the way you want. He wants to know exactly how you want it done and then he can do it. And you saw even yesterday when he gets in some of those periods, he's when he puts his foot in the ground, he gets north, he's making decisions. He's a very decisive runner right there where he understands the intent of the play and what we're trying to get done. He's going to make a decision and he's just somebody that's going to get going forward for us and keep us moving. >> What are you see seeing in the offense [clears throat] last couple of days? I mean, one of you would like to where you seeing spots where you think you guys can step up. >> Yeah, I think, you know, putting the pads on. It obviously changes the intensity of practice and the physicality. We're we're pleased with the physicality we've had. We think we could still go another step with that. I think we've taken a step back honestly in our in our pre-nap communication, you know, from the huddle, breaking the huddle at the line of scrimmage. You know, yesterday was definitely not our best day as an offensive unit. And we feel like, you know, going back watching it, meeting as a unit, we feel like we lost the snap before the ball was ever put in play a lot of times, just not being on the same page, not seeing something the same way, not communicating as the picture was changing. And that's the beauty of playing against DA every single day is you're going to get something that you haven't necessarily repped against before. And we're going to continue. We're going to get it in practice. We're going to go back. We're going to watch the tape. We're going to get it in the walkthrough in the evening. We know we're going to see it again and we want to get it addressed. And in terms of these young players and just growing in their communication, their understanding of the system, it's huge. It's invaluable, but it can expose you if you're not ready and you're not doing a great job communicating or passing it down throughout the line. So, I think that's something we're looking to really improve. >> What have you come to appreciate about DA and kind of the way he takes the lead of that defense? Well, I think you saw it just in the last two days with the way, you know, the pads come on and the physicality has definitely increased out of that unit. You saw a lot of guys um trying to impose their will a little bit yesterday and and being physical and being excitable in that. Uh and then just the variety, you know, the multiple fronts we see every single day, every single play. You got to have a lot of rules and responsibilities and you got to have great communication or you're going to get exposed. And that I think that happened a few times yesterday. uh maybe an unblocked player at the point of attack or even on the backside just because our communication is not great of the difference of a a three technique and a two eye and a six technique and a nine changes everything and DA will throw every single thing at you. They have all the adjustments based on the way you align and what their call is each time. So, you know that that's it's a challenge to play against every single day. going back to what you said earlier about explosive ver explosives versus efficiency. How does your quarterback fit that mentality that you guys are trying to execute? >> I mean, obviously he can he can attack every inch of the field and that's a big part of it. He can buy time. He's very creative. Um he has a great sense of space in the pocket extending downs. But, you know, you're not limited to all right, this guy could potentially we'll we'll get creative with the concept. And you know, I think there's been a time I've been some places where it's like, well, this guy could eventually outrun the quarterback's ability to get there. I don't think that's we haven't found that to be the case yet with Caleb. Um, maybe we'll find something along the way or somebody that can get there. We obviously have tons of team speed, but I think just being able to access every inch of the field at any given time is is a threat. And, you know, he could be potentially late or somebody could be wide near the sideline, he could still get the ball in there, which is impressive. And um it gives you the opportunity just again like I said to attack the whole 53. >> What does unlock >> operations um you know observing his operations observing him in the meeting room. What areas have you seen gains and then maybe what areas has he slipped and need some additional coaching? >> I think it's it's just like anybody. I mean it's a like our entire unit. It's just consistency daytoday. you know, as as practice dragged along yesterday and you're going from live periods to, you know, a 13 personnel emphasis period where things are physical and we're running the ball. Um, to then all of a sudden we're in a two-minute end of game and and the the dynamic, the situation change. Our communication has to continue to elevate in these situations. And I think you've seen he has the ability to elevate his play. We need just the consistency down in down out, the communication in the huddle, out of the huddle, at the line. Um, that's something that will always be a continue ongoing process for Caleb. What does Xavon unlock in this offense that maybe you guys didn't have last season? >> Uh, I, you know, I think just overall team speed. He adds to that element. That that's the first thing you see when you see him. Uh, he's got great hands, which has been, you know, fun to watch him grow. He's, he's still, he's like a lot of these young guys, like he can't get enough reps. He can't get enough time on task in the system. And we'll keep feeding him every single day. We'll keep adjusting. He's done a great job bouncing back every single day because he's like any rookie. Every day is not perfect. We're growing every single day. and we're excited to see, you know, the steps with him every day and where he is by the time camp ends. >> Last one. >> In any of your previous stops, because I know you guys don't use them here, did did the quarterbacks use GoPros on their helmet? >> Um, I think I think at one point in Philly we did, I can vividly picture Chase Daniel, I think, wearing a GoPro at one point in time. Uh, but I think that was maybe just one year that we've done that. >> What was the benefit for coaches either having that film back for quarterbacks to see from the POV? I think you're really trying to get exactly what they see. You know, we have pole cams that stand about seven yards behind the quarterbacks and it's about 8, nine feet tall. That gives us we feel like gives us that view pretty well. You know, we've got quarterbacks miked at any given time so we can hear what's being said. So, it's probably very similar. Um, it's probably just a different feel and the weight of their helmet, I

title: Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. reflects on progress made at AT&T Training Camp | Press Conference
text: kind of on track. Do you think you could be cleared a little? >> Yeah, man. It it it could it could be any day. You know, for me, I'm not really chasing a timeline. You know, I'm just, you know, chasing trying to be better every day. So, each and every day I get out there, you know, I look forward to to being better than better than I was the day before. And that, you know, that comes with obviously just the reps, you know, time on task and also just what I'm doing in in the rehab and the treatment room as well, so that, you know, I can get to where I want to be. Is it hard to not chase a timeline though when you're trying to win the job here? >> Yeah, man. Like I said, I think I mentioned it before. Like for me, like I I can't worry about a starting job till I'm worried about getting back on the field. You know, if I can't be on the field, how am I going to be the starter? So, um that that's all that's all my focus is on right now is just, you know, trying to get back get back healthy so that, you know, whenever, you know, that time does come, you know, then, you know, we we talk about the whole starter thing. But that's that's not my focus right now. Michael, we said uh last week, you know, it's kind of a week toe thing for you. You know, we spoke to you, I think [music] six or seven days ago. Where, you know, have you improved and developed in terms of the physicality and everything from then and now? >> Yeah, I mean, I just getting stronger, getting stronger, getting more confident in and in in my knee and everything like that. You know, my body has been feeling really good, you know, just hitting all my weight goals, making sure I'm I'm taking my diet um you know, seriously, so that you know, I'm I'm doing everything I can to help my knee get better faster. So, uh, I feel like I'm definitely better than where I was last week. >> Do you feel like you're making progress just in terms of, uh, you know, developing those relationships with the receivers despite the fact that you're not playing a team? You know, you're still taking a lot of those reps with those guys. >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, that, you know, you got um you got meetings and stuff like that. We also can get those relationships whenever we're just hanging around the building, you know, waiting for meetings. So, um, the relationship uh aspect of it, that's that's that's easy, you know, that comes naturally. That just comes with, you know, just um wanting to wanting to do it, you know, like you I feel like in our in my position and the quarterback position in general, you know, you you got to get to know all your all your teammates and you know, so that whenever you you go out there and lead them on the football field, you you know how to lead them, you know, what guys uh you you know, you can get get on to, you know, what guys that you might need to pull to the side, you know. So relationship is that's everything about about this game, you know, cuz whenever you have a good relationship with the person that's next to you, you know, you going to want to go to war with them. So >> do you have a a date with your doctor scheduled on the calendar yet where you're going to go back with him and say, "Look at it." >> No, I don't I don't I don't have a date scheduled yet. >> But you But you'll see him before you get like he would be the person he'd be the final check mark, right? >> Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely. Michael, it looks like you've taken a just a touch off your fast ball out there today. Has that been a conscious effort to just throw with a little more uh touch and air into the ball or is that just something that has happened naturally? >> I don't know. I don't know. I I just throw it throw it to my receivers. Um a lot of it come with what the defense is giving you, you know. So, if you got somebody trying to undercut, you might need to put more touch on it. If you got to layer a ball to the second level, you got to put touch on it. So, um it all comes with it. you know, sometimes, you know, I feel like I do got to, you know, throw it hard to get get it in between windows and stuff like that, you know. So, it it just maybe today I just had more second level uh throws. Obviously, we were in third third and longs a lot today in the period that I was in. So, um third and longs and we were in a couple second and longs. So, you know, we were going down the field a little bit more. So, yeah, it's going to be a couple more layered throws and that. So, >> have you spoken to Jaylen? >> Yeah. No, I haven't. I haven't seen him yet uh since yesterday like right on the field, you know, but obviously everybody, you know, um hug hugged him up, loved him up on the field, you know, before u they drove him off. But um definitely prayers to him and I know that he he's a strong individual, so I know that he's going to be able to get through it and um obviously I'm going to let him know if he ever needs anything. Obviously, I I've been through it too much. So, um I'll be there for him and he he know that. So, >> layering passes, Michael, how how much of that is just natural? How much of that can you rep and improve? >> Um, a lot of it is natural. A lot of it is reps. A lot of it is not wanting to throw a pick. So, I mean, if you don't if you don't lay a ball over a backer, I mean, it's it's not going to be good ball. So, I guess it it's all of it. All of those things. >> What is what you've seen from Zachary Branch so far? >> Um, explosiveness. Um, he he's very explosive, you know, um, down the field, short game, catching the ball, transitioning, you know, into a runner. man. He with the ball in his hands, he he's definitely special and uh that's that's somebody who who we want to get the ball in their hands a lot this year. So, he's definitely been looking good. >> Sorry, I came in a little bit late. I'm sure someone asked you, but I know you're probably itching to get back out there completely 100%. What is it like for you on the sideline when you can't go to the full rate that you want to? >> Uh it's it's okay. You know, I'm running my own race, you know, so I'm just, you know, focus on what I can do to to get back out there, you know. So, I just got to take it one day at a time, you know, and just, you know, focus on what I can control. And, you know, right now I can't control not being out there right now, obviously with with my body and, you know, um, what I'm going through, but, uh, that's the main thing, just, uh, controlling what I can control and, you know, just going out there and trying to be the best best of me each and every day. So, >> Mike, a couple of familiar faces in the receiver room, Dylan and Chris Blair. What have you seen from those guys in this kind of game? >> U, I'll say consistency. you know, those guys been very consistent making plays, you know, being where they need to be, you know, understanding the offense and also um you know, just um catching the ball very well, running routes very well. So, it's definitely great to see see those guys uh still in the building and and still playing at a high level. >> How would you describe what it's been like kind of just downloading this offense into your brain just in terms of how much how different or similar it might be in certain respects to what you've done previously? >> How would I >> like just like understand the offense? Um >> um I mean it just comes with studying and reps, you know. Um it's everything is reps, you know, with this game, you know. So it's just uh the more the more you study, the more you you look at the script, the more you look at the playbook, you know, the more familiar you get with it. So um each and every day I'm just studying studying my my ass off and just trying to, you know, get better each and every day at understanding the play calls. And you know, a lot of it is not only just knowing the plays, but knowing why the coach is calling the plays as well. You know, based on situations and you know, the spots that you're at on the field. So, um, I've been doing a lot of that as well, trying to make sure that, uh, Tommy, Tommy and I, and, you know, obviously [clears throat] all the quarterbacks, we're all on the same page with that. >> How good is it to have Vision back out there with you? >> Yeah, it's awesome. You know, obviously, you know, we we all know what he can do. Um, obviously he got that that extension and, you know, it's it's welld deserved. Um, I feel like he's the best running back in the league and, you know, he he's been showing it and I know he's going to continue to show it. So, it's it's exciting to have him back. >> What comfort does it give you when you have seven back there? Like mentally, what does that do for you when you know he's behind you right next to you? >> Yeah, I mean um it's great. You know, we make a joke in the quarterback room sometimes. We're like, uh, if you get in trouble, just be it. I mean, just just give just give him the ball and, uh, something something good is going to happen. So, uh, it gives you a lot of confidence to be able to have somebody like that in the back field cuz then as well, it makes the defense have to respect the run as well so that you know whenever you do get in those passing situations or, um, get back on track situations, you can do either or. And, you know, you can have the team off balance, the defense off balance. >> Going back to Jaylen, obviously you've gone through this, you know, more than you would like, you know, with the recovery process. What would be your biggest piece of advice to him as he goes through it now? Um, the biggest piece of advice, I'll say the the hard days are are definitely the the ones that's going to that's going to that if you get through those hard days, that's it's going to make you better in the end. Cuz like, you know, you you wake up some days and it's like, okay, I feel good. I want to go to rehab. Like, I feel good. But then there some days where you're like, I don't feel like being here. My body is not it's not feeling good. My knee is not feeling good. But like you know sometimes those days are the days that I feel like you you really get better and um when you push yourself you know obviously you got to be smart with it with with something like that injury that serious but you know there is a fine line of okay today we need to push through it so that you know we can you know get over that hump and get to that to that next spot. So >> a follow up on that like what has been your motivation just going through that process over and over and just continuing to come back and you know try to get better each year. >> Yeah. Um, I mean, I would say my faith is definitely my my motivation. Just knowing that, you know, um, you know, God give his toughest battles to his, strongest soldiers. So, it's like for me, I I feel like I I just got to trust in him and I got a strong support system behind me with my family, my wife, you know, uh, everybody's just being there supporting me and I know that, you know, I want to make them proud. So, each and every day I I know I'm doing it for more than just myself, you know, and um, so that that that makes me want to go out there and go hard. So, All right. Thank you.

But, um, I think, uh, I like I like I like where we're heading. Yeah. >> And how tough was last year for you? Uh, you know, you gutted out some stuff and, uh, you know, answered the bell uh, just about every 10 time. How did you get to reflect on how tough that season was for you? >> Yeah. Um, injuries and little things, especially when you get them. I think I had that high ankle in like week four >> and then you play another uh >> 13 games on it and it just never gets better. It um it Yeah, I think it's it's it's a good challenge. It's um you know I think it just goes towards you know the pride I take in being out there and and wanting to be with the guys and doing my job. But um yeah, I think this off seasonason was really good just to heal up, feel healthy again, get everything back to where it needs to be and um you know, like I said that like earlier we're talking about Jaylen injuries and stuff. It's the worst part of the game. It's what sucks, but it it's a part of it and you got to deal with it. So just trying to do my part to prevent that stuff, but um keep fighting through it like I have been. >> You know, obviously the big news yesterday of Jaylen going down, you know, you guys had time to sort of reflect on it. you know, when you it's always that next met up mentality, but what are some of the things that, you know, can't be replicated with this defense with Jayen Walker being helpful? >> Man, he was, uh, he was definitely coming into his own. But he's still going to be here though. Still going to be here helping out everybody. Just, you know, just being in the room. So, you had a chance to talk to him yet? >> Uh, yeah. I texted him. texting him just say wishing him wellbeing that God got him. You know what I'm saying? Like everything happens for a reason and uh it's going to be a testimony when he come back. He come back with Avengers. >> You know, going back to that next man up mentality. You know, obviously things shift. You know, again, you can't replicate what Jaylen does, but how is this defense set even though with his absence? >> Uh everybody just got to be able to do their jobs. You know what I'm saying? Like we we all playing in the NFL, you know what I'm saying? So you got to be able to go out there and compete. do your job is the best that you can do and let let everything fall where it may. >> Timu was just talking about this generational thing that you guys are trying to shake within the linebackers. You guys want to try to get after the quarterback. How much [clears throat] is the generational curse that he's talking about a point of emphasis in that room? >> I mean, I've never heard of a generational curse, but I know that we got pass rushers in the building. So, that's that's exactly what we're going to do this year. So, I've never like thought about it any other way other than getting after the passer. Uh getting after the passer. That's it. >> For you, a change of scenery, it's always good for anybody, but how refreshing has it been to be around this team so far? Oh, >> it's been good. Everybody's going, you know, uh, younger group is kind of weird being the oldest in the room right now. So, but it's it's really cool just to see everybody. Everybody's just yelling really, really well together, just meshing in a locker room. And once we come out here, we're all competing, trying to get each other better and sharpen that knives. going back to the end of practice yesterday and you've been in the NFL, you know, injuries are a part of the game, but when you watch something like that happen, what are the emotions and the thought process behind that? >> I mean, I've been a part of that uh type of injury. So, I think that he'll be all right. He's going to come back strong. >> And what do you enjoy about the next man up mentality and just trying to prove, you know, your worth? >> Man, that's the beauty of the game. That's the beauty of the game. you know, uh, whoever that goes down, the next person stands up and you got to be able to perform to the same level, you know, no let down. So, that's the beauty of the game. >> With the news about Jaylen, how do you sort of process that with the blood of this defense? >> Yeah, I'm I'm gutted from my brother, man, when it when it happened yesterday. And, uh, it's just he means so much to this team and his defense as a leader, the way he works, the way he brings it every single day and his voice. He's a he lead by example guy. It's just it's sad to see him go down yesterday, but I'm praying for him. I'm talking to him. make sure he's up and I know he's still going to help us this season. So, I'm happy to hear that. >> You know, you know how it feels when it affects him and he has his emotions, but when you see it as a player and knowing that it could have happened to you as well, how do you sort of process that? >> Man, you know, it's uh it's a injury sport and it's sad to see though. But this is one of my brother man close to him and I just see how hard he work every single day in the offseason and wait room and before it happened was really sad to see. But, uh, we know praying for him, come keep keep his spirits up and I know he's still going to help us, man, this year. >> Aziz, you've been through this before. You've been through injuries plenty of times in your career. What is it like as a player and what would be your mindset that you want to pass along to Jaylen? >> Yeah, you know, it's definitely tough when you're not out there. Uh, you know, we all want to be out here, play the game we love, but you know, I would tell him just keep your head up. It's going to come. You're going to be good. You're going to make it back healthy. You got the best staff and they're going to get you right. and uh he's he's going to be a brother for life anyway. So, [snorts] we going to keep keep his head up and stay with him and keep his pra keep praising him. So, keep his head up. So, sure, he'll be good. >> Okay. You mentioned the best staff. What do you like about this defensive staff so far and just the mindset they bring to what you guys want to accomplish on defense? >> Yeah, I love I love him as attack style and uh we try to get after every day, be the engine. Uh we we don't want to play slow, we want to play fast and just attack people left and right, whatever it is as a unit, all playing as one. And off of that, with what they're implementing in this defense, even with Jaylen's absence, how confident are you in what this group can do? >> Uh, I'm confident for sure, man. We, you know, we work hard every day. We try to be the best every single day. We compete good on good. And, uh, I feel like we all going to keep improving and try to bring it every single day to just get that 1% better every single day. Just improve our game and feed off each other and play the schemes at the high to the highest level. >> Look, it's not like you wanted Jaylen to get hurt by any stretch of the imagination, but you have an opportunity here. How do you wrap your head around that whenever you have an opportunity to step up, >> man? You know, it's just you just got to put your head down, keep working, and just keep grinding, man. Just take it one day at a time. Uh following your brothers and your coaches, play play team defense, and uh you know, just just keep working hard every single day. Try to improve 1%. Uh do your job. Really, that's all you can do. Just do your job. >> Change of scenery, breath of fresh air for you, I'm sure, at this point in your career. How much of a breath of fresh air has it been here in Atlanta so far? Uh, you know, I'm I'm happy to be back home. >> Yeah. >> Uh, like a dream come true to play for the Falcons and, uh, you know, I'm excited, man. I just can't wait to put all put it all together out there. >> How would you describe this linebacker room? >> I feel like we we got all different types, explosive, you know, versatile players in there and uh, we all all could rush the passer and I feel like uh, just got to keep working every single day and show it every single day and just keep improving. Watch tape. Coach Teimu's getting after us every single day. He's demanding the best out of us and uh we got to bring it. >> What's important for you in this training camp for you personally? Other than getting better every single day, what's important to Aziz this training camp? >> Oh, honing into the details, you know, and uh being myself and not not overthinking stuff and just just try to play as fast as I can, physical as I can, and just do my job and continue to improve and just head down and keep working. That's it. Just work. >> What's it like getting to work with Teemo every day? >> No, it's amazing. and he's a guy that brings energy every single day from the start of practice and he's demanding, you know, he's demanding greatness from every one of us and he's going to push us every single day. So, there's no days off. We got to keep going. We're going every single day. We're getting after it and that's that's the way we got to improve. >> Jumping in late here, um Georgia connection, you know, a lot more dogs around here. Yeah. Uh, you know, than there has been in years past. >> What stands out about a Georgia guy uh in the NFL? What makes him different? Uh, I feel like, you know, the way we prepare and the way Kirby Smart have has built his program down there in Georgia and coming from there to here, you know, it's uh, it's like you get a good jump in the NFL, we what we do at practice and just coming here is like it's a smooth transition. Other other than, you know, learning the playbook and all that extra stuff, but preparedness, we're actually up there for sure the way he runs his program. So, big props to him. Zachariah was saying the other day a little bit different you know the way practices run TL's you know you're not hearing the megaphone and the mic is that an adjustment >> no it is it is different you know when you when you're in Georgia he has that mic so everyone if a student's here walking around campus this is crazy like everyone knows if you mess up or something the whole school might end up knowing by the end of the day >> on a better note than what happened yesterday which is probably the day >> yeah I'm kidding yeah that's tough man we all know what he means to this team. Um especially the guys in the room. Um when he comes in, we feel it. He says something and we feel it. So um he has huge loss cuz we know obviously the barrier that he presents to the team from a leadership standpoint. Um and then just for him personally like he was on the way and so u you know just tough tough for him cuz we know what he was going to present for us this year. >> How do you your job gets harder [music] now? you know, having to get somebody ready or at some some level of yours. >> Yeah, I wouldn't say it get harder. Um, it's training camp. We always trying to have have a development plan for everybody um to see what they can do. So, we want to push them to see what can they do best and then uh how does it help our team. So, um the course is the course. It's just such that we love Cameron got a few more opportunities today. How has he looked? >> He did. He always looked good, man. He's another guy that's his style of play is what he brings to the table especially on first and second down and now uh we just got to continue to develop their um their game holistically. >> I saw Doris uh with uh you know the edge group and uh in individuals is that maybe part of the the replacement plan for for Jayen? >> Uh no it's just cross trainining as much guys as we can. Um really the vision for all those guys is the more you can do the more you get to do. um again the training camp where we can actually train to see uh and push guys to see what they can do from a holistic point and then um see how that fits our game. >> You talk about cross trainining obviously Jaylen is an incredibly versatile player. Talk about his versatility and just how much of a differencemaker that was for this defense. >> Yeah, it was a huge deal cuz it allows us to to play again to provide multiplicity to the defense. That's a big deal. Um where is Jaylen going to be at on this snap to another snap on first, second, and third down. So um but again he's not the only one that can do it. I think there's other guys that has a possibility. Um, that definitely was his game and his value, part of his value to the team. Um, so it was it was tough news for us to lose. >> Brilland Tra is someone that has been trying to come back for a long time. What have you seen from him so far in >> A huge improvement. Huge improvement. I think number one is obviously he's got to take care of his body, stay healthy. Um, losing him for the last two years for a full season, that's tough on anybody. And so easing him back into it, uh, being aggressive and smart with his approach to to practice. Um because I don't have any issue with him playing football. >> His mind, how does his mind look, do you think? >> Good. Real good. >> Like clear and everything. Clear head space, confident. >> That's right. So, uh my experience with him in the past has been awesome. Uh being at Udub, so I know a little bit more than other people. So, um I can I can push him as much as I need to and then pull off when I have to. >> Going back to Jaylen to that point, it's always, you know, next man up mentality, but what are some of the things that, you know, are irreplaceable or can't be replicated Jaylen Walker does? >> Yeah, obviously the versatility. Uh the beauty in how we developed or or built the room was find guys who would do a lot of different things. Um he obviously him being off the ball was kind of the value that he have to the defense for us to have multip multiplicity in how we want to play. So um losing a small piece of that is kind of tough. >> John, is is Cameron Thomas in your room? >> Yes, >> he is. What have you seen from him so far? >> Style of play. >> Style of play. I think um how we want to do things versus what we do is far more important uh than the scheme. So when we out there talking about setting edge, how you set an edge is important. >> And how is he setting it? Like what is his style of play? >> It's got some uh it's rugged. That's the definition in that room. Um the beauty of those guys that we have is we try to build a rugged mindset where we want to carry the torch for the defense and that's a huge challenge cuz we're fighting generational curses in a room and that's the message in we got to fight it, fight it, fight it. So, uh, Styler plays important. >> What is that generational curse that y'all are are fighting? >> Well, there's a bunch of, uh, we haven't affected the QB, you know what I'm saying? And so, for us, the philosophy in the edge room is we got to affect the quarterback so we can affect the game. I mean, it starts with the one game. >> The curse wasn't broken last year with uh, franchise backed socks. >> It's one year. >> Got one year. You know what I'm saying? So, if we don't do it again, we'll talk about to the end before, right? So, uh, good to do it one year and how we did it was multiplicities and pressures. Um, now we got to do it from a fourman rush standpoint. I mean, that's the challenge. >> Going back to Brillin for a second, you said you know a little bit more than most do about Brillin obviously. What's different about his approach to the game? >> Uh, one, well, I don't think he his approach is always the same. Like when it's 11 on 111, he attacks the game >> and so I appreciate that from him. It's just everything it takes to get to that standpoint. Um, so, um, he's the same brand that I know there. Um, obviously a little different in regards to like the injuries that he had to partake the last two years, but I think he's far more mature. He's got a family now. So, that's that's a huge, but it affected his wide and affects his game on the big picture. >> It looked like uh Kendall Daniels, Harold Perkins were getting a couple of snaps kind of on that edge spot. Is that anything you guys are considering given Jaylen's >> Yeah, it's a good question. And I think again the biggest thing is like what can guys do and so the more you can do the more you get to them. So we want to like crosschain as much people that we think we can so that we can give the offense a lot of different looks. We want to make sure they can operate post snap especially at quarterback. So never want to give them a clear picture. Always want to make sure that at the snap of the ball, that's when they start their thinking and not thinking.

Um [laughter] and and but [clears throat] you know that that's just all part of the the plan and the business of the business side of things. So, it was it was a cool experience, but it it was definitely getting getting a little tough tough at times, too. >> Why was it important for for y'all to get this deal done now? So, he was like, why change? You know, you you should always be yourself. You know, never change. He's never act like you got to be Superman on the field, you know, just be Jean. And, you know, you don't have to be nobody else. And I I knew that because just my faith and how I go about it. Like, if I just play my game how I always play it and always know how to play it, then, you know, everything's going to take care of itself. Um, so it was it was definitely a cool moment, but yeah, I I'm always going to be myself. I'm never going to change um after getting this and you know, I that's just who I am as a person. No, we have um you know obviously we we talk a lot just because we're kind of we're in the same you know conversation. Um you know our our the BJ Gibbs debate is is actually cool to see. Um, so it's cool to to experience that. And then we just we just told each other just just hang in there. Um, everything's gonna get done. Everything's gonna gonna be all right. And, you know, it's it's cool to see him go through it, too. and I hope he gets the most out of, you know, what he deserves because he deserves it. Deserves it all. Um, but it's it's definitely a cool feeling to see two two offensive guys, uh, offensive weapon guys that, uh, got drafted in the same class. Um, and and now that we're in our going in our fourth year, we're talking about extensions. And, you know, it's just it's just a testament to what God blessed us with and and who we are as people. like it don't mean that you got to you know start buying everything you know just just be yourself you know just be myself and you know I want to just you know just say thank you to him because you know he he made it hard for me for a reason and when I first got here like he made me do everything and he had a plan for me and he made me go to receiver, kickoff return, punt return, running back like did I did everything and I had to know everything and for him to do that and for him to just understand the plan from when I first got here and you know it was it was a very tough first summer for me but you know now now that I'm sitting here reflecting on that like it was all for a reason obviously and you know then then with Raheem coming in um and continuing the same plan and Zack Robinson continuing the same plan and then now with Kevin and Tommy like you know I just get blessed with these coaches um and then with coach Petri you know he's been here the whole time like he's the I say he's the best running back coach and it's not just because of what's the product on the field but just who he is as a man as a person but he's he made it hard for me like this journey people think that you know it could be easy or or I can just I can just get things handed to me like that that was never the plan um with coach Petri and yeah he's a father figure to me a big brother but on the field no matter what we do like I don't care if I had the 2,000 yard season like he's like bro there's more in the tank there's more in the tank so um just reflecting on all that stuff and then now to to sign the contract like you know even coach Peter is like bro like this contract don't mean nothing don't mean nothing so uh yeah it's a blessing to to to reflect on it like that and to see Uh because you know I try to do do everything for them and and lead for them and and just put a smile on my face. So it it was cool. >> Who's the most surprising person or maybe the coolest person that you've heard from in the last couple days? Um, well, there's been some cool people, but like as soon as the news hit, Matthew McConna hit me. As soon as it as soon as it hit, I think I think it hit at like 7:56, like 7:58, he texted me. He texted me. Um, so, but yeah, a lot of like awesome like really cool people texting me, but like it was cool to see him, you know, as soon as it hit like he was the first one. Uh, so that was cool. I know you said, you know, this isn't going to change you or anything like that, but just mentally. >> Yeah. Been on the field the last two days, does it feel different? Is it an exhale for you? Like, is it obviously going through the whole offseason, it's still on your mind. Yeah. You're out there. How do you describe it? >> Oh, man. I'm I'm happy. Like, I'm happy. Y'all probably see me out there. They're slowly ramping me up, but even during team drills, you know, I had to go over there and and do my conditioning and run and stuff. So, I'm trying to tell them like, bro, like let's do it. But I got to give back to the guys. Um because that's just it just that's just what it means to me and and they mean a lot to me. So, you know, I love to be like I'm a competitor and I love to talk. I don't talk smacking games obviously, but to the defense like I be talking talking and but they love it though because it just gets them better. So, when I get back out there um you know, I can't wait to get back out there. I think it's like later on this week and and then we'll we'll go from there. But yeah, it's cool to it's cool to be back, you know, with the pads on and and getting going. >> Go ahead. I was just telling teammates, are you aware of what the quarterbacks say about you as a safety valve? >> Yeah. Yeah, I am. It's um it's always cool like to to know that both the guys um even even the new guys, you know, they're they're like be you know if if if all else fails like you the guy like and they don't I it's cool cuz you know I I always say like you know you could take a five yard pass and take a 50 yards or you could take a 15 yard pass take it like they rely on me to not just catch the ball but they rely on me to catch and and score or or make something spectacular happen. And you know, it's cool to to have that trust from them cuz anywhere where I'm out on the field. Um they just look and then they'll look and they'll see me, they're like, "All right, you know, just just to make sure." But, you know, it's cool to to be that kind of guy for them. Obviously, Drake's the best receiver ever. Um you know, he's he's the target. Uh and then Jan, he's balling. Oz balling. Um all the new guys, young guys. Obviously, Zachariah is, you know, he's going to be a star, man. Um, so, and then Kyle is a star. So, it's like it's cool seeing all the the new faces, too. Um, even in my room, you know, bro is is been learning a lot, been getting so much better. And and then, you know, Nate, uh, TG, like all these guys, um, have been playing really good. Cash. So me like like to back to his question, seeing all that from my perspective and now being on the field um has been a really cool thing, really cool experience because they're getting better and every single day is going to be hard and you know I can't wait to just you know embrace that hard with them. So it'll be cool. >> I know Nicole like um you know negotiated a lot of the contract and stuff like that but how important was the three years for you just with running backs like you know trying to reach the market as many times before 30. So, how important is that for you? >> Yeah, that that was that was huge. Um, you know, I know running backs typically negotiate four four plus years. So, for Nicole to negotiate that and for them to come down and in in that year uh to to make it three years is, you know, is is pretty cool because I know where this position can go. Obviously, I pray for no injuries um and all that stuff and continue to stay healthy through this journey. But, you know, for that to happen is is, you know, it's cool. Obviously, like the three years is just a is a break point cuz, you know, I ain't trying to go nowhere. Um trying to be here, trying to stay here. Um that's why I'm happy they got it done two years early cuz like, you know, I just want to I just want to create a legacy here, man. Like, you know, for the fans, for the city. Um, you know, the city of Atlanta's been nothing but support for me. Um, and I I need them to to feel that because, you know, when shoot, we I live out here in Brasleton, Brasleton, Georgia, and I be I be getting gas and the gas clerk, you know, be just happy just, you know, smiles like I don't think she watched football her life, but she knows like just who I am. and and that's that's the effect I want to have on on everybody in the city. Um so that's why we're trying to work as hard as possible, man, to like to to to win here. Uh because, you know, just seeing all the support here is is a cool thing. Um and I just want to be a part of it. >> So many guys say >> Yeah. You know, so many guys say, you know, it's a business. >> You go through it. I mean, uh your agent was with you throughout so much of the process communicating. What was part of the business or going through this? I don't want to say surprise you, but that you learn, you know, from it that was most important to you. >> Yeah. [clears throat] Um the cool thing the cool thing with them and with Nicole, um even Ian, like they they know who I am as a person and I be trying to stay as far as away as possible. So she was like, "We're going to handle this. Um you know, you're going to if we need something like you can you'll step in." But you know, I was I was really out of it um for most of it. Like the only thing was the business part was just not practicing. Uh but that's that just happens. Uh but other than that like she she took she took the wheel. She took care of everything and you know they were they did the same thing upstairs and it's it was a smooth smooth process for me. So but I know like you know if if guys do go through it be you know after me um just just embrace the process. Don't get stressed out. Uh that's I think that's the one thing that I try not to do like and she told me too like just just stay who you are you know let me stress if that's the that's what I have to worry about. Um so it was cool. >> Can we get a more formal introduction of your family here? I mean you can't just bring them in here and not see who they are. >> Yeah that's my girlfriend day. Um that's my auntie Cararissa and then that's she works for Clutch but she's my favorite person in the world. She one of our that's Coral and Nicole. Heat.

title: Marlon Humphrey Joins The Lounge, Discusses Approach Entering Year 10 | Baltimore Ravens
text: [music] Welcome into the lounge. I'm Garrett Downing. I'm here with Clifton Brown and we are so excited to sit down with one and only Marlon Humphrey. Marlon, thanks for the time today. So, I want to start with your off seasonason because I got to believe you have the most unique offseasons of anybody on the team and this one it seems like it went to a whole new level cuz you basically were living in South Korea based on what I saw on social media. Tell me about that. Yeah. So, it's I will say there's always some sort of a side quest that seems to just happen every offseason for me. Um, this one was very unique. Um, living in was living in Soul um, South Korea for basically total of like 2 months. So, it was very uh, obviously different. It was a lot of uh, it was it was just completely different. a very fast-paced city. Like, you know, I've been in New York obviously, but they take, you know, walking fast and like stay in your lane and move and to another level. But it was it was really fun just kind of seeing a different culture living somewhere for for that extended period of time. But it was uh it was very fun. >> And then I saw on social media that you welcomed a baby over there. >> Welcome a baby. Yes. So, we went over there. My wife um >> congratulations. >> She Yes. Thank you. She went down her own rabbit hole of the the postpartum care and Korea was I guess ranked the best in the world and um I obviously did not do that research. So I was like it seems a little expensive to go out there and she was like this is for my health. So once she said that and all that jazz I was I went with it. So happy wife, happy life. And um experiencing it it was it was just totally different. They are like all about getting the woman back into great health. And just as soon as the baby came out, they were like, she's like, "How's the baby? Is this They're like for the first 24 hours we're going to take care of the baby. You were just focused on healing." And then it's like a week goes by, they're like, "You need to focus on healing. We'll worry about the baby." So there's a lot of um it was crazy. I didn't even hear the baby cry for an entire month. >> They basically if they even heard a peep from the baby, they were like, "Hey, you need help?" when you and so it was very unique. They had the my son they had them in a room that you could it was a glass wall so you could see through it [snorts] and you could it was just weird cuz they were like with you but they weren't. But whenever you wanted to see the baby you could but they were just big on like let's get you you need to eat this, you need to do this. Hey we're going to do this massage. We're going to do this yoga. There was so many different things going on. I I obviously didn't know what was going on. I would just come back from workout and be like where's the baby? like right there. And so it was [laughter] uh but it was really cool. She um we actually cut the strip short cuz she was just she healed so much faster than um the previous birth. And um it was it was all good. So it was uh it was different. He's got a he has a birth certificate all in Korean. So [laughter] I can't tell you what's on there, but he's he's a healthy baby boy. >> That's great. >> You you come from a great family, Marlin, and now you have a family of your own. How has dad life changed you as a player person both either? >> Man, it's um I would say it's it's changed my my you know the job of football, but it's really changed it's changed the planning. I would say um I'm very routine and trying to get in here early like in the off day. Try to get in really early >> just so I can get back and kind of help out with the breakfast and different things. And um that's kind of just how everything goes. If I in the offseason if I want to go golf, I try to golf early to to get back to to help out with the kids. But it's also really made me want to play and prepare, keep the body in as best shape as possible to kind of play as long as I can. It's been, you know, having a suite last year, it was it was really cool to be able to come over, kiss the kids, kiss the wife, and um, you know, my dad when he played, I I wasn't alive, >> and I I really want to be able to make some memorable plays, have some memorable moments, and to be able to have the family all experience them. So, that's kind of what's changed, transformed, um, from, [clears throat] you know, this job and having a family. How did you handle the challenge of getting prepared for this season during the time you were in South Korea? >> Yeah, so that was that was a challenge. I was I was happy I kind of pre planned. I actually brought a trainer from the States um to South Korea and then I had a um South Korean kind of rehab guy. So it was a very unique team. Um one guy knew English, one guy didn't. So, it was a lot of translating throughout the rehab sessions, but I was very um I was very impressed by the advanced guy was Sunen was the guy that kind of knew a little uh he knew English but not that much. And then Jay, it was a really good team. Um their their place is called PT Lab. Vinn was going to Korea. There's a really good rehab place. And um they I found out some things about my body that I just never never known as to everyone has something in their body and say like this usually bothers me, this usually bothers me, but they really got down to kind of the root cause of why your body does this and why your body does that. And he was >> what I initially went for was just kind of generic rehab work. And what I received was it's basically like a alltime care was checking in with me every morning, check with checking in with me just all the time. and uh we were able to get some good stuff done and I was able to come back here feeling really good. >> Do do you feel like because of that you are going into the season like healthier uh better shape like any kind of how that's going to affect you this year? >> Yeah, so last year man it was um it was a really tough year from the health perspective. Um, I just I I let kind of something linger um for a while and I kind of pushed really hard to get through training camp. I was very admin on trying to be out there every single day. Um, and it just you you kind of fought fought fought and so it lingered throughout the entire season. And so that was my biggest goal in the offseason to go into the season painless. And that was that really was my biggest offseason focus. So, it's been great to just like I mean it I have been just enjoying this camp just being able to just not have to worry about something lingering every single day. And really I was not able to find really uh a solution to it. So that was kind of the main focus and so far it's working really well and uh hopefully it just remains like that. You're a guy that like you you you always practice like you don't miss many practices and and it seems like that's something you take pride in. >> I do. Is that was it hard I guess to deal with that last year because you probably hearing it sounds like you maybe should have or could have taken a day. >> Yeah, that there was actually like days when they hey let's just take a day and I'm just you know it's the football has changed a lot as we all know. It's but there's I'm a little still like wired old school of the whole like no man you don't need off day like you're you're whatever. So that that those were if I I don't really regret many things in life but that would be something I probably did up I mean if someone comes up to you and says hey you should take today or you should we want you to take this day you know it's even if you go out there do a little but I was like nah I'm doing the whole day and and [laughter] so I think I was the only veteran last year that practice every single training camp day um and so that's that's a you know pride is whatever whatever But especially if you're kind of dealing with something, um that's when it's really important to kind of listen to the resources you we have here cuz we got some great resources that you know kind of were telling me, hey, hey, this that. But that's that's kind of what made last year different. You don't want to fight through training camp because the season, if you're going to fight, you want to fight through the season. >> Yeah, that makes sense. >> Like a lot of guys around here, you have never played for a head coach other than John Harbaugh until now. Can you just describe the energy around here since you've been back? >> Yeah, it's um that that's something I didn't think would be that's what's been surprising. I would say it's uh I've kind of got to ask that a little bit and I I don't it it's um it's hard to put into words. It's just I don't know if change everyone's just excited about change, but from Jesse to even the the echo of the coaches, man, it it's like it really is like night and day different. Um it's it I I just don't know what it is, though. It's hard to really put into words um what what it is. There's just a a really different energy. Also, it's I really like, you know, that the head coach is a defensive head coach. It's really cool to be in a meeting and Jesse just takes the clicker and he's like, "I'm about to coach for the next hour." So, [laughter] it's it's uh it's it's very it's very uh Harbs would always pop in every once in a while, but he would never just take over like that. But, I think Jesse's a really good teacher. He has a very calm, >> collective presence about him. But when he addressed something cuz I knew Jesse obviously when he was not the I don't even know what his position was exactly but that's kind of what surprised me as well when he gets in the team meeting he he does have that presence uh that kind of you know Harball obviously love that guy he but he was like alpha like you know as we all know. So when he addresses a team, it's like you already know that's kind of how he is. But >> it's been um very interesting to how Jesse's addressed the team, how I feel like he's addressed certain situations in practice already of like, hey, we ain't doing this. Hey, we're not doing this, we are doing this. And so it's been uh it's been encouraging though just because the >> the coaches also echo that same bell and they it seems like I know in my room for sure it seems like these dudes really want to figure out how can we help you and how can we be a better team and um I'm really liking the energy they're kind of spreading throughout. >> That's awesome. to I guess the average person, how much do you think this defensive system will be different or similar to what the Ravens have played before? >> I think it reminds me a little bit of um Mike Mcdonald's defense with all the the different things that are that are in it. It's um I think it's cuz we got some really smart safeties. It takes it takes some pretty smart players and I think we got the smart enough guys. uh around, but it's uh it's definitely takes it takes some time, but playing it so far these days of camp, man, it's it's really if you get it to where you want it to be, it's just really hard to beat. And um I remember when Mike kind of inserted it, I wasn't the biggest fan of it just cuz it was just new. It was just new. But I think that year we had that number one defense, I think. >> Mhm. And um it just once you get really good at it, it's and there's even some new wrinkles um that Jesse's kind of put on it, but once you get really really good at it, it's really really really hard to stop. And um so I'm just excited. I think it'll it'll be kind of similar to some things in the past, but I think the the coaching points that are being put in, especially for like me and Nate and Cheeto, it's um it's making us play. It's making us think more in a in a good way as opposed to just, hey, let's just kind of just put all of our buckets and play man and play zero and different things like that. So, I think it'll be similar, but I think it'll it'll be kind of back to that staple of, you know, Ravens defense that holds on, ends big games. So, I'm really excited for it. >> Along those lines, you've talked about this over the years, but kind of the expectations of a defense and the history that exists here and the legacy and the tradition and all that. Do you feel like, and I remember going back in the spring, Rocoan Smith talked uh on podium and he said he feels like it's kind of a contract year for the whole defense just like from an expectation standpoint. Can you give me your perspective on that and how that approach is affecting you guys going into this year? >> Yeah, I think I think there's been a lot of uh you know, I'm I'm just a realistic person. I think there's been a lot of patience um from the um from the upstairs of the the standard being not met for for some time now. And usually when that happens in most organizations, the a whole you just tear down the whole house and just restart. And I feel like there's been a lot of patience um and trust and belief in the guys. But at some point, you know, there's we got to get it to where it needs to be just cuz I mean, not every organization is the Baltimore Ravens known for defense and different things, but you know, Jesse brought up the other day, you know, we had the most fourth quarter blown leads in the league last year. Um, or maybe the past two years, whatever he said. So, there's just it's not like we're far off. We're just not finishing. And it doesn't matter where you what's the reason as to why you're falling up short. there's just what's acceptable and what's not acceptable. And so I kind of agree with Roan. It definitely does seem like that. It's like we either got to figure it out or they got to get somebody in here that can figure it out. So we we kind of do feel like that. You know that you know it's it's just time and so that's kind of what we're chasing. >> You're always honest whenever you talk. Um and I remember at the end of last season you were I mean you were pretty honest. You were like I don't know if I'm going to be back here next year or not. like it's I know the business side of things, but like how did you approach I guess the uncertainty around that going into the off season? Um and what was your outlook on that? >> Yeah, I think um I think just I went into the offseason um Harbaugh got let go and I was just in like shoot, we'll see where I end up um if I'm on the team or not on the team. But I didn't I didn't really treat it much different. I think um I was really to honestly end the season the only thing I was thinking about was how can I get healthy to be able to to play, you know, kind of the level of the brand of football that I like to play. And so it uh it did it was going to be a little different. I was uh I had some some things of just hey honey, I don't let's just kind of play it by ear to figure out [laughter] what we're doing. Um but um shortly there kind of towards the start of the um offseason, you know, Eric kind of let me know that I was I was going to be on the team. Um so I kind of took from there just kind of stay trying to get back healthy and um now we're here. >> Mhm. >> You've been open also talking about the end of your career or whenever that is. Do you have any idea how long you want to play? Man, I uh it it's so hard to even to even think about it just because like I I just I feel like it just feels so incomplete. I I um I just we've had those teams where like, man, we could win it all and you you feel like you're you're so close and you you you want that. And that's just it would uh that's just something I I really just want to be able to say that you know at the end of the season you could just sit back and realize we won the final game. And it's it's uh it's just hard for me to even like think of you know some people they're like you know I'll just fade off in the sunset but it's uh it's hard to just even put into perspective without at least getting a Super Bowl. Um, but it so it it makes it hard. I sometimes I'm like, maybe I'll do this and then I'm like, man, maybe I should be Kas Campbell and just be out here till I'm almost 40 years old [laughter] if if if I could still get the job done. So, um, it makes it it makes it hard to think about, but I I uh I do I will say for like the last two years, I've I've definitely taken it just one day at a time trying to enjoy um trying to enjoy every day because you you really don't know when it's when it's going to be your time. I'm holding Lombardi in February. [laughter] I I that that would Oh, man. If that that would that would be that would be awesome. And I would definitely that would be a sit down with the wife and that that [laughter] would it would definitely spark that conversation. I think you it's it's when you win one I I would imagine you definitely feel like man it would be awesome to team I got drafted with >> right had a play that contract out finish out another contract finished it with a win that would just be uh kind of just a chef's kiss on the on it all. So, seems like, you know, it would it would also be then you're like, "Ah, but do we go back to back?" So, [laughter] it would be But, um, that that's just a a goal I've had in mind. When I came to this league, I had two goals. It was to make a Pro Bowl cuz my dad made a Pro Bowl and get to a Super Bowl and win one. Cuz my dad got the Super Bowl, he lost his. So, those were the two things I remember. It's It's crazy. my dad um and my mom used to tell me when my dad stopped playing. They didn't do like anything football related for like years. So he he he [laughter] like we didn't even he he he talked so little about football we didn't even know any of anything about him. And so I remember like just randomly going through some random stuff and picking up a football all the pro um Pro Bowlers. >> It was like dusted off, faded. My dad just not even taking care of it. And so that was like when I just remember thinking like man I want to play in the Pro Bowl and man I want to go to the Super Bowl. And um so I've been able to get the Pro Bowl. That's that's been awesome to to have those posting accolades and Super Bowl is it's that's just that's just number one on the list. >> I mean I think everyone wants to win. You won one or two at Alabama. >> One, lost one. >> Okay. >> Yep. >> So you have that championship experience. Yep. >> And is that kind of like in the back of your mind when you think about what you still want to accomplish in your career? Yeah, it is like, you know, I won a high school state championship, won the college, and it's just I just I I remember I was talking to another Alabama teammate and this is a while ago. You hop in colleges. >> I I thought that was like uh I I didn't know anything about the NFL, but I thought that was like cool and I've just come to realize that's really not that cool. That's kind of the envision that I that I see for it. And obviously Derek in in that offense coming downhill just makes it. So I I think there's so many different ways to do it. And everything I've I've heard I just introduced myself to Doyle yesterday. I had not I had not got a chance >> to really talk to him and I heard he is a just football >> junkie. title: Motivation Remains the Same for Zay Flowers After Contract Extension | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: The big story for the Ravens at training camp this week was the contract extension for wide receiver Zay Flowers. before hitting the practice field this morning. He officially put pen to paper on that new deal, which is reportedly a 4-year contract extension that will pay him $140 million over the course of that extension with over a hundred million guaranteed in an average per year of $35 million. It's a big time deal for the Ravens top receiver. And a big question for him today when he met with reporters after practice was how he's going to stay motivated after this deal. He is now set financially for life. He talked about the fact that his motivation remains unchanged. All he knows is how to work and he plans to continue with that mindset. [music] >> We ain't we still got to get a Super Bowl. That that nothing don't change. Nothing don't change. I'm still doing the same thing. 5 in the morning getting in here and working every day. Now, getting this deal done before the season is just great for both sides. The Ravens know they have their top receiver under contract for the long term. And Z Flowers knows that he has that guaranteed money and that financial security. So, it's a win-win for both sides. And something that is abundantly clear is that the Ravens are going to find ways to get the ball in his hands this season. They gave him that contract because he is a major weapon in this offense. and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle talked today about how valuable Z is to this group. >> I feel like he's been a lead by example guy where like he shows up, he he handles his business, he's a really hard worker. Um he doesn't have many bad days and and that's that's a a great trait, really. >> Sean, how much would you have liked the opportunity to do a speech to introduce your recent seventh overall >> Yeah, great question.
