What have you seen from the rookie Blake Miller? Maybe leaning on some of the veterans in that room. Uh yeah, I think the rookies have done a really nice job of coming in and embracing the culture. You know, I think that all starts with Penil. He's an unbelievable player. He's an unbelievable leader and I think when you walk in that room, you know the standard and you know that he's going to do it and he's going to hold you to it and I think it makes everybody around him better. A >> lot of weapons on this offense. I know you've got to be excited, especially with a quarterback with such a high completion percentage year in and year out. What has stood out to you the most that's maybe gotten you excited ahead of the season? >> I think just having the weapons and so many different people that can make plays and change the game. you know, we'll draw up plays and we have scheme, we have reasons we do things, but at the end of the day, it's about those guys going out there and making plays and, you know, when you have the level of talent that they've been able to build here between Brad and Dan over the last six years, uh, it's really fun to be a part of, and it it creates a lot of problems for other teams. >> We'll get more specific now to the quarterback Jared Goff, your first year working with him. How would you describe how the OCQB relationship maybe looks like behind the scenes and how you two work together? >> Yeah, I think it's a very close relationship. I I you know, maybe that's what people assume, but it's it's constant conversations. I'm getting calls on my way into work. I'm getting texts at home. You know, I'm calling him and texted him, and it's you know, you you could be in the middle of the day on an off day and and something pops into your brain and the first person I'm going to go to is him and he's probably going to hit me first and say, "Hey, can we do this? Are we thinking about that? What do we do here?" Uh it's something that I I've loved as I've gotten to know him is he never puts it down or walks away from it. I'm very much that way. Uh so it's been so much fun to just challenge each other and push each other uh to get the best out of each other. And I think that's really what stood out to me here these first couple months. >> It's interesting you mentioned the comparison just watching now six days of practice. You guys almost have the same demeanor out there. Just business as usual day in and day out. Doesn't get too high, doesn't get too low. How do you think that makes him one of the most effective quarterbacks in the NFL? I >> I think it's a huge part of playing that position. You have to have a short memory. You have to be even keel. You you can't live and die on every play. Uh you do the best you can. Every time the ball snapped, you reset. You get back in the huddle and you do it again. I think that's so important to play in that position at a high level and I obviously as you said he's done it that way for so long. Uh it's really impressive. >> All right. Outside looking in, what made this job so appealing to you before getting here? >> I think a lot of the things we've talked about so far, you know, it's the talent they've been able to build here, the culture, the attitude, the way that they do things as an organization from ownership on down. Uh it's a special place and it was, you know, just uh I was thrilled to have the opportunity to be a part of it and it's been everything probably more than I expected uh when I first took the job. >> Well, we heard from Sam Leaporta. He's excited you're here. You've typically had a tight end friendly offense. Can you take us into that a little bit and how maybe the NFL in general is maybe going more toward tight end friendly sets that they've been running. >> Yeah, you've certainly seen that trend around the NFL. I think a lot of that again is going to be talent driven. You know, I've been around a lot of great tight ends, which has been awesome. So, their production has increased, and that's kind of the challenge you make to the offense. Say, "Hey, you want to have production in this offense? You have to show me that you can do things at a really high level." Sam has certainly done that throughout his career, and it needs to continue every time we step on the field. Um, and I think that's kind of what you're seeing throughout the NFL, the matchups that are created in the passing game, the things that these guys can do in the run game. Uh, it makes them and the offense very difficult to defend. >> You're also known for your run game. What would you say is your staple or most important philosophy in that area? I >> I feel like I'm coping out a little bit here, but it all comes back to what do the guys do best. You know, I can come in here and say, "Hey, we're going to run this type of scheme and we're going to do it this way all the time, but if the guys on the field, that's not what plays to their strength. We're not going to get the best out of the offense." So that to me is a lot of what the offseason in training camp is about is figuring out what schemes we are good at, why how we can dress them up, how we can complement them, what fits our players best. I think that's so important in the run and the pass game. And then part of the run game is about attitude. You know, I think the overall mentality of a run game, and I've said this to the offense, and I've challenged them on this, is at the end of the day, if you're really good at running it, you should be able to tell the other team you're doing it. And if they can't stop you, it's really hard to defend. Uh, and I think that's a mindset as much as it is execution. You talk about your scheme and it really depends on the talent and and wanting to utilize what you have in the room. So, how have they kind of responded to what you've brought to the table? How has it been meshing with the new guys on offense? >> I think it's a big part of the culture that was probably here before I got here. And I think you see it every day of practice. These guys go out and compete. You know, Saints been doing this how long now? And he's done it at such a high level, but if you looked out there, he's probably going as hard as he did his rookie year as he's trying to make a name for himself in this league. And I think that attitude, that effort, that intensity brings out the best in all of them. And again, as you said, it's going to show me, hey, if you want it, let's go get it. Let's earn it and make sure the ball comes to you because I got to look everybody else in the eye and make sure we're doing the best things for the team. >> That's got to stem from the head coach. I have to ask you, and I think everybody wants to know, too, what that relationship is like with Dan Campbell. >> It's been uh probably again more than I ever imagined. I I I'm a sponge. Like, I ask questions, pick his brain. uh not in awe of him at times, but you just feel really blessed to have the opportunity to learn from him, work under him, uh challenge him, and try to make him better as he pushes me. Um, and it's it's been awesome. I've learned a ton, uh, grown a ton as a coach, as a person. So, it's it's been great. >> You've learned a lot from Dan Campbell. You've obviously been at a couple spots before this. Your path as an offensive coordinator. Is there anything unique about your journey that maybe people might not know? I >> I think I've been very fortunate to be a lot of around a lot of great coaches in a small amount of time. You know, I think back to six years in Minnesota, four offensive coordinators, you know, uh Pat Shurmer, Norv Turner, Gary Kubak, Kevin Stfansky, like so many different people I think helped grow me as a coach, grow me as a person to help me get to this opportunity. Um I'm very fortunate of that. Um but that's probably the biggest thing that maybe people don't know or or weren't aware of. >> We know that people know you and Ben Johnson, the familiarity with him. How often are you guys maybe even still communicating, keeping in touch? You were a groomsman, I believe, in his wedding. >> Yeah, so we gaed together at Boston College for two years and got really close. He was in my wedding, I was in his wedding. Um I hope they lose every game this year. [laughter] No, I'm kidding. Uh but no, he he's a very close friend. He he's a person I put a ton of trust in uh as a friend, as a mentor. Uh I know he's not going to give me any insight in for any help. You know, I I think we're way past that. Um but no, we talk, you know, regularly. Uh someone that that I'm going to rely on for football and a lot of things outside of football. And uh yeah, he is he's a special person that I really do enjoy being being acquainted with. >> Big into golf and and that stems from back in Massachusetts. Uh can you give the fans a little peak behind the curtain as the the caddying days? >> And so I I grew up cattying. That was my high school, my college job. So I love the game. I put the clubs away. I'm done playing. They're not going to come out till after the season. Uh but it is it's a fun sport. It's a challenging sport. Uh it's a mentally draining sport. Uh Welssey High School native run the Rocket Mortgage Classic this weekend, so got to give him a shout out. uh always like to watch him play and but I did I grew up around the game. Love Caddy and I'm happy to carry bags for a little bit of extra money when needed and uh it was a great job growing up. >> Well, coach, we so appreciate the time. We're happy to have you here in Detroit and good luck this season. >> Yeah, appreciate it. Thanks a lot.

title: Early Risers & Slow Starters at Lions Training Camp
text: Welcome back everybody to another episode of Lions Collective today. Pack show training camp. We got to get into it. Shamir Gibbs, what's going on with his extension? We'll talk about it all here on Lions Collective. [music] A lot of things are different here on Lions Collective. I'm testing a new microphone I bought 20 minutes ago. I'm wearing these big headphones and no Colton Pouncy. So, there's a lot of things going on right now. Colton is is is busy with real life things right now. He's going to miss today's show. He's been he's been active, so we appreciate him. We'll catch him next week to kind of recap some of the stuff, but I'm your host Jeff Freddy. Worth Sports Grunch Time Sports joined alongside me, Justin Rogers, Detroit Football Network. Will Birfield 971 the ticket and guys, training camp is happening. Things are happening. Jir Gibbs' contract hopefully is happening in the near future. We'll talk about that. Brad Holmes went on SiriusXM. I know people are pro probably saw the clip and and got to see, you know, people try to read between the lines and and Brad was asked about it, but what what was your guys' interpretation of that and just maybe the timeline just week to week here updating the fans on when you think it gets done officially? >> Go ahead on the XM thing, Will. >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's just a GM asking a question carefully about an ongoing negotiation. And I think a lot of people probably latched on to the fact that when the follow-up question was posed to Brad as but you're going to get it done eventually and Brad said hopefully it might have cast some level of doubt on onto this conversation. In my mind there isn't any and I don't think anyone should read into that that Jir Gibbs is making an outrageous ask. I'm sure based on Bejian's contract that he signed yesterday, Jir is looking for and going to sign in the neighborhood of $23 million per year. I know the reported figure for Bejan was up to 75 million over three years, but the actual average base salary is what 22.5 22.25 and um I would venture to guess pretty confidently that um both the Lions and and Gibbs would be comfortable with an average base salary per year of 23. And and I think that would get this deal done and I think it'll get it done soon. Let's uh let's get everybody to tune out right now as I go even more math heavy. Um [laughter] so going back to offseason projections, I projected uh Gibbs at four for 77. And [clears throat] when I said that number, it was baking in the 14.3 million fifth year uh option they had. And so when you look at at Bejon's contract, as Will was saying, it was presented as three for 75. In reality, it's it's about three for 67. And that money, it kicks in in 2028. So it's 2028, 2029, 2030. The 27 figure is his fifth year option. And so the the only notable difference there is his fifth year option is actually less than Gibbs. Even though he was drafted earlier, because Gibbs had multiple Pro Bowls, Beijian had one. Gibbs' fifth year option was 14 million. Uh Bejian's was 11 million. Uh, I I look at these two guys as 1A, 1B in terms of value running backs in the NFL. I'm talking production, age, durability, like these are the two guys. I you could argue in one given year, there are other guys in that mix obviously, but in terms of like long-term value, these are the the cream of the crop in the league. And I think there's very little that separates them. It's really just the type of back you like. Do you like a little bit more dual threat and speed or you'd like a little bit uh bigger between the tackles? Uh probably a body frame set to handle a bigger workload over a longer period of time. So they're both unbelievable talents. And if Gibbs' annual average value is identical to Bean's, it would not surprise me. But he does have that little $3 million extra on the fifth year option. So, I was just doing the math and and realistically I think Gibbs is probably looking at three years uh I don't know well four years I guess 80. So if John's is is four years 78 Gibs is probably four years 80 four years 81 um there's going to be the similar incentives in there that let him elevate it to what he needs to but I I think these contracts are going to come in real real close and rightfully so. I like I said, Bejian has gotten better every year. Behan led the NFL in yards from scrimmage last year. Uh they're they're just both exceptional talents. I don't think either one can make a case to be paid even beyond a fraction of a percentage more than the other. It's just just the way it is. And so, um you know, the Lions have to belly up to the table and and and pay the piper. It's just what it is. You can't get around it. You can't uh undercut Bejian. going to have to at least match that. But, uh, I I really thought there was a good chance it got done today. It did. You know, they had an off day that Bejan got done. I think the Lions are are urgent in wanting to get, >> uh, Gibbs into camp. So, I I would be really surprised if this thing drags out for too long, regardless of maybe the cryptic tone that that Holmes had in this interview today. Yeah, I will say now that the pads have come on in camp and and the run game is treated a little bit more seriously, there is somewhat of a ticking clock to get Jir back out there, especially in a new offense with a new OC and with a number of new or reshuffled offensive linemen. I mean, you talk to offensive linemen who have played the game for a long time, either past or present, like I was having a conversation with TJ Lang a couple days ago, for example, and and and John Jansen from our station, which said the same thing. And it takes time for offensive linemen and running backs to operate in concert and for a running back to understand how an offensive lineman plays his blocks and for an offensive lineman to understand how a running back sees things. And look, Gibbs is a pretty instinctive player. I don't I don't think um he he is a very hard running back to block for there's a crease. He's going to hit it. But look, you you do have a new right tackle in there. You've got a new center in there. You've got a a left tackle who previously has only played right tackle for the most part. So, um, with with the the pads on and and these team periods now being more meaningful in the scope of getting the offense ready for the season, I do think we're beginning to feel just a little bit some anxiousness. In fact, that was the word that Campbell used to get Jir back on the field to get him into the offense and just for the the team to have a better idea of what it's going to look like when they hand him the ball this season. >> I think Jacob Sailors and Jabari Small are very excited by the opportunity they have right now, right? Like Vaky's out. This is a good chance for them to kind of state their case for a roster spot. But I also think they would like Giz back in there because they are working their asses off of practice. I looked at Jacob Sailors walking off the field the other day and you know just just sluggish. But like he had double the workload in this practice. So they're putting a lot of of work on the other guys. I think Pacheco's looked really good. We'll get maybe more into some of the names that have looked good here in camp coming out. But um you know I I think like I said Jabari Small, Jacob Sailors, this is an opportunity for them to take advantage of. But >> by the way, >> Jean sign, you know, they've been kind of bouncing ideas off each other, and it sounds like Bjan is telling Jir to hang in there. And Campbell's like, "No, get your ass out here. >> Let's uh let's get to uh training camp." So yeah, >> uh early early risers. If you're a good news first type of person, this is this is perfect. We'll get into the good news. So give me give me some early risers for you guys during training camp. I got a list, Will, so I'll let you go first and I'll bounce back off of that. >> Okay. Well, yeah. I mean, I I wrote some names down here, too. I I will start with I think the player that everyone is rooting for, and that's Ahmed Hassan. And look, he is the o most open of all books. And so, when you get a chance to talk to Ahmed Hassan, you get not only his life story, but also a lot of really valuable insight into sort of how he is approaching the game this year versus last year and how he sees himself fitting in. And obviously he's made noise in the early stages of camp and and certainly with the two two PA practices, I think he's popped in both of those. And when I say he's making noise, literally he he he has a new routine of after making a positive play, flexing and roaring as loud as he can and oftentimes staring down the player that he just beat in a one-on-one rep, as he did a couple days ago in a special teams drill against tight end Thomas Gordon. And the way Thomas Gordon reacted so casually and unbothered made me realize that everyone is just used to Ahmed Hosin roaring after big plays. And um he has been in the back field a lot. I think in team drills and and he's getting pretty consistent second team reps now. He's he's had a knack for for tackles for loss for for getting at least to the quarterback and setting up sacks for others which he would tell you was just as valuable as a sack of his own. And it's notable here that he he's playing a different position this year in the Lions defense. And even more notably to me is the fact that he's playing the position that he played throughout his time at college at Boise State. He was the big end there, playing opposite what the Boise State defense called the stud end, which is more of the traditional rush end in the mold of say Hutch or Derek Moore or DJ Wanom. And that's what he was doing for most of last season. The Lions started him out last year as the big end, moved him pretty quickly to rush end. And so Amed spent most of his first season once he got healthy honing a new position, a a new part of his game. And I he also spent a lot of time watching film and studying guys like Hutch and other traditional rush ends past and present around the NFL. And you know, in some ways might have lost sight just a little bit of what he does best and who he is. And he said this year he's kind of back to to being himself. and he feels like his body type for one and his play style is suited to playing that hand in the dirt, do the dirty work, big end role. And and I think so far we're seeing some fruits from that labor. And look, we can maybe circle back to this name when we get to three slow starters, but you know, I don't think it's a stretch to say that Hosanine is is at least closing the gap if not on the level of Levi if you want to talk about big ends, potential big ends on this roster. And I I know they also see some interior value in Levi, but to me like Lacy clearly, Tyro Lacy, another fast starter, is clearly going to play a big role in this defense as the big end. But Hosanine is making a case to to be the number two in that department. And uh you know, he was walking off the field a couple days ago. Well, actually most days he seems to be walking off the field with Brad Holmes or finding Brad Holmes. And their conversation on Monday was uh a pretty sincere one where Hosanin actually teared up telling Brad how much he appreciates Brad, taking a chance on him, believing in him. And he told us yesterday, I think he told Colton the same thing when those two spoke a couple days ago that the response from Brad was awesome. And I want to make sure I get this right. So I'm going to pull up um the quote itself and the story I wrote today. But um so like you know Ahmed sitting there with tears in his eyes and and and just like stressing his desire to Brad to prove the Lions right to prove Holmes right. And uh he said Brad's response was um Ahmed you're proving me right by doing what you're doing and the big end role is going to be good for you. I'm excited for you. You're a football player. And Hassan told him he loves him because he loves everyone and Brad said I love you too. So, I know it's a long-winded answer, but I do think Justin, you probably agree that um we're seeing Hassan begin to climb the death chart in a pretty meaningful way because he's probably playing a role where he was he's more suited to play. >> Well, I can say this because I love you. All your answers are long-winded answers, my friend. [laughter] >> Uh yeah, Hos has been awesome. And I think more than than Levi, it's Payton Turner is gaining ground on, right? That that's a guy I I thought highly of through OTAAS. I go, "Okay, I get it. I see the body type. I see the vision." Same thing we said with Marcus Davenport. The concerns were the same as Marcus Davenport in terms of durability. Turner practices once, hurts his back, hasn't been back to practice since. And so that's opened the door for a guy like Hos. I look at Levi. Uh Levi's been working mostly as a three tech through OTAAS and even into training camp. He does do some of the big end stuff. It's like a almost like a reverse flex for him. But uh I mean that's that's an interesting conversation regardless because he's been doing a lot of third team stuff. So uh I will stick with the other big end though. Uh Tyler Lacy I think is maybe the biggest surprise of camp for me. Um kind of a an afterthought in a lot of ways. Um and I feel like I should explain what big end to is to people that maybe don't know what it is. Um, when the Lions are in a fiveman front, typically for rundowns, the big end lines up directly over the offensive tackle, it's called a five-te and then typically has a a more of a rush linebacker, your Derrick Barnes, your Trevor Noski to their outside shoulder. And so with with a Hosanine or a Lacy who's 300 lb, you know, the size almost of a defensive tackle, um, you know, allows them to lean into their their power. Uh, you still want some explosion there, but you want violent hands, the ability to shed. Hosanine's probably weakest skill is his bend. And so when you were mentioned, I I'd completely forgotten that he was playing Hutchinson's position and he was talking about mirroring Hutchinson last year. Like it's it's a ridiculous concept. >> Not going to happen. [laughter] >> That's that's not his strength, right? Like Oanine is a power player, so it just makes perfect sense that that's where they're putting him. But, uh, Lacy has been taking the first team reps at that big end spot, and he's basically in like a a rotation with DJ Wam. Wanom comes in on pass downs, a little bit wider, fourman fronts, smart player, instinctual player. You can understand why the Lions him, but Lacy has been a force in camp. He's uh done a lot of good stuff in one-on- ones. He's done a lot of good stuff in in team drills. He blowing up run plays the other day. Pressured Goff on a throwaway. pressure Teddy Bridgewwater on that long completion everybody wrote about the Dominic Love it. That was actually a Tyler Lacy sack. >> 100%. I'm glad you said that. [laughter] >> Yeah. And so like it's a guy that I probably didn't think a whole lot about, but it's it's weird with those guys that get claimed off waiverss right before the season opener because they just get dropped in and expect to acclimate right away and it's so difficult. Tyler Lacy like Thomas Harper has gotten this full off season with the team and really kind of got to tap into what they know about him now, what he knows about the scheme now. And uh I mean like if I created a 53man roster like right now Tyler Lacy is safe, like exceedingly safe. I don't want to say lock, but like very close to a lock. Um and so that's that's been a really interesting one. >> Agreed. Jeff, anyone popping in the the Twitter sphere as as far as fast starters, guys who are making an an early push for a starting job or even a job on the 53 that that people are talking about out there. I think the big one and it's more of a personal one for me because um my co-host Booner went to SPSU Nick Whiteside who also went to school with my co-host Boer and he's well aware and I Boer used to tell me all the time about him and be like this guy's a grinder you know like when he first was on the practice squad >> back at SPS this guy used to be in the gym late you know he used to have a key to the gym working out now I see him making plays I know we're going to talk about the quarterback two battle specifically >> but I think that's been the one people have been like oh like you know with the TA stuff And now people paying attention to corner and you have Nick Whiteside by the way part of Legion of Whom who last year started played really well against the Bucks. People forget about that too. But I think it's been um Nick Whiteside to be honest with you that people probably are paying attention to. I I know corner that corner two spot obviously has a lot of eyeballs but I think Nick Whiteside probably deservedly so based on the reporting I've been reading from you guys. Um he's been having a pretty good camp. >> Yeah. >> My man had four PBUs in that Tampa Bay game. I know they [laughter] list him for three, but he also had one on a two-point conversion that doesn't go on the stat sheet the same. Like that was >> a remarkable performance. The thing I really like about Whiteside, Will, >> it's it his personality, his demeanor is very similar to Rocky. Like it's just >> all business, very serious. Everything kind of rolls off his back and and >> like that's just such a great demeanor. like you you so frequently get these these flamboyant loud >> uh verbose corners like that's that's just the nature of of you have to have this almost projected confidence and like >> with Yin and and Whiteside it's like >> quiet killer right and uh the build is prototypical I mean it's what you love for the position he's 61ish he's got long limbs he's physical at the line of scrimmage he's physical down the field and Yeah, that leads to some some extra penalty flags in this league, but like just fits the Lions play style like a glove. And I don't I don't want to pretend like he's in the mix for the starter job. I know Dan Campbell said it the other day, but I think that's probably a stretch, but that's a guy that I think with with the Arnold news on top of it has played himself uh from maybe like fringe bubble to on the right side of the bubble as we kind of approach that second wave of training camp with the first preseason game coming up. >> Yeah, that that dude is just like laser focused on the next rep in front of him, a lot like Rocky Scene. And he's not going to say a whole lot even when he's playing well. In fact, when I asked him a couple days ago um about the fact that in my own words, say you're kind of balling out so far in camp, he said, "I wouldn't say balling out. I wouldn't say balling out at all. I'm just making a few plays here and there." Which kind of felt like talking to Rocky seen honestly. And if you had taken that same suggestion to someone like Terry Arnold, you would get you would get a much different response. You'd get the the prototypical corner response that Justin is talking about. But it's funny you you bring up that that Tampa game. That's sort of the flash point for everyone when talking about Whitide because he showed that in a big opportunity he could really thrive in the NFL against, by the way, great receivers that night. Like he was in a bunch of matchups one-on-one with Amika Ibuka and and he won most of those matchups. And when you bring it up to him, he's like he doesn't even want to talk about it. In fact, he says, "I got asked about this all the time by my parents, by my friends, my sister." And I'm like, "That's in the past." Like that that happened almost a year ago. It doesn't mean anything to anyone anymore. which is again is exactly the way the Lions want their players to be wired. But I agree, you know, that one of the big differences for Whiteside in camp this year is that he came in last year in his own words as a camp body. Like they they they they needed they needed people to play corner with a really thinned out secondary based on some camp injuries. And so they brought him in to be a body and they never really had intentions to keep him around and they didn't. They brought him back when they need to. He enters this year and this camp with a real chance to to win a job. And he also enters this year and this camp with an understanding of of Shephard's defense that he didn't have last year. And he said that's that's been the biggest reason that he feels like he's again not balling out but making a few plays in camp. And he said it's actually the first time in his professional career, the u even the the XFL included, where he's returned for a second season in the same defense. And that can go a really long way for a young player. And so I think we're seeing him um you know not just win matchups one-on-one but understand how the rest of the defense is operating around him where his health is where like how to play with leverage and um so far man Nick Whiteside is is definitely making a strong impression >> turned Tim Patrick into a camp body when he came in as a camp body's like this guy's out of here. Uh I those joint practices I remember like Dolphins writers are like, "Oh my god, we're when it comes down to cuts, like we're all writing that the Dolphins should claim this guy." Like he >> was killing it in those those early practices. And he he faded in preseason 4 and it cost him a job. I was really surprised it cost him a pre uh practice squad spot, but you know, he he dug in and and kind of refound himself mentally and I I think he's all the better for it. Before we move on, I I we haven't talked about it yet, but I I would I'm curious to get your guys' thoughts on maybe the the fit of the role. I know someone actually Kyle asked it in the chat because Rder got hurt. They signed Deon White and I know people see the name and they're like Devin White, you know, and it's really like what what does the role look like? You guys have gotten a chance to kind of see him out there. People heard from him. What's your guys' interpretation of maybe how Devin White fits or what an ideal role best case would be for a guy like Devin White? far away, Justin. >> First of all, super disappointing for Boulder. Uh I I thought he was um he was way ahead of I guess my personal expectations of where he would be. Uh, obviously the downhill stuff for him has always looked good on tape, but I I thought he was just kind of showing a pretty advanced understanding for a rookie of what he was being asked to do in all phases and and and tracking toward not necessarily a starting job, but I think a a sprinkling in defensive role as a rookie, which is maybe more than you probably anticipated. Um, Deon White comes in, Deon White benefits from that. Uh, you know, there was some reports or speculation that the Lions were going to bring in White anyway, but I think this kind of accelerated that. >> Um, >> not a camp body. So, it's we're taking care of him the proper way. Tank is handling his business the proper way. Everything is running really smooth. Colin is one of the rookies who's showing up almost every day. He finds a way to you know, get a get a get a get his hands on the ball in some type of fashion, right? Whether he's picking the ball, whether he's playing sticky coverage, and attacking the ball, getting PBU's. He's done a really great job of always, you know, showing that capability of being attached to the football. And that's a that's a good quality to have as a corner. So, he's done a really good job. >> A few days into pads, I mean, what do you kind of make of the offensive line? And is there a point in camp where you'd like to kind of see those five guys emerge as your best five? >> The five guys who will play that'll that'll we'll that'll hash itself out, right? Those guy what I've saw from my offensive line is I've seen physical play. I've seen guys finishing at the second level. And I've seen a huge improvement of our offensive line from where we've been, you know, in years past. So, I'm excited for that group. Excited to see, you know, we have probably the deepest group that we've had, you know, since I've been here as well. So, a lot of good depth, a lot of good players, guys you can move around at different spots. They're doing a really good job this camp. >> What do you feel What do you feel is so important to protect the team when it comes to the fans and the pictures and the videos? >> Well, it's important to protect the team, not just videos, but for us, you know, how we operate as a team. So, it's it's all about the team. So, if you're true Texans fan and you want to see the Texans succeed, you wouldn't showcase our plays to teams who don't know what we're running. >> rookie O-lineman San Hagen >> Say it again? >> Uh rookie O-lineman San Hagen >> do you see from him? >> Yeah, Sam is Sam has done a great job. We've moved Sam around from guard to tackle. He's played both spots and he's done a good job competing. Excited to see him go play in the games, but overall Sam has came in, he's worked hard every single day, done everything we asked him to do. >> Defensively, thank you guys. Defensively, you guys were pretty efficient stopping the run today. How were you guys able to do that on the offensive side? How do you feel about your your running backs with the running they've had here in the game? >> I feel good about our running game. I feel good about our run defense. >> What does Henry bring? >> What Henry brings to our defense, he brings his smart calmness to our defense. Right, he's always in position, always exactly where he should be. So, he's you can count on him, you can put a lot on his plate, he can handle things. He can play the Mike and the Will position. Very versatile guy and Henry plays with passion and fire. Man, that rubs off on the other guys. Like to see him play is fun to watch him play and you mix him in with a Z and Lassiter, got some wild and crazy guys running around who love to hit, love to play physical. But, Henry is a guy that I feel I can always count on. Like asking guys who are probably change up techniques, I'll put him in those situations where I may want to change some things. Henry is a guy who can take the coaching well and go apply it on the field and put himself in position to make plays for us. Higgins came back ready this camp. He came back ready, it showed in OTAs, it's showing now. It's not surprising. Him and CJ are finding a connection because Higgins is doing a really great job of running his routes the proper way. He's playing with precision and he's he's excelling at every level. Third down, he's winning, making plays for us. So, I mean, sky's the limit for Jayden Higgins because he's he's prepared himself the right way over the off season, and that's what he's a really great example for young guys. You prepare the off season the right way, you come to camp with the right mindset that you're going to get better, you can do that. And he's put the work in, and it's showing here in camp. Yeah, you guys saw the speech about the the NASA mission. That's So, I don't like getting videos in my my team meetings. So, that's probably the first one you guys saw. But, I I draw I can draw from a lot of different things. Our guys did a great job. I can draw from a lot of different places to just really tell the story to our guys. And And I try to make them think in different ways and try to correlate it to football as best I can. Try to find some parallel stories and and uh Artemis 2 and the preparation that it took for Artemis 2 to launch. Uh it took 3 years for that mission to take place. And that's the beauty of it. Uh you want to do things, you want to go places you've never been before, there's a lot of preparation in the background that a lot of people don't see. All right, that's the same I correlate that to football in the training camp. There's a lot of preparation, a lot of behind the scenes that goes on for us to prepare the launch. And we're not we don't launch tomorrow. You don't just get there just by talking about it. You got to put the work in. And that's the main message. That's the main goal and the message that I was trying to relate to our guys is how are you putting the work in? How are you getting yourself prepared to go? And you don't talk about it. You just put the work in every single day and when launch time comes, we don't have to be nervous about it. We don't have to be anxious. They seen we've had success over the past couple years and for me, I just I like to keep it real with guys. So it's I don't need a long drawn out conversation to try to convince guys to come to like, "Hey, what are you about?" title: Big step in Texans' Tank Dell comeback, Jayden Higgins, C.J. Stroud in sync, Lewis Bond excels
text: Hey guys, another step forward for Texans wide receiver Tank Dell. Incremental progress, but progress nonetheless. He participated in individual drills in full pads for the first time being full pads since he tore up his knee December 2024 Arrowhead Stadium while catching a touchdown pass against the Kansas City Chiefs. That's when his knee exploded. Dislocated knee, the torn ACL, MCL, LCL, two surgeries performed by Dr. Walter Lowe, and now starting to see some of the fruits of his labor where Tank is out there catching passes including a catch today from CJ Stroud throwing him the football delivering it to him. And he looked pretty good in the individual drills. They did not have him do the one-on-one drills, which is a time where yes, he could be exposed to contact jostling possibly falling when you're leaping and diving for catches. And that's a real fine point, a real delineation between being really back and being kind of back. He's kind of back. So none of it to me forecast necessarily that he's going to be ready for the first game. But at some point this season, I believe they will try it and try to get him back out there and see what he can do. But he could obviously give this offense a real shot in the arm to have that target and you know, he's explosive, he's dynamic, he's got the muscle memory, he's still a good route runner, and that's the real strength of his game. When I think about Tank, it's about having him out there when he can stay out there, and that's been the message throughout. As DeMeco Ryans outlined today, this has been all part of a plan and they carefully designed it to try to protect Tank. It's not necessarily about protecting Tank from Tank. Sometimes it can be, but I think also like he's been on the same page realizing if he dislocates his knee or tears up his knee again, this could end his career. So, when he gets back out there, he's got to stay out there. And to me, it's a situation of you know, just being patient, staying the course, because at some point, you know, he's going to get the opportunity and he'll be ready for it. But, it's just a matter of his medical health and just being very cautious with it. And I think that today was a important step, but not the final step in his recovery from such a devastating knee injury that definitely endangered his career, but medical science is amazing what they can do now with the procedures, with the science, with the surgeries, and his rehab, and he's worked so hard. So, this was a nice moment for Tank. And you know, it is emotional for anyone that has been around him, watching him. You want to see him do well. So, uh good for Tank. That's a a cool step for him. We'll go through some of my other observations and thoughts on camp, but first some news. Texans running back British Brooks, a special teams hammer, and a good versatile guy that can play full back and run the football when needed and block, he has broken his hand and he had surgery yesterday. He's out for 3 weeks, I'm told. So, per sources, this is going to be a short-term injury, but nonetheless, he did break his hand. And so, British Brooks is out for now. So, looks like this would end his preseason. The hope is to get him back for the first game. Jake Hanson update on his ankle injury. They still feel like there's a chance he could be ready for the first game against the Buffalo Bills. So, touch and go on that. Just it is for British Brooks. Special teams taking some hits here. So, uh for Frank Ross's units, cuz most of those guys are very important to that. A rest day for Nico Collins, which is smart. He's done a lot of reps. He's had a great camp so far, but they felt like it was time to give him a couple days off in a row. So, tomorrow, Thursday, the Texans are off and we're not off. I'm not off, but the Texans have a day off from practice and then they'll resume Friday and then Saturday night under the lights, the night practice for the Texans. Segwaying and sticking with the theme of the offense, Jayden Higgins, as recognized by DeMeco Ryans is in a better level of chemistry and comfort zone with C.J. Stroud. The time that they've worked together, they have now achieved something where there's some good timing and chemistry and we're seeing it out here on the practice field with touchdown passes, with good timing on the passes in terms of how he breaks, knowing where he wants the football. He's a real big target. He's 6'4". They've got twin towers with Higgins and Stroud, I'm sorry, Higgins and Nico for Stroud to throw to. So, I look at it like this. If Higgins takes this leap after six touchdowns as a rookie, what if he becomes a 1,000-yard receiver like Nico? What if this offense truly becomes a formidable passing game with multi-faceted receivers? Higgins can line up outside or inside. They'll get back John Metchie at some point. He gives them that vertical slot presence and of course he's 4.39, he's very fast and his pinky's getting better. I can report that. Right pinky injury, making progress and I don't think it's going to be that long before we see John Metchie. He does work out on the side and seems to be comfortable enough. He's not wearing a cast or a splinter or anything like that. So, with the Texans and the offensive line, not a a of push today in the run game. I thought it was difficult for them, some tough sledding. Uh other than a Woody Marks run, it was really good, but overall wasn't a lot of great long runs or anything like that, but it was still you know, I would say some tough sledding for them against this top-ranked defense. Uh we'll stick with offense, and then we'll take a break, and I'll give you some videos from guys from footage of Tank, of practice, and DeMeco Ryans, and then we'll talk defense. So, in terms of other things on offense, Braden Smith looks like his neck is feeling better, and now him and Trent Brown are duking it out for the right tackle job. I still think that with the investment they've made in Smith, that he's the likely projected starter, but they have a lot of respect for Trent. They don't lose when Trent's in the lineup. They lost that playoff game, I think, partially because Trent wasn't able to play because of injuries. And he's healthy and in good shape this year. I had a good conversation with Wyatt Teller. I'm going to bring that to you in its entirety. Can't wait to share the insights of Wyatt Teller. I can say this, he is very, very encouraged by the state of the offense, very happy he signed with the Texans, and him and his family, they love it here. Okay, Keaton Rutledge, the frontrunner, and I think it would be an upset at this point if he didn't win the starting job at center. Uh the rookie has aggression, he has mentality, he has grit, and we universally the same talk about Keaton Rutledge and what he can do, what he brings to the table. Just a very tough, old-school football player, who's also a good athlete. I like what I've seen from him so far, and I think that he's going to give a boost in their you know, Teller made a good point. It's not like they were a bad offensive line before, but I think what they're doing now, it's different. I see the difference after watching this team for now 12 years, and I feel like the offensive line that they can impose their will a little bit. It's still tough against the top ranked defense, never easy. Uh but I thought C.J. Stroud threw the football very well today. Xavier Hutchinson should be okay. He like strained his lower back a little bit, but then he got back out there. Um Lewis Bond had a touchdown catch beating Jalen Pitre. Good play by him. Still seeing some good push from O'Betche Waehwu with the second team. Uh not a starter. I'm saying Ingram's the guy and that's on the depth chart. I know you've taken it up lately. I'm like I'm surprised that I made it through with the same golf set uh throughout this whole offseason. I'm like well there's plenty of times I definitely wanted to snap that club in half after I lost my eighth ball and we're on a whole four. But um [laughter] um I think yeah that's been something it's very I think uh very similar like you got to play each play. And I think sometimes DBs can feel very up and down because so much of their game is based on that guessing game. And then whether or not you throw one hand as just a stab to just kind of like absorb his momentum a little bit and you know get a hand on him just to feel him or are you going with a full two-hand jam which is really aggressive or you not jamming at all because you're just trying to keep your balance and you don't want to um you know overcommit because you got to turn and run because this guy's super fast. Like what are you doing, right? What's your context? How where's your help? Who are you playing to? And all that stuff is really interesting. So with DBs where you don't have where with DB wide receiver one-on- ones where you don't have any of that stuff, you have no context for why you should make one decision or the other. And so the DB is going to make that decision maybe arbitrarily, but in in our world where we're in the NFL and every detail is super crucial, or are they pretending, right? Are they making up a simulation? I'm going to play this one like it's third and 10. I'm going to play this one like it's actually third and goal from the two. And I and I got to play it this way. Or first and 10, first play of the third quarter. Right? Like all super different situations. And how we're how I'm how I'm going to do that. I'm going to play this like I'm in cover two or I'm going to play this one like I'm in palms. So I'm I've got I'm going to have his vertical route, but I've got to play a certain angle because it's like a different situation that I'm in. Or or I'm in cover three. So I'm actually going to bail on this one and I'm going to do that. And I don't know how you would organize that at the NFL level. I I would be fascinated to know from like a DB's coach how they're organizing that or are they just saying, "Eh, vibe it out, play what you want. We're just going to be man coverage. Pretend it's cover one all day long. What are we doing?" I I would be fascinated for what strategies and thoughts go into that because every rep is super precious in an NFL training camp. You only get so many of them and trying to to to extract the most value out of them is the name of the game this time of year. I kind of talked in circles. I don't really have a conclusion off of that, but I do think it's really interesting to think about just the release and then from there, you know, what you do with your hands and then once you're running with them in phase or out of phase, the rest of the route is the die is kind of cast. I do think a lot of these one-on- ones are decided in the first few steps and then you're either in phase or out of phase. And if you're in phase, you're on them. You know, you turn your head with the right time. You try to get the ball. If you're out of phase, you probably can't turn your head and you got to go play the play the guy's arms when his when he goes up for the catch. You got to try to, you know, play the ball that way. But either way, it's an interesting little game within the game. So, if you're going to watch the wide receiver DB one-on ones, maybe I've given you something a little extra to chew on. Uh, for better or worse, I will talk to you all tomorrow. And as always, let's go.

title: Garrett Wilson & Demario Davis Break Down the Energy at Jets Training Camp
text: You're watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen here with Quincy and Nuna and one of today's stars, Garrett Wilson. So, I got a question for you out of the gate. First two practices, no catches in team periods. Did you tell Gino, get me the ball [laughter] right away? >> Nothing like that, man. I, you know, uh, Gino the type of guy where he feel it. You don't need to say nothing to him, right? So, I trust the process. You know, I'm at the point now. I'm trusting the process. when it comes my way, I'm going try and, you know, just make the play. But, uh, we in practice right now. Let's let's all build our trust, our our, uh, you know, just spread the ball around. I love it. So, it's been a, uh, start to camp. >> Gino's no domin first two plays and then Garrett gets the first touchdown of the day. Gino today 111 and team drills four touchdown passes. >> Felt like it. It felt like it. No, that's hearing the numbers. That's crazy, bro. It felt like it. >> No, very active day for you. So I guess my question right coming in I always want to know it from the receiver perspective what were you thinking about coming in like what was something you were like coming off of injury this is what I want to work on nothing else this year. >> Yeah I mean honestly just getting back used to that that playing through contact playing with the DB trying to get a press on you right and and there's a little aspect there that takes you going out and doing it that is harder to mimic when you are dealing with an injury. So, I I wasn't able to exactly work that the way I would have wanted in the offseason and not to mention it it made the break between my last time doing that a lot longer. You know what I'm saying? So, just getting back used to that that playing level of uh contact and and still being able to get into your routes, come out your breaks clean and um you know, I feel like I'm getting there. I'm feeling good. >> Definitely. I saw actually your first catch was actually an out route. We won't talk about who the DB was. We're going to keep that under wraps, [laughter] but I saw you run on the sideline. A lot of contact at the top of the route, but you broke off. It was a good route by you. Yeah, definitely. Um, we talked to you in the spring. We felt your positivity, your passion for the game. You said the other day here when you were talking to the media that it feels different. Can you elaborate a little bit on that? >> I mean, this this energy I hope the fans and y'all being out here today could kind of feel just the the intention that we're having out there on practice at practice. Um, that the the talent level of the team and just from we're I feel like we're deep, man. It it just feels it's a good group to be a part of. I'm happy to be a part of it and and and it just all of us are taking it off each other's shoulders, right? So, when that ball does come your way, it's like, "Oh, this my this my chance right here. Let's go make it." It takes the pressure off, right? So, I feel like just knowing exactly what AG wants out of us. Um getting to know Coach Reich and and the way he asks us to run offense, run our routes, it's pretty friendly to, you know, the mo the way most receivers think. And I and I think that can't be glanced over either. There's just a different level of intention and energy that I feel out here on the field and and hopefully the fans got to get a little taste of that today. >> Can you take us through your touchdown catch from your perspective? And also I wanted to ask you about AD's crosser because I thought maybe Gina was looking for you and AD stepped in front and he got it. >> No, no doubt. Um yeah, so that so that touchdown I think I was on a corner route and and you know it uh quarterback tried to get a collision, right? So, I ended up getting getting inside off my release knowing I got a flat route that's going to pull that corner, hopefully pull him down, but hopefully just get him a little wider. Maybe I'm expecting the ball right on my back shoulder when it's cover two. It ended up being he fully took the flat and and Gino just got it up early, made it easy on me, get the ball, you know, get down and let's make sure we don't take a hit and let's ride, you know, celebrate with your teammates. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. Go. No, go ahead. Go ahead. >> You talked a little bit about AD. Um I remember um Bree saying a lot in the media that you and him like to compete who's going to be the best player. Is that what's going on inside the receiver room too? Are you guys competing like who's going to be the best receiver? >> I mean that's just that's just how receivers are wired and you always want to want to make that next play and and and once you know we take a lot of pride in as me adim uh Omar like we got to start this practice the right way. We got to we got to show the young guys what the energy is going to look like for today and set the plate set the uh set the tempo. That's what you take on when you become a, you know, top-notch receiver. And AD's on that level, man. And I I love watching him go out there and make his plays and and uh he usually starts the day off with a banger. And I got to catch up, right? So, so I think it was just my turn today to get it first. And then we know what AD is going to do. >> I was kidding with you a little bit because I think there was only 24 team reps the first two practices and we knew you were going to get your share. It was just a matter of time. How about the young tight end Kenyan Sadique, >> number 16 overall pick. He got a touchdown as well. What have you seen from him early and how can guys like Sadique and Cooper help the entire offense as far as spacing is concerned? >> Yeah, I mean the speed that that a guy of that size has and and um the way Frank in his head can can visualize ways to use him, right? And and I'm sure as as uh time goes on, they'll keep building new ways to use him, new ways to get him downfield or out getting just the ball cuz cuz he's special. Kenan that is. And then Omar the same way. He's he's just getting his foot in, right? And and we do got a lot of guys to spread the ball around to. So, I think just every catch it's like, oh, Omar getting that getting that foot in, feeling more comfortable um doing that. Like today, he he caught the ball and made a move, almost made made the linebacker miss and lost his footing a little bit, but you could see that he's just getting that that comfortability and level, knowing where guys going to be. And I love to watch it. So, um yeah, man. It it it's it's truly for me now like being in year five and just knowing and have been through some of these things at the start and not knowing how they want to want to use you but but just working through it and getting better every day and I see that from those two. So I'm I'm excited. Man, >> you talked about the leadership council the other day. Has this all went fast? Did three seasons of 80 plus catches, 1,000 yards receiving. We know what happened last season. Um, anybody who's watched you knows how extremely durable you are and as far as fantasy owners are concerned. Hey, watch out for this dude. Um, but can you believe it that you're out here and it's the start of the fifth camp already? >> No, man. I can't. I can't. And I'm just not trying to take any of it for granted. Making sure every day I look around, look at the trees, look at look at the people I get to work with, you know, take it all in cuz uh it's flying, you know. It's flying. And I am biased. I think it's going to be special. you know, this is gonna be the year. So, I'm just pumped to get out there and and get to work. But this this start of the camp, I've been taking it all in and and um Yeah, man. It's all getting away from me. It's crazy. >> No, you're not even in your prime yet. I don't think >> I appreciate that. >> So, I know it intentions as far as the end of practice. Some guys might want to go in, get in the cold tub, get the regen going. This is the only public practice day out here. You stood out and signed everybody's autograph and took photos well after practice. How much do these fans mean to you? >> A lot, man. Everything. You know, it's uh I always say they're always, "Oh, you so nice to the fan, man. They treat me with the most the utmost uh just since day one, the most love and and support." And um I just want them to know it doesn't go unnoticed. I appreciate it. You know, I don't love to be on social media responding to it all the time or or maybe liking it, but but that don't mean I don't see it. You know, that's my way of of telling the fans I appreciate y'all and and um you know, we owe them one. That's the reality of this thing. These these dudes are they loyalty never in question. They they faith and uh they belief is not in question and it's our job. You know, it's on us to go make right on it. So, I take a lot of pride in that for sure. >> Two quick ones and then we're going to get you out. Gino, now that you're three days into camp, we talked to you throughout the spring. You practiced with him throughout the spring, but what's standing out on the field? >> Just just how fast his his mind moves and the way we can talk about it after he's uh so cerebral. I remember telling y'all like he he the first day when he had tell us the the cadences and he went through it and and uh I was like, "Bro, did you bring that with you from from Oakland and Seattle?" And he was like, "No, that's that's Coach Reich stuff. I just had learned it last night." And that's when I knew. So he he's he's just so cerebral, processes so fast and and um like I said like they kind of misststepped on that corner route to start the practice and he he balls up two ball fell on like you know take the safety out of the play stuff like that. You don't you don't take that for you know not everybody could do that. That's that's Gino man and and we're all excited to to play with him cuz we all going to have a shot to make some plays and it's exciting. >> We're not scoring at home but I'll tell you this five receptions in team a touchdown. He set the tone for a red hot day for the offense. That's Garrett Wilson. And by the way, I wanted to tell you, I looked in the stands today. By my count, by a wide margin, more fives than [laughter] anything else. >> Thanks, Garrett. >> No, that's cool to see, man. I appreciate y'all having me on. Good to see you, man. Appreciate you. >> You're watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda, Eric Allen, Bart Scott, and Deario Davis. Don't call it a comeback. Everybody's reunited here. >> Let's go. Take three. And it feels so good, man. I [laughter] tell you what. >> Reunited. Yeah, let's do it. Um, what was it like putting the pads on for the first time in camp? >> Oh man, it's awesome. Um, you know, the first day of camp is always everybody's on edge, everybody's ready to go and then it's that next day where everybody's in paths for the first time where everybody's a little jittery and our coach uh just told us don't let the details go to the wayside just because the pads are on. And so, you know, everybody kind of got that angst. Um, but you get that out the way, get you a couple licks in and then you know, okay, we back to playing football. I was talking to Minka, he got an interception. I was like, hey man, I was giving him a hard time. Like, by the time you showed up, he's like, "We finally playing football again." And not not playing, you know, tag. So, that was cool. >> Who's that guy that you guys kind of been waiting for, you know? We know when we got the the shorts on in the Olympics. like, "All right, it's a different ball game when you put these pads on. You going to have to have those like physical, you know, those physical consequences from some of all this stuff you've been doing when we were in shorts." >> You know what? I got a ton of respect for our offense. Um, Frank has came in and put in a good regime. Gino is keeping everybody on pace. Um, and then the the younger quarterbacks are doing the same thing. Uh, but we got three tight ends that can come in and give you different things. You got Ruck, very physical um, at the point of attack and in his routes. You got Mason who can do a little bit of everything. And then you got Sadique who can take you vertical downfield. So that little element of change up for linebackers is tough because they go 13 and 12 a lot. [snorts] >> And then you got, you know, two to three running backs in Bree and Brilen and Isaiah. And so just that dynamic of the game is naturally physical. So you you kind of anticipate it when you going seven on and when you going kind of tag, but when you get the pass on, you can really feel, oh, this element of offense going to have something to it. Um, mixed with an offensive line that has had time to play together in jail. So, uh, it's it's a very physical practice. >> I know it's practice. You're in your 15th year, but the offense had >> you can't just gloss over 15. How does that feel? 15 years. Like, what keep I'm sorry, EA. What keep what what keep what keeps you motivated? What keeps you going? You know, 15. We always know that it's not the games that's hard to prepare for. It's the mental preparation and anxiety and the fatigue that comes from doing something that you've done over and over and over again. Well, I think the beauty of this game is we all get a chance to carry the baton from one generation to the next. You know, it's like >> it's almost like two different lifetimes inside the sport. When I came in, I had guys like you, Dave Harris, Antonio Kardi, Derel Rivas, you guys were passing the baton to me. I was looking up like, man, I just want to be what those guys are doing. I remember my first couple practices, you like, hey, when they run ISO, you got to go blow that MF up. You, you know, that's how you And it was like, oh, okay, I see what it's like. And so you showed me how to play the game as an inside linebacker and be that enforcer. And I learned that and I took it and I took a little bit from everybody to Brick Shaw Ferguson being a pro. And now I was able to put that into my game and build a career. And now I'm able to come back to a locker room that's very familiar to me and do the same thing for other guys. So yeah, I'm still wanting to play at a high level, but it's even more important for me to make sure that I'm pulling a young guy to the side say, "Hey, this is the way you want to go if you're trying to build a career." 15th year. Like I was saying, first day in pads. The offense had a pretty good day on Saturday as far as red zone is concerned. Do you tell the guys in the room, hey, first day of pads, contact, we really can get after them. Let's set the tone here on Monday. >> Well, I'm a big believer in what's understood don't have to be explained. And coach uh Aaron Glenn and Moo and the front office did a great job of bringing the right type of guys into the building. And you can see that. So, a lot of that stuff doesn't have to be explained. The offense had a great practice the day before our off day in the red zone, scored touchdowns. We wanted to protect the house and we didn't do a good job of that. Um, but nobody had to say anything about responding. I mean, you got a great lead up front. Harrison uh Phillips came out from the from the uh uh the beginning saying, "Hey, let's set the tone. We know what today got to be in pass." Mink Fitzpatrick getting a pick in the first drill. Guys already know what we have to do. And that respond is there. And that's the type of team that we got because even when the day was over, Gino was coming up to me saying, "Hey, y'all got today, but we gonna respond tomorrow." So, it's just an environment that's being built the right way because we're trying to build a culture of winning and that starts in how you practice and how you respond, especially at the adverse day. You know, it was crazy at the end of practice, I saw that AG kind of stayed back. And I think, you know, my interpretation of that is that he's trying to have a team in a locker room that's led by their their leaders and their peers. And what type of pressure does that put on the person that decides to step in the middle of that circle, you know, to make sure that they live not only by their words, but they have to live by example as well? >> Well, I think it's just a assembly of guys that's that's being built around the organization, not just players. That's that's coaches included. Uh bringing in Frank, bringing in Duke, Coach Banjo, top special team coach in the league last year. And that was coach Banjo who broke down the huddle. So I think it's a culture of coaches, of players, of staff members, uh from uh Eric and Corey in the wait room um to our our media team. I think it's everybody going in one direction and you can feel it. You can feel that energy uh is contagious and everybody pushing upstream. And I think that's what leadership is. It's everybody modeling what it means to go upstream in their lane. >> Bert was talking about Banjo. You mentioned special teams. >> First of all, first of all, I never I never seen a coach out there with shea butter on before practice, man. I he was looking real greased up, man. >> Listen, Banjo could give you a couple snaps right now. And those special teams were elite last season. Yeah, no doubt about that. Um, MA, you knew he was a great player. This is the first time you guys are teammates. anything surprising you out there or is like he he exactly what you thought he was going to be? >> I mean, I didn't I didn't know uh Minka before I got here. I had only knew about him as a player. You know, his name is, you know, around the league as being a phenomenal safety. Um but guys who played with him, I asked him about him and they said, "Man, he's always on football. Like you going to find him in the building all the time." And then that's that's literally the case. Uh I'm very similar in that demeanor and so every time I'm in the building I see him and uh every time I'm leaving the building I see him and that's that's how he is. Uh we were able to train together in the offseason and we've gotten a chance to uh grow closer in our relationship. Um our significant others get a chance to spend time together. Our kids are getting a chance to connect. And so building that relationship off the field is just as important on the field. Um because you think about that dynamic when you playing with a linebacker and a safety. I always think about um you know Ray Lewis and Ed Reid. That tandem is so much communication and so much in sync. Those two got to be on the same occur. Um and so getting a chance to spend that time and grow with him as a player. I mean it's it's you know it's well known who he is on the field. Um but off the field he's he's equally or more impressive. >> Yeah. I think you speaking about the why, right? And that's kind of where we at when you're trying to cultivate a a culture. It's about understanding your teammates and the why. Not everybody can be motivated and pushed the same way. You know, how are you guys, you know, coming together, whether it was the OTAAS, competition, but also kind of going across the aisle and learning about the guys on the other side, right? Like you said, your counterpart would probably be Gino. Uh you guys both are in your second stint. How are you guys going about trying to cultivate that and come together, right? Because what people don't realize is the most important part about camp in my opinion isn't what you do on the field, it's what happens off the field. and you spoke about what you and Minka are doing, but how are you trying to come together with all your group of leaders to do that for the entire team? Well, I think very early on um there was a select group of guys that were brought together on both side of the aisles as hey you guys are the culture bearsers and the standards of the team and we've been meeting since uh phase one you know and we had 100% part participation in phase one and so we were meeting and connecting at that time and that essentially had somebody from each position group so that type of connection is already there but what was even more impressive you know how I've always been I've always been a guy who was started Bible study or men's group on the team. That's just how I roll. And I I've never been on a team that had that, especially with 25 dudes on a regular. We were even in the time that we were away over the four weeks, we were getting on a Zoom call and guys were were tapping in and that's guys on both sides of the ball. Gino's been a big part of that as well. Um and so uh I think that type of uh connection and accountability is there and we we know what the standard is for us and we setting that and we checking each other on that every day. My argument from the get-go was after the Jets brought you back, run defense is going to be better immediately. Can you talk about this unit being built from the inside out? You mentioned Harrison Phillips before David Anya, a former teammate who you called one of the top run five run stuffers you've ever played with. Devandre Sweat hopefully going to be on the practice field soon as well. You got big Daryl Jackson, the rookie, but then behind you a guy like Minka as well. So the strength of this defense. Can you speak about the middle and also what you're going to see from the unit run defensively? >> Yeah, I think to for any great defense, this goes all the way back when I came in the league, any great run defense, I mean any great defense has to have phenomenal run defense. Um that's just foundational. And I I think it begins before you get good players, you got to have good coaching as well. So having Carl Dunar up front is is phenomenal. You know, he's done it across the league for a very very long time. having coach Ben with the LBs, he got a chance to do it at a high level in Houston and been able to bring a lot of that swag and energy uh over with us. But then you talk about the guys inside out. I think we haven't even had T Sweat out there with us yet and we know what type of monster he is. Um but you know, Harrison in the middle, Joan Briggs, David Onyum, those guys are setting the tone, playing with great hands, great feet. Like I said, the way coach Dunar has taught it consistently, you can see it showing up on the field. Um, you kind of got Kingsley on the outside, Will McDonald on the outside. They setting the edge and I was I was kind of laughing today because a good edge is like a firm foundation. You can build a defense on that. If you got a good edge, you know, somebody who can set the edge and make the run, come back inside, then you got it. And then I think from the linebacker level, we're we're just taught to kind of keep the ball in between us and be able to make plays in both gaps. And we got enough athletic linebackers to do that. I'm really excited. Over the past two years, Sherwood, I think, is like second or third in the league in tackles. So, I'm excited to play next to a a super athletic linebacker like him. Um whether he turn the ball back to me, I'm turning it back to him if it's anything to eat with the D line and the way they hunting up front. And so, um our goal is not to let it get to the DBs, but we do know that we got defensive backs that can tackle. >> Yeah, one of the early uh plays in practice today was you getting into the backfield and stopping Breeze. That was right after I think Ma's interception in the first team period. Yeah. I just feel like when you got a good defensive line, you have to go faster to the ball because it ain't going to be nothing to eat. [laughter] >> Now, when you talk about Sherwood and you know, one of the most intimate relationships you have is your partner right next to you and kind of getting that chemistry because not all things go as according to plan at times, you know, that nonverbal communication, being interchangeable, being able to say, "Okay, when the motion goes here, we don't have to flip-flop. I trust that you can do my job and I can do yours." How is that relationship going as you guys continue to now you're going to be put in live situations where you can communicate and talk things out so when you see him on the field you kind of get to understand each other know each other like inside and out and kind of know what each other's thinking before without having to physically communicate it. >> Man I uh I talked about this uh before but I'm really proud of my linebacker tree. Now, I'm I'm a product of you and Dave's uh linebacker tree, but my linebacker tree exists of Alex Analone, Kate Nellis, Zack Bond, Quan Alexander, Christian Kirsy. Like, I've played with some guys besides some guys who who've had phenomenal careers and in my top five reasons of coming back to New York was to play next to Jamie Sherwood. I'm really excited to play against. He may be one of the most athletic linebackers I've played beside, and that's that's saying a lot. Um he's just he has range, um long arms, not afraid of contact, he is super smart, and he loves football. Um so he has all the all the pieces and he's been very productive. As I said, one of the over the past two years, um he's like second in the league or third in the league in tackles, so he he finds the football. Um and so those are all the mixes. And so if anything I can help add to his game to help him take that next step, um then I'll be doing my job well. But I'm really excited to play about him and um everything that I've seen to this point has been what I was expected or more. >> Your relationship with Aaron Glenn well documented. What's it going to be like now that he's the defensive signal caller? You're the mic linebacker. You're the green dot. So he's sending you what he wants called out there on the field. So you have to be his eyes from that point forward. >> Yeah. Um, I think if anything with him calling the plays and and being there with us, it just creates clarity. Um, as a as a football player, defensive football player, tell me where to put my eyes and tell me where I'm supposed to stand and then let me play. At that point, you got to trust that you put me in this position for a reason. And I think he has all those elements. He's going to let us know exactly where we're supposed to be looking, exactly where we supposed to be standing, but he also goes another level and teaches us what's the technique to doing the job. And then from there, he lets us be football players. And I think that consistency on every single level after practices and and it's streamlined from him to the coaches to the players. Um when he's not in the meetings and coach Duke is in there calling it, there's notes for the Dline for the whole team to see. There's notes for the linebackers for the whole team to see, there's notes for the safeties and the corners. So everybody can see clearly exactly what the job is and what it's supposed to be. Um and the way that we practice is built into the way that we practice. So, um, I think more than anything, it it creates clarity for our defense and and that takes you a lot a long way, >> you know, going out to practice today. I mean, I would call it the microwave practice, right? Because I remember being out there with the Junction Boys. Football used to be totally different as far as the workload that you put in. How do you make the adjustment physically to be ready to to to play and tackle and take guys down without being able to actually physically do it or not have to do it? How are you making that adjustment? And how do you teach those young guys that you may not have the opportunities to take guys down in practice, but you have to practice you and have the same technique that you're that you need to have like you're trying to take them down. >> Yeah. I would just say that the reason why I'm able to play at year 15 at a high level is because of the way the game is wired now. It's a different game than when I even first came in where it was much a grind. it was grind is how you get better where now it's much more uh work efficiently and you putting in the same amount of work but it's more efficient and so uh we don't want to overuse certain muscle groups to where you wore down and that science allows you to know that ahead of time and um our strength and conditioning uh team uh Eric and Cory Cory they're phenomenal um even in the way that we were training in the off season in OTAAS and mini camp was to get us ready for training camp And the way that we're practicing in training camp is to get ready for the season. And there's a ramp up period in the practices and they've already let us know. Some days we have sprints after practice, but it's all scientifically measured, but it's also them constantly coming and check with us and see how you feeling. So if guys, you know, if the sign says one thing, but guys are feeling better, they might get a little bit more. If guys feeling worse, they might get a little bit less.
