title: Dillon Radunz talks Saints run game | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: How do you like camp going so far? >> Uh uh good. Um yeah, it's it's uh joking around the old line room. It's like you're banging the rust off those first few days, you know. Uh especially in pads and whatnot. It's like uh once you finally get those first three under your belt, you're like, "All right, we're getting into the rhythm of things." Getting the getting the technique back down and uh yeah, obviously it was a hot one today, so you you really uh find out what you're made of uh on days like today and uh yeah, we're starting to get in those dog days of camp and uh it's it's time to grow and time to flourish in these days, so. >> What's some of the differences you notice in the run game with Travis's arrival, David's arrival, and then also just like the general coaching staff kind of narrowing down what you guys are >> For sure. Uh obviously what we were like 31st in the run game last year, so it was just unacceptable. So, that's a huge focus for us obviously going into this camp. Um so, yeah, everything uh all attention to details uh during this camp uh are going to be huge. Uh we're going to notice a lot of changes cuz obviously that's where our attention's at and uh uh yeah, with the arrival of Dave uh I mean, just the techniques that he's used to bringing, uh obviously we're going to throw the kitchen sink at it cuz 31st is not acceptable and we're going to grow from that. And uh yeah, having Kamara and H N uh both back there, I mean, we're going to be able to run the ball a lot cuz uh when I mean, we're going to have a lot of gas in the gas tank with those two, so. >> Picking up that running back room, uh just what's your take on >> Uh I think it's it's a blessing. I mean, like I said, cuz it's like if you want to run the ball four or five times in a row, if you're gaining yards, you can because you got two backs who can do it. Um I believe both of them are uh elite pass catchers, whether that's in the screen game or whenever we need them on hot routes or anything like that, so uh having two guys can that can do it at that high of a level, I mean, it's just an added weapon and defenses are going to have to watch out for that. >> Are there any differences between the guys? Are there differences between um Alvin and Travis as rushers? And and how can those differences like actually kind of be a benefit to to you guys and like keeping defenses or yeah, defenses off guard? >> Um I'm no expert uh running back scout uh but obviously I'm I mean Al Alvin's got that balance. I mean you've seen it every time like he gets hit and it feels like he's not even moving um stuff like that that balance in the run game as a pass catcher. Um, so whether that you call that finesse and then A-Chan I mean I feel like he's got that too. Um, and they both have crazy instincts so honestly they're they both have their strong suits. I couldn't pinpoint whether or not one of them's better in one area than the other but I feel like they're both interchangeable and whichever one's in there we're going to call the right play for it and it's we have a chance at scoring a touchdown every time they're in the game so >> Despite the biased question but who do you think is the better back there? >> Oh gosh. >> And if you were to block for who's the fastest? >> The fastest? uh >> in your opinion >> Right. The fastest to block for so far in my career I mean Kamara for sure but it's hard to for me I played in Tennessee with Derrick Henry so I mean you fall forward you fall forward and you gain 5 yards with him. I mean he's a massive back but obviously those are two different styles of play. I can appreciate both of them. I mean getting out on a screen with Alvin Kamara I mean you're basically guaranteed to gain a whole bunch of yards and like I said and then just running outside zone with Derrick Henry I mean there's a treat to that. You just fall forward and you're going to gain 5 yards so I mean there's perks to both. I've I've enjoyed blocking for both. I'm honestly blessed to block for potentially two future Hall of Famers so it's it's been great. >> What was What was your off season process like this year? Like what what were you up to? Did you kind of change anything about your training and what not anything? >> Um, I mean more just get stronger every off season you always try to get stronger try to get in shape get used to this weather obviously I hit free agency so I didn't know exactly if I was going to be here so I trained here till I couldn't and then went training elsewhere and then we I mean we got it done the deal done the week week and a half into training and came back here so in Ted Rath I trusted and yeah, he's he's got us a good off-season program and I felt like I've come back stronger and in better shape than I ever have. We ran that conditioning test and I felt great, so yeah, it was nothing crazy, just trusting Ted Rath and trying to get used to this heat cuz it is it is very hot. >> Pretty much at right guard since being back. Is that an area they identified that like all right, we want you to play right and then play left last year or is it just kind of how it shook out? >> For sure. I mean it's kind of how it shakes out. I mean obviously you sign a guy for 16 million to play left guard. Yeah, unless he gets hurt well I'm not playing left guard. That's just the fact of the matter. That's the nature of the NFL. So yeah, I mean it's just a matter of I played all year at left last year, so hey, go get used to right. If you're going to be our swing guy, we're going to need you to play both, so you would just played left all year last year, so now go get used to right and so that's kind of the mindset I'm going into and wherever they need me, that's where I'm going to play, so. >> David I would say he actually likes being a swing guy. Have you ever heard anybody say that? >> That's crazy. I think he might have been hallucinating. Maybe he didn't get enough water after practice. Uh In the winter maybe, yeah, sure. The heat in the winter when it's 75 and beautiful on Christmas, but right now I don't know how anybody could like this. >> And then that's crazy cuz you got three North Dakota State guys on the Minnesota Vikings. >> Yeah, this is crazy. I mean even last year I'm thinking Missouri Valley Conference guys. I mean with Ridgeway, KB, we had Trevor Penning last year, Isaiah Stanback, SDSU. I mean it's crazy how many FCS guys we even had last year and then obviously like you just said three NDSU guys. I mean NDSU is definitely growing and it's making producing a lot of NFL players and I mean more teammates I can have on this team that I've had before. It's yeah, it's a blessing. It's cool. It's cool to see. text: Oh, it's incredible. title: Drake Maye on the Offense: "I Can Do a Better Job of Starting Us Off Faster." | Press Conference
text: What up? >> All righty. What's going on? >> How we doing? >> Hi. >> How does your um relationship? We >> got Karen over here. >> Sorry, Karen. Do you think you're any more vocal this year than you were last year? >> I think you just try to get more comfortable. I think you get more comfortable naturally as it goes on. And um you know I appreciate you know my you know my chances of being in there and kind of not taking for granted of my responsibility for this team and and kind of the power and kind of the natural you know really I think kind of respect you get for playing my position and I think uh just trying to use that to the best of his ability and try to elevate the guys around me and I think it's something that's good to go back and forth you know I think pushing each other you know they push me to you know be more engaging and be more u more vocal and I think you know I'm pushing them to you know practice better and little things like that and just try to be the best you know back and forth kind of communication week and a half. >> You you've always been very close with Will last season. How have you seen Will Campbell grow um kind of from his rookie season to now and like what you know what are you seeing on the field that's different about year two? >> Yeah, I think he just it's it's great for Will. He just gets it man. I think he gets the, you know, what to, you know, how to practice. You know, he gets, you know, having to come here and show up every day cuz, you know, there's no days off in this, you know, in practice in this league when you're blocking guys and one-on- ones and you got team next and then we got two minute like it's constant. And I think he's learned that really fast. And I think he's, you know, taking it um, you know, taking it head on and I'm looking forward to seeing, you know, him this year do his thing. started slow yesterday and then finished pretty strong. I can maybe do a better job of starting us off faster. Um, but no, you got to respond. You know, that's that's the NFL. That's life. You know, responding from times where you feel like you left some plays out there and we really realize that it's self-inflicted. So, we got to take care of oursel on offense. Um, you know, be in the right spot and it takes all 11 of us. So, just knowing we're on the same page. >> Kan's had a really strong camp so far. He's been involved in some trade rumors. Just want to get your thoughts on that and and whether you'd like to see him stick around this season. >> I think just the way Kan's approaching it, man. He's here. He's here now. He's he he's where his feet at and um you know, I'm having fun throwing him out there in practice. He's doing a great job and um he makes plays when the football's in the air. I think he can speak for that. That speaks for itself. So, um I've had some, you know, a lot of great times with Kan and I'm looking forward to, you know, keep getting better each and every day. >> You hear the phrase chemistry a lot. The team has chemistry. A quarterback has chemistry with receivers. What's your definition of chemistry and do you have it with your teammates? >> I think chemistry is ongoing. I think there's different levels to it. I think there's times where you find you try to, you know, build it and there's times where you try to, you know, maybe, you know, feel like you can, you know, even reach that next level. I think there's always, you know, ways to improve with players. I think guys that are playing for so long and um, you know, whoever it was, Brady and Grank, I bet if you asked them, they'd still say in, you know, year seven and eight, they're still, you know, building ways for their game. And I think there's times where, you know, you feel like you're in a at a stage with a player for two or three years with Hunter and there's still times where me and Hunter, you know, so our third year playing together, we can still elevate our games and and kind of, you know, different looks. There's so many different routes and so many different plays and looks where you can feel like, hey, I understand what he's doing, what he's thinking, and we're trying to react the same way. >> Relation to your tape of Tom Brady. Is there anything that you picked up when it comes to the way that he used a manipulated tempo? I think coach McDaniels is the, you know, one of the best about, you know, kind of learning from it because he's the one that was teaching it out there and and calling it. So, I think just having um, you know, the best things having, you know, what to do before you snap it. I think not snapping into a a bad look or just to play fast for no reason. I think coach was great about, you know, making sure we're in a good play. I think, uh, that was one of the things you noticed remember watching some of the tempo. Um, is making sure we have a good play and stay on track because you don't want to snap it fast and have an incomplete or a negative run. You want to kind of keep the chains moving and keep it going to keep the defense tired and on their heels. So, that's the biggest thing I noticed is just kind of, you know, keeping the chains moving. >> Christian Gonzalez's contract negotiations appear to still be ongoing here. You're you're a year from being in a similar spot where you can negotiate a new deal. Does does how this has gone with him make you wonder at all if if you might have to wait for a new deal from the Patriots? >> I'm not I'm not thinking about that right now. I mean, I think, you know, I'm, you know, a big fan of Gonzo and and kind of how things are playing out. So, uh I respect him for being out here and competing and and wanting to practice. I think that speaks a lot for, you know, you know, him wanting to be here and um, you know, I think, you know, like I said, he's said before, he's one of the best corners in the league. So, I'm looking forward to, you know, playing with him and u, you know, I'm glad he's on our team. >> Is it hard not to think about, you know, your future and your long-term future and maybe being >> Well, I don't think um, I don't think it's hard to think about it for me. I try to be in the present. You know, every day, you know, the present, that's why they call it a present, man. It's a gift. So, I just try to, you know, be here, be where my feet are, and uh, try to get better and better. the other day that you talk more trash than anyone on the offensive side of the ball. Is there someone on the defensive side of the ball who who gets after? >> Me and Spill just love talking football. You know, I really respect Spain's, you know, knowledge for the game and um you know, I think he he loves, you know, talking and um he loves seven on seven and trying to pick me off and um I think he's a great player in this league and I think he's just shows up, man. And he uh he has a few interceptions last year. But uh on defense, who talks a lot? Um, on the field, that's a good question. >> Charles Woods. Yeah, I'm I'm They're outside. I don't really hear them as much. I hear Barour inside a little bit. Bar will get riled up. I like hearing Bar talk. Um, but, you know, really, I think all our guys got a little little stuff to them. I think that's what you need in a defense. You like having hearing those guys and you I try to, you know, be nice to them, but at the same time, you got a little you got to have a little, you know, talk back because, you know, they respect it. >> Your relationship with Jared Wilson goes back to when he was almost your college teammate. So, how does that kind of help you guys in this transition with him at second? Um, I wanted to play for him back in college. He took his talents to bigger bigger dreams. So, um, you know, I can't blame him for that, but no, I think he's done a great job of adapting. Um, it's, you know, it's a lot more communication. You know, I think he was one, he was eager to get inside and play center. So, um, he's he's kind of learning the kind of the center he played in college, but in the NFL, man, it's every day and you got to be durable and you got to be, you know, you know, communication and and little things like that. But, he's doing a great job and looking forward to kind of building, you know, center and quarterback. I mean, that's one of the the biggest relationships on the field. How much you talked about a little bit with a guy like Dobs coming into a new system and Josh's offense. How much you have to work with him decision making that he makes kind of get on that same page as you go into this with a sense of >> Yeah, I think he's a fast learner. That's the biggest thing. You know, he's a fast learner. So, it's it's it's really easy for a good player that's a fast learner to to kind of understand things. And I think there's you try not to overload him and try to kind of take it one thing at a time, but at the same time, he feel like he's got a you know, a great capacity for for knowledge of the game, you know, knowledge of how he does things. and I just like picking his brain about how they did things maybe in Green Bay and try to, you know, say how are we different, how are we similar and kind of how I see things. So, um, he played with a great quarterback there and I think, you know, trying to, you know, like I said, build chemistry and and get on the same page and he'll make some great plays for us. >> What are you looking forward to letting it fly against a different defense next week? >> Yeah, we were just talking in the locker room. Yeah, kind of get want to, you know, face somebody else, but at the same time, you got to, you know, not not shy away from trying to get better against our defense, which is a great defense. So, um, yeah, we're looking forward to getting some to more practice against us and then obviously got, you know, Indianapolis coming in. So, looking forward to, you know, getting somebody else to to hit. >> Do you know what the plan is for you when it comes to preseason yet? How long you're going to play any series you're going to get? >> Yeah. No, I think, you know, I haven't even heard. So, we haven't even talked about that. We're trying to, you know, stay focused on practice and um, you know, what what we did last year and, uh, maybe a little bit different schedule this year, but um, you know, I'll be out there. You know, if they want me to be out there, I'll be out there. So, I'm not shying away from I like being out there. Drake, how do you feel you guys are doing against the blitz as far as diagnosing, setting protections, taking advantage of you have an open receiver? >> Yeah, last year that was one of the biggest things I feel like we, you know, we did a good job at, you know, handling blitz and handling where guys are coming from and being, you know, blocking it up, man. Our guys up front and and Raandre and Tayvon, those guys, even Hunter sometimes, man, they did a great job of pass protecting um that offensive line. So, I got to do a better job of, you know, identifying it and getting the ball out and not taking kind of un unwanted sacks in my opinion to get the ball out. And I think a lot of them were kind of on me. So, I'm doing my part, but I think those guys up front, they're listening to me. Um, telling them where to go, and they're doing a great job. >> Is there anything that you feel like you're learning as a quarterback through watching this battle between AJ Brown and Christian Gonzalez day in and day out? >> Anything I'm learning as a quarterback watching them? Um, I'd say just just that level of intensity. I think that's that's gamelike. I think it's game-ike. I think it's playoff like. I think it's um, you know, it's it builds, you know, great players. And I think you like to see it. You like to see a little trash talk. And um I think you know Gonzo and AJ two of the best of their position and I respect them for going at each other and not trying to hey you know just pity pad and and take it easy on each other going at each other and making each other better. So you know I respect that from them you know being two great players in this league and respect of how they're approaching it. >> D going back to how well you guys picked up the blitz last year. The Seahawks one of the few teams that had any consistent success with the blitz. Were there any specific lessons that you learned from that game that you maybe tried to take into this season? Yeah, I think not trying to get in that scenario where we kind of my rookie year of getting behind you know in the score and kind of kind of off to a slow start and uh you know a start that we didn't want and kind of like I said self-inflicted where you know they were great defense and they did some great things and um I think just finding ways to you know not have the score put into a pass drop back game where we can use play action we can use you know running the football and not just have a drop back game where they can kind of you know pin their ears back and fire at us. So um that's the biggest thing in in a game like that and also they got great players so we got to you know block them up front. Um, I got to know what, you know, where they're coming from and and know where the ball's going. >> Dre, quick question. Uh, year two in coach McDaniel system. Just talk about how much more comfortable you are now having the same coordinator for the second year in a row. >> Yeah, I think it's great to have, you know, coach McDaniels who knows this offense at the, you know, best of the best and know, you know, I think the one of the coolest things when I have questions or when I feel like there's problems, he always has, you know, a clip to explain why there's answers or a reasoning behind it. I think that's really cool for me who's kind of inquisitive and and loves to, you know, ask questions and and understand why we do things, who always has, you know, has answers, you know, knows what could come up before it comes up and, uh, that's one of the best things for me. So, just hearing the the same terminology and the same kind of coaching points over and over again and be able to, you know, hit them and and knowing before I come out here on the practice field is is great for me and I'm looking forward to, you know, seeing what we do in year two and know it's going to be challenging, more challenging with the year with, you know, people studying us and and having a look at us, but that's why we got to elevate and continue to get better with us. So, thank you guys.

But you can't miss many more days after that, the 11th, and expect to be ready in less than a month when you just have not participated in full speed football practices to go into the opener. So, to me, we're looking at next week. If he's not there by next week, I'm worried about his availability. Even though he's a guy who look I I I don't know if Doug mentioned this on the air when we recorded last, but Hurley likes to joke, "Oh, he's the only football player who doesn't need football practice." I don't know. Maybe, yeah, like that is a smart, in shape, tough dude. Just give him a little bit and put him out there. I think Harold Landry would be fine. Maybe they agree, but I think we'll all know probably around this time next week. Uh, last two. Burn. Among all the beat writers at camp, who would you select first overall in a flag football draft? Um, so I would love to say my guy Zach Cox at the Herald, though he is technically our Celtics, well, not technically, he just is our beat reporter covering the Celtics. Uh the name is another teammate of mine though at CNS. Mike Hadlick who college quarterback I think did or almost threw a bomb over my head in the last media game. Point is, you need a quarterback and I love my guy Tommy Kern, but someone's breaking the pocket and needs to scramble a little bit and money's on Cadillac overtime. Last one, Nebraska guy, because of course the Nebraska guy is asking for O line updates and lots of them. Still biggest concern about the team, looking forward to joint practice updates, the most things. I feel like we gave you a lot, but we'll just go left to right with the starters and then call it a day. Will Campbell stronger, looking good in one-on- ones. uh has not given up much if any pressure in team drills. Two big thumbs up. He split his reps in 101 pass rush with Michael Money, Christian Barmore, which you could say is a good thing because if either side had won those, you'd be like, "Oh my god, what about the loser? Are we worried about them?" No, I'm not. I think if he's healthy, he's really good. And I know the Patriots think that, too. So, I'm not worried. Jared Wilson, we're just going to have to see it. Like, I love the athletic profile. I love that he will be a part of more combo blocks at center than he was necessarily at guard last year. He's [clears throat] playing out of position, but I I'm not just going to put my entire faith in a firstear center at the NFL level. Um, who's had a couple of bot snaps with Drake May. He hasn't in about four or five days, so that's good. Mike Wenu, solid. You know, again, people will, oh, he looks overweight. Like, he's a big effing guy. Yeah, probably could lose a couple of pounds. I don't know if that would make him a better player or not. I know I like the player that I see out there now. And he's in contract year, so you're probably going to get the best at Michael whatever best he can offer you. Morgan Moses um practiced more today than I expected. And he's got the best practice plan of all because he's now twice showed up. I say midway, but pretty close to midway through practice and then just jumps into team drills and does all the fun stuff. You're like, "Oh, Morgan Moses is out today." No, no, no. He's just joining in for 111s. Caleb Lom pretty rock solid behind him as the backup right tackle. But right now you are using two plug holes in a way that we thought was just going to be swing tackle but the Patriots might go, you know, uh that backup left guard, that backup right guard spot is uh almost a bigger problem. And maybe [clears throat] it is, maybe it isn't. We'll have to see. It's a beauty of camp.
