title: Jalen Hurts on the Offense's Development in Week 2 of Training Camp
text: How we doing? Good. >> How are you? >> Jaylen, the offensive line we've spoken to so far mentioned there's a lot less confusion on the line because of the new offensive team, how they're able to play faster. What are you noticing from the line play so far? >> That could be a loaded response. Um, but I think um I think I think it starts off with the mentality, you know, the the operation of everything. It's the small things. You know, the big things are won in the small moments and the small details and being able to put it all together. Operate at a good pace with urgency, making sure everyone's communicating, everyone's got all ears and they're they're listening and understanding their assignments and what they're asked to do. Um, that's where it all starts, you know, before you run any play. Got to know what to do. Um, know the sense of urgency we have and then what mode we're in. And so, um, it's it's been really good for the unit to be able to get some reps of that this training camp and I think we've taken strides in those areas. >> About a weekend, how do you think things are coming along with the offense? >> Yeah. Yeah. I think similar to what I just said, just continue to take take strides. You know, I like to think of the term calibrating. This is a time where we're kind of putting it together and finding out who we are. I think it's been very good to be able to compete against a defense who has a built and set identity for who they are. And then obviously us on this end, we've we've got a lot of new pieces, a lot of new I mean entirely new uh approach and mo philosophy to our offense. And so being able to put that together and make it our own, I'm I'm excited about where we are. >> How has that been for you overall? This is your third year going against Big's defense. How how has that made you better? you know, it's it's it's just keeps it very competitive and, you know, I think um my perspective is just to learn as much as I can. Honestly, um I've built a great rapport with him over the years, being able to ask him questions, see what's it see what his goal is on the play, what his intent is, and really be able to learn from the position. So, I'm excited to just continue to experience those things. How important as a quarterback is it to know the why behind a play and how is Shawn at describing that why to you? Yeah, I think you've heard me say that a lot over the years about understanding in depth uh what what am I asked to do and just this you know process of um inductive reasoning and really asking and being curious um you know let letting curiosity lead me and asking questions so I can gain full depth of what I'm asked to do, what you know the running back is supposed to do, the tight end, how the O line is treating this, what are the compliments to this, just kind of finding a flow for um how I should see the game and and then how ultimately the play caller seeing the game too from a sequencing standpoint and a MOO standpoint. So, you know, I think asking those questions give you great understanding. Um, and I'm I've been very excited about the conversations that Shan Sean and I have been able to have. >> You got the helmet on the helmet. You find that I >> think um it it gives you know insight and a and a bit of count accountability in the huddle. So, I think there's an aspect of that that is very valuable. Yeah, >> we've seen some more designed QB runs the last few days. How does that mesh with what this new offense brings? >> It's too soon to answer yet. Too soon to answer yet. You know, I think we're still installing things and putting all aspects in our offense in. You know, we we we haven't finished installing. There's still more to come. Um, but we're working and we're building. And I think in training camp, especially with new pieces and a new offense, it's the ability to retain information and then put it together, go out there and execute. And so we're we're continue to take steps. >> The last couple days with Devonte being out, how have you been able to kind of build rapport of the new receivers like how you know? >> It's been great. Um, you know, I think this is, you know, I use the term calibrating again a little bit, right? You get an opportunity to see who's who, what's what, everybody's mentality, their approach. um give guys chances in some situations to build that trust, you know, um that that that doesn't just stop in the summertime in Florida or in Houston, you know, when we're working out intimately. It it continues throughout practice, every day, every meeting, every conversation. So, we're just continuing to build on that, build on top of that, build building blocks on that. And that's been that's been really good. He's such a you keep the ball that dimension of your game seem to be man football is a fun sport. This is my passion. This is what I love to do. Um you know I think I think I think what's just been my biggest motivation is just to come in here and learn and improve. And so, however that looks, you know, that that doesn't really change for me, but you know, I know when every year comes, you you kind of had to have have a reset um and just be able to build an identity for this team this year. So, um, just taking it a day at a time, trying to finish every rep, finish every play, giving my very best. >> Something about that? No, I think um I mean it was a great rep. Um but we had a a mishap on the on a play on the first play of seven on seven that day where he ran we had a outcut on and he ran a outcut return and stopped in the middle of the route and it resulted in an interception. And so I just think that was an example of responding. That's what I was so proud of and happy about that um not not the throw but you know that he was able to play the next play, show up in the right window at the right time and rip it in there for a touchdown the middle of the field. So um you know I think that's just the emmo about um being a resilient team. Um being a a group of guys that you know we we understand the importance of doing our job and how that affects the next person, but we we take pride you know in in the small things. And so I just thought that was a small moment. Um, a great catch by him, great route where to where to find the void in the middle of the field, catch it on the run, but just a a thing of how you respond and so how you respond to adversity? >> Nick mentioned on that practice that it was more of a review day for you guys to go over things that you had installed in the walkthrough the day before. I guess how instructive are those days for the offense when you're not going through like the early install on stuff and you get to wrap it up. >> Say that again. How important uh the review days like you know Nick mentioned that that Monday practice was a chance for you guys to go over something that you had already repped a few times. How instructive are those days for the offense? >> Yeah, those those days are very important. Um and I think in the end, right, we've got a lot of new things going in and so it's just a matter of putting those things all together and the more reps you build in that the more confidence you have and I've seen that with our entire offense and so that's just been the been the approach, right? I think when we've had an opportunity to sit on it, you know, it it builds equity and ingrains into the whole entire unit's minds. There's a urgency out the huddle. There's no questions and asking where I'm supposed to line up, where am I supposed to go. So that's an entire 11 and unit thing where um you know, the more we rep it, the more we break it down, um the more it slows down and um the the more confidence we build in everything. and we've been able to hit some really amazing plays this camp and then we know we're going to continue to just stack on top of that over time. >> When you turn when you turn your back to the uh to the defense of play action on the center of play action, how does that change what you've done in shotgun in terms of going through your reads? >> It changes nothing because it's all going to my feet. So, when I'm playing with my feet and my getting my eyes to the right place, you just play the position. You know, it's um I just think that's a a more of a a flow thing. When you talk about the dynamic of being under center and, you know, running run action, it's a it's a sequencing thing. I think um in the end, you know, you're still playing the position. You want to play the position the same way. play with your feet, sweep through your reads, know exactly where you're supposed to go to with the ball, where your alerts are, whether it's down the field or whether it's a man alert, just try and play fast. But that is more so a just understanding what you're doing, what we're trying to attack, being on the same page, and playing each play, positive plays. Getting back to the new pieces that Martin asked about earlier, Dante specifically, what kind of impression has he made on you so far? >> I mean, he's he's got great great work ethic. He's got great hunger, you know, in in the summertime. He was beaten down the door trying to spend that time and just work. And, you know, he's he's twitchy, can attack the ball. He's got uh you know when you talk about adversity when I said some I said about adversity you know you you get you you learn a lot a lot you learn a lot about the guys around you around this time of camp when it's humid it's sticky it's it's hot you see who's got who's got that who's got that that anger to him who's got a little bit of rage in them for the best. Um he's got it. So, um, that's exciting to see. He's, you know, runs great routes and, um, it'll be exciting to see him work this this, uh, this season. Great aggression he has. >> Thanks, You think?

title: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. & More on Their Personal NFL Growth
text: biggest difference between you this year and last year? >> Um on like what what standpoint are you asking? >> Just as far as physically, mentally, just >> Oh, I I got you. Um >> the defense. >> Yeah. So So I think I from last year, I definitely uh continue to prove myself physically. You know, I always try to make sure I'm ready in the like in the best shape I I am in in my life because I want to come out here and make sure that my teammates know that I'm, you know, grinding and working for them. And um as far as the the defense, I feel like I definitely grown there, too. Just being here three years now uh under, you know, Vic Vick's um scheme and everything, I've been able to just learn and soak in a lot more details and understand the defense and responsibilities and like the little details as well. And I just been trying to learn and make sure I'm I'm studying that to make sure that I know all the ins and outs of my job and my role when I'm out there on the field. >> Said that this is deep. >> How has that changed your approach? Yeah, I I feel like, you know, when you're looking at a different offensive scheme like this, um we've been seeing a lot more motion, a lot more uh different things like that where we have to think as a defense and I feel like that's really good for us as a whole to see like different a different scheme like that and and have to think on the run. That will definitely help us, you know, in season when we face offenses like that and of that, you know, type of scheme of try to get your eyes in the wrong place and and get you out of position. But um I feel like that's been a some one of the changes that we as a defense have to experience with this scheme uh this training camp. >> How is it how important is it for you to mix in with the one? Vic said that's purposeful uh to make sure you get some time next to Jihad and and and Zach as well. How important is that for you? >> Yeah. No, it's great, you know, being able to build continue to build chemistry, but you know, I just whenever I'm out there, no matter who I'm with or, you know, uh, the reps I'm getting, I just try to make sure I'm doing my job and just, you know, helping do my role in the defense because that's one of the things that we talk about in in like defensive team meetings is making sure that all 11 guys are on the same page and when all 11 guys are working as one, it's hard to beat the defense like that. So, I just try to make sure I'm I'm being a part of that 11 guys that is doing their job. A couple years ago, your dad was here at practice and he was on the team had a mic and he walked up to Vic and he said, "You know, you remind me of Jim Johnson." Did your dad ever talk about Jim Johnson as a coordinator, what he was like to play for? Has he furthered on that? Like any connection that he sees between the way Jim did it and the way he does it? >> Yeah, I mean what you said is, you know, correct. I mean, he's always had good things to say about Jim um how and how he is as a coordinator and everything. He really liked playing under him. And as far as the stories and different things that he's told me, uh, it's always been good things. And, um, you know, as far as like, you know, I was probably I was too young to like, you know, really remember that. But, you know, hearing about, you know, the different good things and everything that he said about him, I can see why he he would say something like that. >> What goals do you come into this season with? >> Really just, you know, try to be the best player I can be. You know, make the most of any opportunities I get. Uh, I try to make sure I'm always ready, uh, to, you know, fill whatever role this team needs and and just, you know, play 110% in that role and and be and try to fill that role the best I can to my ability. >> How's that conversation different among the experienced players compared to say two years ago or even last year? >> Say that one more time. >> How's the the level of conversation different among the experienced players compared to two years ago when you first learned the defense and even last year? I mean, uh, I mean, every single year, guys just continue to learn the defense and, learn the scheme, um, a lot better. I mean, when you're three years in and, you know, I I was able to get be with Victor for three years and learn his scheme. And I think every every single year, I just continue to grow and learn more about how he likes it to be run because in our scheme, we have a lot a lot of small details that we have to know. Uh, it's not just I have the flat. It's got to be something, you know, the little details of understanding formation, splits, all that different stuff. But, um, you know, I just just learned that over the over the years has definitely helped out. >> Yeah. I mean, Chance is a great backer. He's really instinctual. He's smart. He um, he's going to be doing his job. He's going to fit the run. He's going to play the pass. And I feel like Chance has all the abilities that you want out of a backer. give any advice to uh Josiah and his first hand. Did you have any? >> Well, I mean, you know, nothing that he doesn't already know. Uh just told him, you know, make sure you go in, you show the coaches that you're going to work hard, you're going to do your job, and you know, just play linebacker physically. I mean, that's one of the main the main key that keys that you want to show when you're a rookie coming in is that you're going to work hard, you're going to learn to scheme, and you're going to be violent. When the Kobe left, they asked him sort of like what he thought he'd missed. And he thought being in a room with a collection of guys, but he also said he needed somebody to keep Zack from being so tough on the young guys without him there. What's he like in that room? >> I'm sure I'm sure Nico if he said that, he was probably just messing around with him, you know. Uh but you know, Zack Zach's a great leader, a great veteran guy in the locker or in the uh in the room. and um you know he cracks jokes just like everybody else, but you know we we love we love Zach and how he treats the young guys and brings them along as a veteran in the game. >> Ch this linebacker room is so deep and everybody can play. How competitive are you guys amongst yourselves as far as who who can make a play in practice, who can, you know, stand out. >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, we're all very competitive. We're all trying to, you know, make each other better. And I feel like when there's competition, that's that's what happens. You got to raise your level of play to compete with the guy next to you. And and and we all understand that we're all just trying to make each other better. We're all trying to, you know, we're all helping each other, learning learn different things from each other, sharing knowledge and everything. And we just got a great connection and great bond through that. >> How does this offense, how does this offense with so much under center play action, uh misdirection, how much does it stress the uh the offball linebackers? >> Yeah, as an offball linebacker, you definitely got have to be cleaning your reads. Um, you know, with the under center and and the play action and just the different motions that they use, you got to make sure that you're reading your keys because it can be tough, you know, when when everything's happen fast and, you know, uh, having to have to play a different style offense like that. But, um, you know, you just got to try to lock into your fundamentals of where your your eyes are to have good reads and everything. >> The preseason is not too far away. Um, I don't know if we'll get a chance to talk to you before that. So, what is your approach heading into that game given where things are for you right now with this team? >> Well, just to be ready, you know, to go out there and and and if they told me to go out there and play, I'm going to be ready to go out of there and play and make the most of every opportunity I get. >> Thank you guys. >> How do you feel it's going so far for you? >> Uh, going good. Going good. Just enjoying and embracing uh new teammates, uh, new coaches staff learn and everything. I've been enjoying it. How would you describe things now starting to get high? >> Uh he's very aggressive. He you know he likes you know for defenses to make plays uh the front variable front so guys up front you know it starts there. So those guys get after get after the quarterback and expectations on the back end starts to feed off that and make plays. >> How and how and why how does like Vic stress about not giving away too much pre- snap to to uh to guys in your position? Yeah, I think a lot of it comes down uh to either veteran quarterbacks in this league who can make adjustments, you know, late in the down, you know, or the check with me offenses where we might have a younger, you know, quarterback where the offensive coordinator can get in and kind of change the play. So, us being able to keep our shell as long as we can, you know, and play a little uh peekab-boo with the with the offense and make them have to adjust, you know, late and either run the play they're going to run or try to adjust late. >> In such a a young cornerback role, where are you providing value behind this? Yeah, I mean just coming in and trying to get my experience, you know, being in the league for 10 years and and giving them experience and seeing what it's like to be at a high level. Uh these guys have seen a lot of high level ball and good winning early in their career. Um and I just try to any wisdom that I have that's been passed down to me from, you know, my veterans. Uh just trying to trying to do the same. >> How do you feel about the >> I think we have a lot of talented guys, a lot of guys that can do a lot of different things. Um it kind of makes it valuable, you know, to guys that can move around uh either from safety to nickel, nickel to corner. I think that adds a lot of value. >> How do you what do you do physically to like during the offseason to to get to camp in shape when you get into year seven, eight, nine, 10? >> Yeah, I mean a lot of running and lifting, trying to keep the body good. Uh it's just a big thing, you know, staying physically in shape. There's a lot of thing a lot of guys, you know, take too much time off and it's harder to get back into shape. If you stay in shape, it makes it easier. >> Does it get harder each year to kind of get where you want to be? >> Uh not really. Uh I thought it would. It hasn't yet, you know, to to really uh take much to get, you know, get into shape, be ready for camp. Um just the biggest thing is just staying in it mentally it becomes a big thing. >> Did you fly to camp this time? >> Uh yeah. Yeah. Game up. I'm here here to stay. So excited. >> How about this summer? How much flying did you do this summer? >> Uh a little bit. You know, back and forth to back to Georgia. Got to fly a good bit. Uh didn't get anywhere anywhere nice as I did on the first break, but it was good. >> Have you thought about going back to New England in a couple weeks at all or >> Yeah. >> What it mean to you? Yeah, I'm I'm excited, you know, more so for the support staff and everyone in that building, you know, being there for nine years. You have so many relationships there. So, just to see the people who were there when I was there to be be a nice, you know, to go out there and meet those guys and see him again. >> Big said he tries to mix as many people in, get some first team reps. How important is it to get those with, you know, maybe the the the safeties and things like that? >> Yeah, I think it's important, you know, just hearing calls, you know, from the guys and hearing the communication and and learning and jelling with the guys. You know, everyone has their certain way they like to play certain things. And so the more you get guys in there and they're comfortable with different people, you kind of understand, you're kind of already knowing how a safety might want to call something, how he sees it. So it makes it a lot easier. >> It's our first time speaking with you since you signed. So you've had some exposure now to the team in these past few months. What stands out about the different roles that he's playing and him as a player? >> He's just a football player. I mean, that's that's how I describe him. You know, tackler, he can run. I think, you know, a lot of people don't give him credit for the speed that he has. Uh, like I said, an aggressive football player and I'm excited to work with him. >> How does the how does campa run this year? >> Uh, I don't want to get into that all of that, but you know, we work, you know, we work here and I I enjoy that. You know, I've been to a place that we didn't work, you know, the kind of way that we get after here and I enjoy that. You know, it makes you feel ready for the season. You know, when you go out there against your guys and you guys get good work, when you come out game one, those first four games, you can kind of tell the teams who have a tough camp, they get after it, you know, they're they're slow into those first four games versus teams who come out and you get after each other in training camp, you kind of feel more ready for the season. >> What perspective can you give on, you know, guys, whether it's it's it's uh either Pini, you know, or Michael Carter who are playing, you know, essentially three different positions. There's already three different positions. What's the what's the challenge with something like that? Yeah, I think what makes it easy um is when they say you learn the concept, you're understanding, you know, not your position, understanding everything and how it fits in into the puzzle. Uh and it slows it down for you. And then the biggest thing is I tell them all the time is just you'll start to feel football instead of seeing it. You'll feel what certain concepts feel like. You'll feel a boot play and it allows you to play um a little slower actually. You know, you're playing slower, more comfortable, more relaxed um just because you've seen those reps over and over and over and that helps. Uh, and just having consist consistency, you know, being in the system, I was fortunate enough to be in the same system, you know, for nine years. And so that adds a lot. So these guys getting year in and year out of consistency. They'll bring up plays from last year that may have hurt them or, you know, things that you want to improve on. So guys being here last year, um, and seeing some of the challenges that present itself to the defense, those guys being able to come out, make some adjustments year in and year out actually helps. I know I know Devonte's sideline right now, but but what's it like going up against him uh on a day-to-day basis versus I'm sure you you faced him a few times in the regular season. What's it like going to a guy like that? >> Yeah, I mean he's explosive. He's one of those guys that can get in and out of cuts. Uh makes you play the whole field, you know, all the way across, all the way down, you know, three-level route runner, which, you know, it's, you know, some guys get stuck in a box is one or two things. You know, when he comes out there, you can understand that at any route he can give you. >> You remember anything about uh the undrafted defensive backs about like your journey and how to make an impression and cancel early on. >> Yeah. Uh talk to those guys a lot. You know, being an undrafted player as you come in and try to make a mark, you know, uh be prepared for anything. Be ready. If a special teams team, uh just being ready and whenever your moment's called, be overprepared. Um I think a lot of times as a young player, there's a lot going through your mind. There's a lot, you know, you're in a new city, you just came, the NFL is new to you. But just the more you can slow it down and just get in that playbook and be ahead, it'll help. >> What do you remember about joint practices two years ago at Foxburg with the Eagles? >> Oh, couple of fights, [laughter] couple of fights. No, it was it was good. It was good. You know, just two organizations that I can speak to that are well ran, two organizations that do the right thing. Um, you know, top down, you know, and just to be in both places and see it, you know, from the other side. We knew when Philly came in, you know, we're going to get good football and good football players. Um, and I think they'll be prepared for that and vice versa. We should be prepared to see some good football players and a good football team up there. >> Appreciate it. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. >> Uh second training camp for you. Uh how do you think it's going so far and what are some areas you feel like improved on after offseason work? >> Yeah. Uh it's going it's going pretty well. Uh of course got to get better. Um just understanding, you know, the difference but between offense in the NFL, offense in college, you know, and now it's year two, you know, I got a year under my belt already by the grace of God. And now it's just um mental, the mental aspect of the game, you know, and uh I think just improving in that, understanding defenses, coverages, and things of that nature, trying to improve mentally is uh my focus. >> You had that one-handed grab the other day. Uh can you take us through that play and yeah, kind of where's where do you feel that? >> Yeah, down in the red zone, you know, got to have it situation. Um and you know, Andy put it up there and uh by the grace of God was able to bring it down. I don't think I got my foot in though. But uh it was still a pretty good catch. So just roll really working on the fundamentals, getting get my drag in, you know, getting to my back. So things of that nature. The catch, you know, the catch that's just extra work. You know, the catch going to happen, but it's like what you do after that. Do you get your foot in? Do you get on your back? Do you do the fundamentals? So that's what I'm focused on. >> Siri said before camp and he mentioned you among one of the guys that does kind of the dirty work. >> Do you kind of take pride in that job and what is that job to you? >> Yeah. whatever is asked of me, you know, putting the [clears throat] team before myself, of course, that's, you know, that's what you do in this game. Uh, so whatever is asked of me, you go in out there and do it 110%. >> What are your impressions of the receiver room? >> I love the receiver room, bro. We we got a great room. We're growing. Uh, got a nice little camaraderie going on there. So, I think we'll be good. >> It was a year ago on these fields where you started to turn some heads. What do you remember about that first training camp and what do you think it took to get to that point? >> Yeah, man. just having that chip on my shoulder, you know, coming from a smaller school, undrafted free agent, you know, that's kind of been my life my for my whole football career, you know, coming from smaller schools, things of that nature, but still making a name for myself, but really just staying humble, you know, um keeping keeping with my faith and everything like that and putting the work in and God going to handle the rest. >> Is that does that chip still is that chip still there even though you you spent all last season with the team? >> Is that chip on your shoulder still there now? >> Oh, most definitely. Most definitely. Uh, look, last year is in the past, you know, so this is a new year. Be be where my feet is, and that I have that same mentality for sure. >> You guys have a couple of receivers who are down the last couple of days. Uh, how much more reps do you get as a result? How important is it for you to to really take advantage of those? >> Yeah, whenever whenever we have some guys go down, the next man got to step up, you know, just having that mentality and that's what for our whole room, our whole room is doing that. Um, and I think that we have some great receivers in this at this organization and we're all ready for, you know, to take that next step. Devonte Smith asking now is that number one sorry Devonte Smith now that number one receiver with AJ Brown no longer here. Does he act any different? Does he do anything different in this new role? >> No. >> Smitty is the same person every it don't matter what's going on. Smitty is the same. He's humble. He do his work and he's consistent, man. That's why he's one of the best in the league. >> What was your reaction uh this offseason when he's bringing in all these receivers that draft they sign [snorts] a couple they trade for long? >> Yeah, I mean it's part of it's part of the game. It's part of the the industry that we play in, man. And you know, you got to know how to adjust. You got to know how to you meet so many people in this um in [snorts] in NFL, man. So, it's it's I'm happy to meet these new guys, man. Learn from them, pour into them as they pour into me. So, it's it's a blessing to me. >> Find the time with Jaylen in the offseason this summer. >> Very important. Very important. Just to you know, yeah, we got some work in, but just the the talks, the conversations that we have off the field is just as important. It was good. >> What's your impressions of uh what's your impressions of this new scheme and what do you think it does? uh how it benefits us. >> Yeah, love the new scheme and we definitely have the receivers to to run the routes. We definitely have the receivers to block on the perimeter for our backs and um I think it's going to be pretty solid. >> Working with Jaylen, they also have some in Houston, right? >> Um yes. >> Did it Did you get a sense that it was his hometown out there? Did they show you around a bit? >> So, actually, I'm sorry. No, we actually got some work out out there in Florida. So, yeah. Yeah. So, it was good out there, man. We had some good time, man. We spent some time together. So, it was it was it was great. Last year you were doing a lot of the dirty work in this offense. This year with the new system, what what is new that they're asking >> I mean, just whatever they asked of me. Um, still still got to do the dirty work. Got to block on the perimeter. Still got to have a mentality on special teams as well. So, I'm still I'm in the same mindset. Nothing is changing for me. Um, but sharpening my, you know, of course sharpening my my things on offense as well with my routes and everything like that, but still in that same mindset as last year. Like, hey, I'm going be a dog on the offense. I'm be a dog on special teams, and that's what I'm going to do. How's it feeling after dealing with that last? >> Shoulder's feeling great, man. Surgery went surgery went well and we back we back 100%. >> We hear a lot about uh how Shawn has been behind the scenes, the film studies, the way he explains things. Sounds like it's it's really easy to understand for [snorts] you guys. How has that been and and uh what kind of a of a teacher is he? >> Oh man, he's a great teacher. He's a great guy, you know, with all the installs that we have and everyone is learning something new, you know, when it comes to the coaches to us. So, he's been uh he's been great explaining everything in detail and has uh he's made it easy for us to go out there and perform. >> Well, a new offensive system. How do you feel like it's going so far with the offensive line? >> I feel like it's going pretty good. Um just me coming from college, obviously, it's an adjustment. Uh just talking to Lane the other other week, he was just saying there going to be some growing pains and just through the system and me switching over to right tackle and playing both, you know, going to be some growing pains, but we getting better each and every day. How val how valuable have the first two reps that you've been getting for? >> It's been good. I've been going against the best, you know, just coming out. I'm just trying to compete. Just trying to get better and trying to earn the trust of my teammates so I can go out there on Sunday to compete. >> How about the right tackle of it all after playing left side? >> You said it again. >> How is going going to the right side for >> Like like I just mentioned, there some growing pains. Definitely some growing pains, but I'm like I said, I'm getting better each and every day. I'm getting more comfortable and it's going to help me in the long run. >> What are some of the growing pains you're working through? Uh, I mean, just ju just going from one side to another is it's a whole different whole different ball game over there. And just for me playing left tackle my whole career and just coming over here and playing right tackle and then going against one of the best defenses. I mean, it's, you know, it's tough, but I'm doing good. >> Jordan Milada, Lane Johnson, what are the conversations like when I I can imagine trying to help you in the meeting room and on the field? Yeah, I mean it's more more of a mental I feel like more of a mental thing and especially like I said just me going going right from left to right more of a mental game and so we just talking talking through plays talking through how do I feel during this play or during this set and just you know just talking through ball. >> You getting any feedback from Nolan or Jix or any guys on the other side? >> Say it again. Jix or guys on >> Yeah, I'm I'm asking I'm asking them for tips and I I go back I go back and I go watch games with them. I go watch tackles that, you know, do good against them. I go watch tackles that do bad against them. Man, I'm doing I'm doing my own scout work. So, you know, just just trying to come out here and compete, get get everybody better. >> What's kind of been the toughest adjustment for you so far between college? >> Um, probably probably the mental side. It's definitely more of a mental strain. I say that, too. But also, everybody is it's a physical strain as well too. So, probably probably just on the mental side as well too. What's what's the like how do they test you now? >> I mean just just the play calls and the the play calls are longer, the counts are different. We're not just going going to the line clapping their hands and we're going like it's it's different. So just got to lock in. >> We always hear a lot about the speed of the game being different. Have you I know it's only been like a week here at K. Have you noticed that? >> Yeah, I mean everything's full speed and obviously different. We're going against better athletes and everything, but end of the day just football. >> Different system. Uh some of the vets were talking about how it helps them. >> Um they've had more experience than you obviously, but from what you have played in before you since that, how different is this system to you? >> Uh yeah, it very different. Um it's very different and I feel like it caters to me as to what I can do. I'm big. I'm I'm physical. I'm fast. I'm athletic. So that's that's what this system allows me to do. Put my my talents on full display. How would you describe Chris Cooper as coaching style and how has he helped you in your adjustment? >> He's he's very helpful. He's very helpful. Uh he he knows the the strain I'm in. I'm in right now. He's he knows the position I'm in. Me personally, I'm just trying to seize the opportunity I have in front of me. I mean, that's pretty much it. But know Coop every step of the way. He he's been patient with me. He's been helping me. He's he stayed staying after. He man he's helping. He got both feet both feet forward. Uh, who your teammates have you connected with maybe on more of a personal level so far? Say again. >> Who have you connected with on more of a personal level so far? >> I mean, my old line guys for sure. My old line guys for sure. Them guys I'm going to be playing playing next to, but I mean everybody I mean we're all a team. We all brothers. We all family. So man, just just getting to know everybody to be honest. >> You mentioned the opportunity that lays ahead of you. Do you feel like the swing tackle role is an opportunity that is within reach? >> I feel like I feel like any opportunity I can get on the field is opportunity for me. I'm just trying I'm just trying to be ready when my name's called. doing that in Miami, uh, coming in for injuries and such. I mean, how much do you feel like that's prepared you for that kind of role? >> Yeah. I mean, yeah. And this is I'm in the same kind of predicament, you know, um, me coming from Jo to Miami, I didn't know what to expect. I didn't know what to expect. I was just trying to go out there and compete and be ready with my name called. So, I'm kind of kind of in the same position right now. And so, really ain't nothing too much. Just football. And how much do you think like going against the edge rushers that you went against in practice at Miami, how much do you think that helped prepare >> Oh yeah, it helped me a ton. Help me a ton. They were NFL tap tell them they both win the first round and now now I'm going against first round and myself when them them guys got three years in the game, three, four years in the game. So it's all going to help me out in the long run. >> What impressed you about you know going against them in the practice from a skill set perspective? >> Yeah, they they're very smart. They're very smart. They're very savvy. uh they they take pride in their in their craft and so I try to do the same. I'm doing the same when it's my time to do what I got to do. >> What's the relationship with my lot like continuing to train here? >> Yeah, it's really good. It's really good. Um I feel like he he he's turned to the big brother that I needed, especially on this level. He uh like I said, he's been there with me. He's been patient with me and you know, we just we just talk about everything. We talk about life in general, talk about football. We can laugh and joke all we want to. Oh, yeah. >> First uh week and a half has gone for you. >> It's been good, man. Um I'm I'm blessed to be out here. It's a blessing to be able to, you know, be at this stage and be able to compete every single day. Um I've enjoyed it, man. I've had a great time. So, I'm out here continuing to learn every day and trying to get better. So, >> what would you say has been the biggest adjustment so far? >> Uh biggest adjustment, I'd say probably the mental challenge. I think that um the offense and and the way that the the defenses do their schemes at this level. Um it's a little more complex than it was in college. And so, um, I think just a mental challenge, but, you know, that's just about putting the time in and, uh, learning it and trying to get better with it. So, >> Nick talked about your ability to kind of find a soft spot in the zone. Where does that come from? Is that your quarterback background? >> I'd say it probably has something to do with that. Yeah, I think that's, uh, just the way that I've grown to see the game my whole life. Um, and I think it does help me in that way. And then trying to, you know, intertwine that with learning the game from the tight end perspective. Um, is what I'm trying to do right now. >> How do you get through, I mean, they're throwing a lot at you guys. uh how do you get through the moments of frustration, the challenges that you face? >> Yeah, I mean at the end of the day, this is this is a game where there's going to be ups and downs and um you just got to learn how to bounce back from adversity. Uh no, no one who has ever played this game has ever been perfect and um the ones who are great are the ones that can bounce back from the adversity and go make the next play. So, >> is that easy for you or is it a challenge? >> Uh I think it's continuously getting easier for me. Um but I think that's something that's a challenge for for a lot of people. Um, and you know, it's always a challenge when something when something bad goes goes down and you just have to learn continuously learn how to just get back up, not worry about the last play and continue on the next play. >> What sort of feedback you getting so far from coaches? >> Uh, it's been good, man. I mean, really, I'm just out here trying to learn um continuously learn every single day and um I'm really appreciative of my coaches so far just trying to help me out. Um, you know, kind of get me going at this at this level and you know, I'm super excited for for what's going to come. One of the ways you guys learn is off the field and we've heard a lot of guys raving about the way Shawn Banam is is teaching with film and how he's teaching behind the scenes. What are you experiencing through all that and how much is that helping when you get out here? >> Yeah, I mean every single day we are doing uh meetings as a unit um in the offense. It's not just positioning. We'll bring the whole unit together and we'll go over film. Um we'll talk about plays and you know every single day he's going to set he's going to set a standard and we have to you know uphold that standard. Um, and when we don't, he tells us in the in the in film, uh, with the entire unit, and I think it just helps us grow that chemistry together. So, >> Dallas and Johnny have about, I guess, 20 years combined NFL experience. What What does that do for you having them in the room? >> It's awesome, man. Like, uh, just being able to learn continuously. I mean, I've been playing this position for going on three years now and, um, you know, being around those guys who have been in the league for 10 years. Um, just learning from them. They have so much experience, so much knowledge, so much wisdom. um they've they've taken me in tried to help me um get better with the things that I'm trying to get better at as well. So, >> Eli, we've seen alumni around the facility the last two days, but didn't see Jordan Matthews. >> Did you reach out like where are you? What's happening? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. No, he's uh he's got his own stuff going out there in Nashville. Um you know, that's my guy. He's always checking up on me. I'm always talking to him, texting him, calling him. So, um you know, I love him to death. He He's been a huge mentor for me as well. So, >> you mentioned that it's only been three years playing this position. Is it surreal at all for you? I mean, be at this point, you know, to be >> Yeah. I mean, I'm just I'm super thankful and super blessed that that God's given me this opportunity. Um, you know, it's been a lot of ups and downs, a lot of hard work, and, you know, just to get to this point. And so, I'm super thankful, man. Not nec I mean, it is surreal in a way. Um, but I'm just thankful and I want to continue to, you know, try to work as hard as I can to be the best I can be. At >> this stage of camp, how much attention do you place on? >> Uh, I don't think at at this point in the camp that that's something that you should pay attention to at all. I think right now it's just focusing on trying to get better. You know, that's what training camp is for. You're trying to get, you know, at the best that you can be for the season, prepare for it. Um, and I think that's what I'm focused on right now. >> How about the blocking side of things? How much challenging how challenging has that been at this level to try to grab and I mean, I know everybody's trying to learn it on this team. It's all new. >> Yeah. Uh, no, I mean, that's that's another another aspect to the game that, you know, really everybody has to learn. Um, everybody that blocks, you know, the O line, the tight ends, even the receivers. Um, that's a part of the game that's super important in the run game. Um, in the pass game too and pass pro. And so I'm trying to same thing, continue to learn and and put the work into so that I can be the best I can be at that. >> Johnny told us something yesterday I didn't know that when he was well he was undrafted and when he joined the league he was he considered himself more of a pass receiver and then made himself a blocker. Is that a story he's relayed to you and what do you take from it if so? Yeah, I mean Johnny is is um super inspirational in the way that he like approaches his work. Um you know, like I said, you can see the experience um and how he approaches every single day. Uh just the way he prepares for practice, the way he plays in practice. Um you know, he's super technically sound and and you can tell he really focuses on that and he's done had a lot of hard work to get to that point. Um and so yeah, he's talked to me about it and I'm just trying to learn from him as much as I can. >> Couple more. Aside from uh Dallas and John, who who's been the most helpful to you? Who have you kind of gravitated towards so far? >> Um yeah, I mean there's a bunch of guys like a bunch of a bunch of veterans and like I was just talking to Elijah Moore earlier today and he's been in the league for six or seven years or something like that and um you know a lot of the receivers um Devonte Smith um Dantavian Wixs, all those guys. I mean, I'm I'm trying to learn from as as many people as I possibly can who have been in the league for a while. Um because there's a learning curve at this level, and that's what I'm trying to, you know, I'm trying to get over that hump and get to the point um to where I can be the best that I can be. >> Do you feel yourself getting better? >> I do for sure. Yeah. I mean, just the just this last week, I've I've already seen a ton of improvement in my game. Um and that's props to to the coaches who've been helping me out, the other players who've been helping me out. Um and me putting in all I have to do is put in the work. And you you know, you'll continuously see progress. And that's what I've seen so far. >> Thank you. Thank you.

title: Vic Fangio on Defense's Development During Camp
text: All right, who's up? >> Uh, safety Michael Carter uh has shown up a little bit at least made a splash play yesterday. What What do you think of that competition? >> Yeah, I think Michael's had a good camp so far. He's um might be the only guy I'd have to think, but uh he's learning three positions. He's playing safety, nickel, and when we do go to our 6dB stuff, he's the 6DB in there. So, I think he's had a very good camp and uh has done nothing but helped himself and and not eliminating himself from anything safety. He could he's progressing nicely. >> Vic, what's the biggest difference in Drew Makuba this year and last year? >> You know, I I really think it's just experience and knowledge and knowhow of the defense. Um, you know, you might look and say, "Man, he looks quicker. He's in better shape." This that. And I really think it's just the thought processes have speed it speed it up comfortability with the uh defense and what he has to do. And I do think he's in a little bit better shape too. >> We saw that Jad Cample yesterday. I I know that that was a big pull with the Kobe. Will Jad have that initial? >> We hope so. Um you know it was nice to see him do it yesterday, but we'll see how he does in the game. But yeah, I mean he should be able to. >> Is Cooper already? >> Yeah. Why you ask? >> That's news to me. >> Is that something that wanted them to do or did they just do that on their own? It is something the team wanted to do. Why? >> No. Um, yeah, I don't think they have. I mean, Jix is weighing the same that he's was last year. Nolan uh came back in the spring heavier and now he's back down to where he should be. >> Saw a lot from >> Have you noticed Have you noticed Jaylen Carter being a lot more active in camp? I mean, is that because, you know, he's fully healthy? >> Yeah, I I think he's had a good camp up to this point. he's um [snorts] doing the little things better, which when you're in good shape, you know, those the little things are done better cuz when you're not in good shape and you're just kind of getting through practice, the little things suffer. And I think he's doing a much much better job and, you know, really excited for what the possibilities are with him. >> Reek was talking about how he's enjoying playing off the ball a little bit more. Um he said he's known it's more impressed situation. What have you seen from him playing more off uh >> Yeah, like he's like we said earlier um earlier in the offseason um for a guy as tall as he is, he's got good movement, you know, he it's not press or nothing. He can play off, he can mirror routes, he can come out of a break. Um and I think it's good he's working on that. you know, it's easy to always do what you're good at, you know, and you need to work at deficiencies that you may need to incorporate into your game, and he's done a good job of that. >> How has Jordan Davis gone about improving his pass rush moves? >> Well, it first started, you know, towards the end of the uh 24 season. Um, he got in better shape. you know, he's a much better pass rusher at in the 330s than he is what he was. And um that to me is the biggest thing. Um you know it he's I think he's 66, right? Or what is he 605? We'll call it 66 for discussion. He needs to be 66 when it's to his advantage and he needs to bend his knees and be 6'3 when he needs to be. And when you're in better shape, weighing less, that's easier to do and you can do it for a longer time and that's what's made his game take off. >> What about the offense implementing a new scheme? Do you work with them at all? Were they what's that? >> With the offense implementing a new scheme, right? Do you work with them at all where they ask you to give certain looks during the course of practice or >> Yeah, we do that with each other. Um, you know, where I'll give them what they're looking for and and vice versa. >> What are your impressions of uh Ebiki on the edge? >> He's he's um he's made nice progress here. You know, I think coming in the off season in the six OTAAS we had um it was kind of new to him. uh he was hesitant. Not sure. I think he's made a lot of progress in that manner and is having a much better camp and he's him and some of the other guys are taking advantage of the lo of the reps they're gaining with Grenard being out for a while >> with the with the two guys who are so good. How do you balance getting them the reps they need versus not pulling the team back? What are your >> Yeah, it's it's hard, you know, cuz there's a health um >> part of that too, you know, um to where you don't want them or, you know, one of in there against say your number one offense or even with your number one defense because you're never quite sure what's going to happen. And um so yeah, it's going to take a long while. I mean those you guys can come off get off that topic you know they're they're light years away but >> I mean from that perspective you are invested in their development how do you balance all that >> it's not easy you know we are invested in their development but not at the detriment of our team >> spoken about trying to figure out the depth on the roster a couple guys how long is it going to take that Bill, how you feel about them? >> It's different at every position with every player. Um, you know, for instance, you know, Michael Carter right now, I mean, I feel good about him playing nickel, playing safety if need be. Um, maybe some of the other DBs that are in that bag, not so yet, but that doesn't mean they won't get there. Um, we don't have a lot of new young players on defense. So, um, most of the guys that are here have been with have some background with us. So, it should come we should be able to make those decisions a little quicker. >> One of the guys who don't doesn't get talked about a lot, but the offensive players all raved about him on the scout team last year, Chance Campbell. What What do you like about Chance? >> Yeah. Don't sleep on Chance now. you guys when you make your list out there. Um, we like Chance. Chance, uh, is a good football player. You know, had some injuries earlier in his career that, um, you know, set him back. Um, but since the day we picked him up last year, um, he's shown that he's a football player and we like him. Um, you know, interesting. Last year we picked him up the last week of the preseason game and I don't remember the exact date. It was just a few days before the game and he didn't need that acclamation period. You you said before that your preference at offball ball is to is to not uh sub in packages, you know, if need be, but has Troder done anything to kind of like put himself in the conversation of like certain looks you would play him um as opposed to Campbell? >> Uh possibly. I mean, but Trot's had a very good camp. you know, Trot to me, uh, along the same lines as we talked about with Makuba, looking better, moving better, playing better. And I just think it's not so much a conditioning and physical thing. It's more of knows what he's doing, seeing things quicker, faster, and playing faster. But he's he's had an excellent camp. He's the it's the best I've seen him look since we've had him. I know it's a relatively small sample size still, but do you have a sense of Shawn Manion as a play caller and setting things up? >> No, because you know there's there's no scoreboard out there, you know, and we're doing a lot of call it periods to where it's not scripted and, you know, to kind of get him acclimated that way. But, and it's good to do that. Um, but it's not a game and um, and I wouldn't be worried. I told him, you know, we obviously got the best of yesterday's practice by a long shot, but that's the way it's been the last two years in training camp. The defense has gotten the best of the offense. So, you know, not to, you know, be too concerned. As a follow to that, is there is there defens? >> Yeah, I mean, not that that doesn't mean that there's a lot of teams that are primarily in the gun. There's some that on first, second down or a lot more under center. So, this gives us a good look for those teams that we're going to be playing. Um, so it's a good mix. You know, we're still in the gun some out there. on the early downs and it does give us a good perspective and mix in practice that we probably haven't had the last couple years. >> Andy Dalton was talking about pure progression yesterday. Um, a lot of people point to you as why the league has gone to so much pure progression. What how does that differ as much as you can talk about it from the old >> What do you mean what kind of progress? >> Pure progressions. Do you just go one, two, pure? >> Oh, from the quarterback standpoint, >> I don't know. Um, >> you know, we're always hopeful of making the quarterback progress, not always have the first read, which is not always possible, but, you know, I'm not really sure what you're going at there. Well, a lot of people give you credit for why so many offenses run that way uh compared to the old school coverage. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> I'm not sure how or or if I want to answer that. >> These past few years, you played more than anything. >> I don't think that's true, but we're high. um based on the numbers. Is that is that based on matchups you get or is that you like? >> Well, first off, um the whole league as a whole is playing a lot more nickel and there's many reasons for that. The biggest being the fullback has disappeared in the NFL and he's been replaced by a third wide out or a second tight end who's a good receiver. So they're splitting out people more from the core of the formation than they ever used to. So that's one of the main reasons for playing more nickel. Um in 24 we played a lot of nickel one because I thought it put our best combination on the field whenever we could and to a certain degree last year also. Um, but I do kind of sense that the league is coming back a little bit. Um, not that there's an influx of a bunch of fullbacks right now, but they're maybe playing two tight ends. Um, so I think there's a chance you'll see more base, not just from us, but from other people, too. >> Definitely going to improve their offense. I'm I'm uh we'll see how it does defensively. Um it'll be interesting. But do you see some of these other guys? I mean, Castanos, Stum, Bader, uh Walker, man, Thompson did a hell of a job with managing those guys through to the playoffs last year. All right, thanks everyone.

title: OC Zac Robinson Speaks to the Media Before Training Camp Practice | Press Conference Live Steam
text: We've asked you just kind of each step with five practices under your belt. how you feel about being able to implement things and how how well they're taking what you're getting. >> Yeah, I think it's been good. You know, it's uh it's been a lot of great work against the defense. You know, you see a bunch of different looks. You're able to work through a number of different things just based on what those guys present each day. And, you know, the installs, it's a quick install to kind of get everything in. And so, um you know, we're at a point where, hey, got a lot of stuff in and you're trying to dial everything in in terms of, you know, formations, motions, alignment. you know, now we've got basically, you know, I would say 85% of the offense in and so we got to hone in on the details, fundamentals, all those things that, you know, all of our coaches are coaching in their position rooms. But, um, guys, and I know talking in the spring with guys and guys have been here in CG and Bake and some of these guys, it's like, hey, how much new to, you know, guys previous, you know, and so they've been saying it's 50/50. And so like there there is a lot of new uh but there's also you know some good carryover from previous years. So that's been good but getting a lot of great work in and we'll just continue to kind of hone in on what what we're going to look like once we kick this thing off. >> Coach, you you met Baker and coached him when he didn't have a job and he was there for a couple days and played with you at the Rams and you know anytime guys go through contract things. I know he addressed the team about it, certainly had his his say, but you were a player like just how how much do you think his ability to to kind of separate that and and what signs have you seen that Baker's Baker game man when the lights come on? >> You said it. Baker's been Baker. Um, you [snorts] know, the contract stuff's been out there, but haven't been able to tell. You know, he's he comes in, he's the exact same guy every single day. competitive, wants to know what's on the script, what we got, what the defense is doing. And uh you would not be able to tell at all that that's going on. He's been I know he said it, but he's he's been all balling. He means it. And that's exactly what he's been every day. >> Zack, as you implement things, to have TJ to have them easy to have guys that you work with, you know, how much does that help just to have more people that have been there and know what you want to to help? >> Yeah, it's been huge. you know, those guys obviously we worked through a lot of things the last couple years together, kind of getting into our own rhythm and flow and then um it's been a lot of fun to just kind of keep collaborating and then also learn some new stuff that um has been done here that you know we could possibly carry over into the season as well. So uh that's been great and then the the coaches that have been here um it's been really fun to work with carbs again. Obviously, we had some time in LA and being around BMAC and obviously I was around Skip in LA and um you know, first time being with Peele and Castle and Blaine. So, like it's been a really cool collaboration. I mean, you get in there in the offseason, you're like, "Okay, what do we want this thing to look like?" And it's a lot of work that goes into it. Everybody's got their hand in it. So, it's been a great collaboration between the whole group. Um but having kind of a mix of some of the guys that, you know, been around and also just some new thoughts that that we can always take and and try to learn from. So, uh, been been a blast working with these guys. Look forward to, you know, just keep continuing this thing and obviously getting into the season and what it's going to look like knowing that from, you know, this day to September 28th, it could look completely different. So, uh, it's been a great great collaboration between the whole group. >> Whenever we talked to the offensive line, they've stressed, you know, working on the wide zone concept this season. The Bucks have had successive gap in the past, but how do you think that transition is sort of going now? And what about this offensive line? Their skill set make you think that, oh, this is going to be a great >> this offensive line is incredibly versatile. Um there's really nothing these guys can't do. Watched it for, you know, past couple years on tape, just on crossover tape. Obviously, seen the gap stuff, seen the zone, seen the duo game, seen number different variations, perimeters. So, uh, you know, it is a a well-rounded group that, um, they're taking everything in stride and exactly what that's going to look like once we start kicking this thing off, you know, kind of to be determined. But we're working everything right now. We'll start honing in on what we want to be, you know, truly here in in a couple weeks once we kind of reset after um, you know, the Jets practices and you're looking at, you know, just a handful of weeks before you actually play a game where you want to, you know, kind of hone in on what you think you're going to be. So, uh, those guys can't say enough about just the investment they that they put in, how smart they are. Um, it's a it's a great group to work with. They're incredibly physical, you know, feeling what it feels like in pads with those guys, you know, especially in some of the pass protection stuff as well. Um, it's a firm, you know, group up front. So, uh, been great working with those guys. Look forward to just keep building, keep getting reps and, uh, ultimately kind of figuring out where we go with it. >> You didn't have a chance to work with Bucky much in a team type setting. Now that he's out there, What have you noticed about him and just uh you know the fit that he's going to have with Kenny and what you're trying to do? >> Yeah, Bucky is a stud. I mean, watching him in 24 explosive play waiting to happen. Obviously, you guys saw it up close every single game, but um he's just got such a great attitude, great spirit about him, team guy, always has a smile on his face. So, just the person has been just cool to get to know him. You know, still getting to know a lot of these guys. you only have so much time in the spring, but uh kind of, you know, feeling the personalities of guys now. Buckyy's been great and obviously the talent speaks for himself. Uh the way that he runs the football and just his feet are always in the ground. So, he's always able to change direction and obviously that keeps him so balanced to to break tackles and uh the versatility he has in the pass game, you know, run game. Uh you know, he's he's done a great job. It's been a blast seeing him just kind of cut some of these runs and you you start seeing it. So, uh, the compliment between really him and you mentioned Kenny, um, he's done a great job since the spring. Obviously got the bulk of the reps there and, uh, got a good feel for. And then shoot, Tux, Tux obviously made a lot of plays and Josh Williams has had a great camp as well. So, we have some backs that are that are exciting that have a versatile skill set and we'll just kind of keep taking it uh, where it goes. But those guys, it's a great group of guys, man. But Bucky, he he gives me a smile every time I look at him. He's he's a stud. >> Zack, how's your chemistry evolving with Todd? I mean, obviously that connection is going to be important, obviously in critical moments on game day. So, how is that starting to develop now? >> It's been great. Todd is awesome to work with. Um, obviously has so much experience. Um, seeing how he sets up practice and the situational work uh that we're getting has been has been cool. It's been a little bit different than places I've been, but we're getting a lot of great work and it's very intentional with the reps and why we're doing things and why we're working all these situations now for when those come up. But it's such an easy guy to obviously pop in and ask any questions about. Um, you know, there, like I said before, it's a lot of defense in training camp. Going against it in games is one thing and then you see it up close and realizing, uh, the issues that, you know, they can present to an offense. Uh, I've always got questions for, you know, for him and it's been cool. You know, his office is right next to mine. So, uh, it's been a good relationship and and, uh, look forward to just continue to build throughout training camp before the season starts. >> When you go into a new place, you have these of what you want to implement, but then you got to kind of get under the hood and really see what you're working with and sometimes those ideas maybe evolve a little bit. Is there anything that maybe you thought you knew about this offense or that you thought you wanted to do, but then as you kind of got to know the guys more or got a feel for things more, maybe you decided to pivot a little bit? >> It's a great question. Like we talked about the first day of camp, it's a great time to try things out and kind of, you know, figure out what we what we can do and and maybe something that, like you mentioned, we thought we were going to do, but we're not going to end up doing it. And so, uh, we're still in that process, though. And, and right now, we're, like I said, we got the bulk of the offense in um, and then really tailoring it down to, you know, get those reps that we need to get reps at. Uh, in order to get good at something, you have to have some sort of identity, obviously, to be a good offense. And uh that's what we're focused on right now. But uh there hasn't been anything since we got here like, "Oh, I don't think we can do that." Or there's been some ads, you know, that you get you go through the spring, get summer break to kind of take a look at the stuff from the spring and you're saying, "Okay, hey, maybe we can do this or this or maybe we need to add this formation to get this person in this spot." So football is always evolving and it really never stops. And so, um, like I mentioned before, from now to the middle of the season, things could evolve and take a life of its own and you just are in a discovery state. Uh, and that's where it's awesome to have really smart players as well. So, those guys can handle a lot of stuff and, uh, us as coaches just have to make sure we don't give them, you know, too much where we can hone in on things and make sure that we're fundamentally sound and, uh, the things that we're all all coaching. >> What does Dain's play style bring to the offense? >> Yeah, he's super versatile. Um he's great with the ball in his hands. He's very smart. Um he's great pass protector. Uh there's really nothing on the field that you can't put him in a situation and it seems like you coach him up one time on something and boom, he's got it. So, uh that's been a luxury to have. And so we'll we'll continue to just find out, you know, where we can put him in the best spots along with the rest of those guys with Bucky and uh the rest of those guys. But um but yeah, Kenny is he's really smart. Obviously, you see it on tape when you watch guys. You get a good feel for um you know, just how smart, how instinctual they are, how they see the game. Then you get to talking to him and you're like, "Okay, that matches up with, you know, how he plays." But um he's another one that's just got a you know, energetic, you know, kind of spirit about him and uh he's he's been a blast to work with and looking forward to just kind of continuing this thing going. >> You don't have a ton of offensive starting spots really up for grabs, uh but a lot of backup spots. Are there any backup jobs right now that you think are are particularly intriguing in terms of showing off the depth you have? >> Yeah, I think the the the wide out position, it's really deep. You know, I know we know the guys that we're going to be really counting on and then it's finding who those other guys are going to be and and I know Tez has had a great camp. You guys have seen that have been out of practice. He's making explosive plays every single day. you feel his juice out there and um he's done a great job, you know, from the spring to now with the offense and getting lined up in the right spots and um he's he's doing a great job. And obviously, you know, Ted's coming along. He's still still young, still learning, still, you know, figuring everything out, but he's he's been uh he's been sharp so far. And um you know, you got Cam and Sills and you know, some of these other guys that are all competing. They're doing a great job. All of them have made plays throughout camp. the ball's really been kind of going everywhere as you guys have been out there. A lot of guys are getting involved. So, um it's been great. And then the tight end room, you know, finding out with Bower and and um you know, and co and and those guys and Culp seeing how that's going to shake out. But, uh so early in camp still, but it's been cool to see just the versatility throughout you know, all those position groups and and uh you know, the different things they can do. >> Zack, this offense has been through a lot of change the past few seasons with different offensive coordinators and a lot of injury. How has that kind of resilience and just willingness to do whatever it takes and like able to pick up things quickly? How has that helped them to pick up your scheme pretty quickly? >> You said it, it's a resilient group. Um, from the moment I got here, guys coming up to my office, introducing themselves, like you could just feel the group like they want to be great and that's uh obviously they they've experienced that as well. So that the evidence is there for for them to you know play at a very high level and um but you feel it every single day from those guys whether it's the offensive line setting the tempo you know that Baker's going to bring it every single day and and you know guys like Jayla McMillan um obviously resilience from you know his injury last year and uh coming back and and and how he looks right now um you know all those guys. So it's it's a it's a really cool group. Uh but that word that you mentioned, resilience, um it's definitely helped with just kind of like, all right, hey, whatever we got to do is whatever we got to do. And you definitely feel that from those guys every day. >> What are some of the biggest things you've seen from quarterback Jaylen Daniels, you know, as a offensive coordinator and a former quarterback and maybe what are some of the biggest things that you're working on with him, you Chandler, the rest of the staff? >> Yeah, he's he's done a great job. He's really smart. He's uh you know, coming into a completely different scheme, obviously from a college scheme that he played in. Um he's taken it all in. He's getting a decent amount of reps, you know, throughout practice, but his arm is explosive. You guys have seen it out there. Uh there's not a throw he can't make or a throw he doesn't believe he can't make, which obviously that's finding the right balance um with a young cap. But uh he he's he's done a great job and and um you know, he just continues to learn to play the position and you know, hey, when when can I hang in the pocket and go through my reads? When can I bail and and try to make a play? Obviously, he's got some unique ability outside the pocket. But that's the biggest thing with all those young guys, you know, is just, hey, play within the scheme, play within the timing and the rhythm of the offense, get the ball where it needs to go, and then if it does break down, that's where you use your god-given ability and make a play. But, uh, Jaylen's doing a great job in his arm, like I mentioned, it's, uh, it's it's one of the better ones I've I've been around. >> What's Faker doing now that's better than when you saw him few years ago, and and where does he need to still improve? Yeah, I think he's he's gotten, you know, drop back pass is always for every quarterback. Those those passing downs, that's the toughest downs. And um his ability to continue to progress and move on from one to two to three if three's not there and you got to move, go do your thing. But, uh that's probably the biggest thing is just those those reps in the pocket on third downs in those tight situations. he makes so many plays outside the pocket, but then his ability to click through things and and find a find a completion on the backside, that's NFL football. Everybody's got to got to do it. And so that's probably the biggest growth also being, you know, in a system that he's comfortable with a lot of the, you know, the reads and so he's had, you know, built-in reps, uh, you know, throughout the last handful of years. But, um, arm, you know, looks even better than I remember it from LA. And, uh, he's throwing the ball accurately. Chandler's done a great job just tightening up his footwork and uh getting the fundamentals, you know, over and over. I mean, if you guys talk to Chandler, uh there's nobody that likes, you know, footwork more than him. And so, uh those guys have had a great relationship, good working relationship. So, uh there's there's a lot of things that he's definitely grown, but I would say the drop back pass is is probably it. >> Two more questions. >> You've seen Baker kind of respond to disappointment a few times, right? LA. He was just trying to get his career back on track and he was a little worn down, beaten down by that. And then of course here he doesn't get the new contract that he wants. Just how have you seen him respond to that? >> Like I remember watching him at University of Oklahoma or at Texas Tech for that matter, he he believes in himself and whether other people believe in him too, he really doesn't care as you guys know. And so uh he he's the same guy every single day. one of the most competitive just people I've been around and uh being back out at practice in these settings and seeing that and really the ownership he takes as if something doesn't go right, you know, he's he's got a great ownership about them of of you know, hey, my bad, you know, that's that's all you always love that from your starter, you know, you always love that from your leader. If those guys have accountability and ownership, it bleeds to the rest of the group. And so, um but yeah, it's been so fun to just see again, you know, just being out there and feeling the juice that he brings. He's of course talking to the defense and um you know just he's the guy that's getting the whole thing going and and we wouldn't want to have anybody else. >> What does it then for for somebody that because he's talked before he's been open about the fact that yeah sometimes he does have negative selft talk turning those disappointments into something that can actually catapult you forward. >> Yeah, I think you know you probably have to talk to him a little bit more about it but he's um you know he's just he's been through a lot. you know, obviously he was your number one pick and then um kind of gets kicked to the curb in Cleveland. Not sure [snorts] if it was warranted or not, but is what it is. And then he, like you said, mention was able to reset himself in LA and uh just take off from there. But uh his his mentality is that, you know, kind of underdog mentality he's had since I'm sure he was eight years old starting to play football. That'll never leave that guy and and um it's a good thing. and just channeling it the right way, you know, just channeling everything the right way and and using that um that chip that he has um in a in a positive way. >> Thank you guys.
